Forbidden.description: The app_key is valid, but its permission scope or the creator's role does not allow this operation or object.

error.message: The resource you request is not found

ServerError.description: Unexpected server-side error. Include the request_id when reporting.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The service is temporarily unavailable. Include the request_id when reporting.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit hit. Wait for the number of seconds in `Flashcat-Request-Rate-Limit-Delay`, then retry.

Flashcat-Request-Rate-Limit-Delay.description: Seconds until the current rate-limit window resets. Absent when the request was rejected by the gateway's global protection limit.

A2AAgentCreateRequest.description: Registration parameters for a new A2A agent.

agent_name.description: Agent display name, used to address the agent in sessions. Must not contain `@`, must not be `general` or `explore`, and must be unique within its scope (account-wide or one team).

instructions.description: Natural-language instructions for the remote agent: a Markdown document with optional `summary` frontmatter and a non-empty body, at most 50 KiB (51200 bytes). Required — a deprecated `description` field is still accepted for legacy clients and, if both are sent, must exactly match `instructions`.

card_url.description: URL of the remote agent card. Must be an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a non-empty host; a URL with no path is resolved to `/.well-known/agent-card.json`. If an execution environment is online, the card is fetched and must declare an A2A 1.x `JSONRPC` or `HTTP+JSON` interface.

auth_type.description:
Authentication used to reach the remote agent with a shared credential:
- `none`: no credential header.
- `api_key`: sends `auth_config.api_key` in the header named by `auth_config.header`.
- `bearer`: sends `Authorization: Bearer <auth_config.token>`.

When omitted the value is stored as an empty string, which behaves like `none`.

auth_config.description: Shared credential key-values: `header` and `api_key` for `auth_type=api_key`, `token` for `auth_type=bearer`. Values of `api_key`, `token`, and `client_secret` are encrypted at rest and masked in responses.

streaming.description: Whether the remote agent supports streaming.

team_id.description: Team scope: 0 = account-wide; >0 = team. Creating at account scope requires the owner/admin role; creating into a team requires actual membership in that team.

environments.description: Execution environments this agent is callable from: `cloud` and/or BYOC runner environment IDs. Omitted or empty means all environments.

auth_mode.description:
Who supplies the credential:
- `shared` (default; an empty value behaves the same): one credential stored on the agent (`auth_type` + `auth_config`) is used for every caller.
- `per_user_secret`: each user stores their own secret, sent in the header named by `secret_schema.header_name`.
- `per_user_oauth`: each user completes their own OAuth authorization; discovery and client registration run on first use.

`per_user_secret` requires `secret_schema` with a non-empty `header_name`; any other value returns `InvalidParameter`.

secret_schema.description: JSON-encoded secret schema, e.g. `{"header_name":"X-Api-Key"}`; required when `auth_mode=per_user_secret`.

oauth_metadata.description: JSON-encoded OAuth metadata; populated by the OAuth discovery flow for `per_user_oauth` mode.

allow_insecure_oauth_http.description: Allow non-loopback HTTP OAuth discovery/metadata endpoints for this agent instead of requiring HTTPS. Defaults to false.

allow_insecure_tls_skip_verify.description: Skip TLS certificate verification when connecting to this agent's endpoint (self-signed/private certs). Defaults to false.

Target agent ID, from the list returned by `POST /safari/a2a-agent/list`.

account_id.description: Owning account ID.

team_id.description: Team scope: 0 = account-wide; >0 = the owning team.

can_edit.description: Whether the caller may update, enable, disable, or delete this agent: `true` for an account-scoped agent only for the account owner or an admin, for a team agent only for members of that team.

environments.description: Execution environments this agent is callable from (`cloud` and/or BYOC runner environment IDs). Always present; `[]` means all environments (also the value on legacy rows created before this field).

instructions.description: Natural-language instructions for the remote agent (formerly named `description`).

card_url.description: URL of the remote agent card.

auth_type.description:
Authentication used to reach the remote agent with a shared credential:
- `none`: no credential header.
- `api_key`: sends `auth_config.api_key` in the header named by `auth_config.header`.
- `bearer`: sends `Authorization: Bearer <auth_config.token>`.

An empty string means `auth_type` was omitted at creation and behaves like `none`.

auth_config.description: Shared credential key-values (`header`, `api_key`, `token`, …). Values of `api_key`, `token`, `client_secret`, and any other value stored encrypted are masked: longer than 8 characters shows the first and last 4 characters around `****`, otherwise `****`. Omitted when empty.

streaming.description: Whether the remote agent supports streaming responses.

status.description:
Whether the agent is offered to AI SRE sessions:
- `enabled`: available for dispatch (the state after create).
- `disabled`: kept but not offered; re-enable with `POST /safari/a2a-agent/enable`.

agent_card_name.description: Agent name read from the remote card on older records. The server no longer fills this in, so it is omitted for new agents.

agent_card_skills.description: Skill names read from the remote card on older records. The server no longer fills this in, so it is omitted for new agents.

card_resolve_timeout.description: Card-resolution timeout in seconds. Always 0 today — the API does not yet expose a way to set it.

task_timeout.description: Single-task execution timeout in seconds. Always 0 today — the API does not yet expose a way to set it.

auth_mode.description:
Who supplies the credential; omitted when empty, which behaves like `shared`:
- `shared`: one credential stored on the agent (`auth_type` + `auth_config`) is used for every caller.
- `per_user_secret`: each user stores their own secret, sent in the header named by `secret_schema.header_name`.
- `per_user_oauth`: each user completes their own OAuth authorization; discovery and client registration run on first use.

allow_insecure_oauth_http.description: Allow non-loopback HTTP OAuth discovery/metadata endpoints for this agent instead of requiring HTTPS.

allow_insecure_tls_skip_verify.description: Skip TLS certificate verification when connecting to this agent's endpoint.

created_by.description: Member ID that created the agent.

created_at.description: Creation time. Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

updated_at.description: Last update time. Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

A2AAgentListRequest.description: Pagination, scope, and search filter for listing A2A agents.

offset.description: Pagination offset — number of rows to skip, starting from 0.

limit.description: Page size; 0 or less falls back to 20. No upper bound is enforced.

scope.description: Visibility scope: `all` (account-scope plus the caller's visible teams), `account` (account-scope only), or `team` (team-scoped rows across the caller's visible teams).

query.description: Case-insensitive substring search across agent name, instructions, card URL, agent ID, and the resolved card name.

team_ids.description: Restrict to these team IDs. IDs of teams the caller does not belong to are ignored; empty means all of the caller's teams.

include_account.description: Include account-scoped (`team_id=0`) rows. Defaults to `true`; ignored when `scope` is `account` (always included) or `team` (never included).

items.description: A2A agents on this page.

total.description: Total number of matching agents.

A2AAgentUpdateRequest.description: Partial update of an A2A agent. A null/omitted field is left unchanged.

agent_id.description: Target agent ID, from the list returned by `POST /safari/a2a-agent/list`.

agent_name.description: New display name; omit to leave unchanged. Same rules as create: no `@`, not `general` / `explore`, unique within the scope.

instructions.description: New instructions document (same contract as create: optional `summary` frontmatter, non-empty body, at most 50 KiB). Omit to leave unchanged. A deprecated `description` field is also accepted; if both are sent they must match.

card_url.description: New card URL; omit to leave unchanged. Validated and compatibility-checked the same way as on create; a real change also clears `oauth_metadata` unless a new one is sent.

auth_type.description:
New auth type; omit to leave unchanged.
- `none`: no credential header.
- `api_key`: sends `auth_config.api_key` in the header named by `auth_config.header`.
- `bearer`: sends `Authorization: Bearer <auth_config.token>`.

auth_config.description: Replace the whole auth config; omit to leave unchanged. Keys missing from the map are dropped. For a sensitive key, sending back the masked value keeps the stored secret, while sending an empty string clears it.

streaming.description: Toggle streaming support. Omit to leave unchanged.

team_id.description: Reassign team scope; omit to leave unchanged. Moving to a team requires membership in it; moving to account scope (`0`) requires the account owner or an admin. If the team changes without `environments` in the same request, the current runner entries must stay selectable by the caller or the update is rejected.

environments.description: Execution environments this agent is callable from: `cloud` and/or BYOC runner environment IDs. Omit (null) to leave unchanged; send a list to set it — an empty list clears the restriction back to all environments.

auth_mode.description:
New auth mode; omit to leave unchanged. Values (who supplies the credential):
- `shared` (default; an empty value behaves the same): one credential stored on the agent (`auth_type` + `auth_config`) is used for every caller.
- `per_user_secret`: each user stores their own secret, sent in the header named by `secret_schema.header_name`.
- `per_user_oauth`: each user completes their own OAuth authorization; discovery and client registration run on first use.

When sent, `secret_schema` is overwritten with the value in the same request.

secret_schema.description: New JSON secret schema, e.g. `{"header_name":"X-Api-Key"}`. Applied only together with `auth_mode`; sent alone it is ignored.

oauth_metadata.description: New JSON OAuth metadata. A non-empty value is stored as sent. When omitted or empty, the stored value is kept unless `auth_mode` or `card_url` changes, in which case it is cleared.

allow_insecure_oauth_http.description: Toggle non-loopback HTTP OAuth discovery for this agent. Omit to leave unchanged.

allow_insecure_tls_skip_verify.description: Toggle TLS certificate verification skipping for this agent. Omit to leave unchanged.

account_id.description: Account identifier.

account_name.description: Account (organization) name shown in the console.

phone.description: Account contact phone, masked for privacy.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code of the contact phone (e.g. "CN", "US", "HK").

locale.description: Account language preference (`zh-CN` or `en-US`); empty string when not set.

time_zone.description: Account default time zone (IANA name, e.g. `Asia/Shanghai`); members without their own setting follow it. Empty string when not set.

created_at.description: Account creation time, Unix timestamp in seconds.

restrictions.description: Account access restrictions. Omitted when none are configured.

ips.description: Source IP addresses or CIDR ranges allowed to call the console and API for this account; `null` or empty when unrestricted.

email_domains.description: Email domains allowed for new members; invitations to other domains are rejected. `null` or empty when unrestricted.

allow_subdomain.description: Whether subdomains of the allowed email domains are also accepted.

mp_plat.description: Cloud marketplace the account was provisioned from: `aws` — AWS Marketplace. Omitted when the account did not come from a marketplace.

mp_account_id.description: Account identifier on the marketplace platform. Omitted together with `mp_plat`.

AckIncidentRequest.description: Parameters for acknowledging one or more incidents.

custom_fields.description: Custom field values for the acknowledgement form. Allowed keys and values depend on the incident's visible form.

images.description: Images attached to the acknowledgement timeline entry.

incident_ids.description: Incident IDs to acknowledge. At most 100 per call.

summary.description: Form summary recorded as a timeline comment. Accepted only when the acknowledgement form contains a summary element.

AddIncidentResponderRequest.description: Parameters for adding responders to an existing incident.

person_ids.description: Member IDs to add as responders. IDs that are already responders, or that do not exist in the account, are skipped.

notify.description: Notification settings for the newly added responders. Defaults to `{"follow_preference": true}`.

follow_preference.description: `true`: notify each person through their personal notification preference. `false`: use `personal_channels`, which must then be non-empty. When omitted, `personal_channels` must be set.

personal_channels.description: Channels used when `follow_preference` is `false`: `sms`, `voice`, `email`, `push` (mobile app push), or an IM app channel written as `feishu_app:<integration_id>`, `dingtalk_app:<integration_id>`, `wecom_app:<integration_id>`, `slack_app:<integration_id>`, or `teams_app:<integration_id>`. Ignored when `follow_preference` is `true`.

template_id.description: Notification template ID, as returned by the notification template endpoints. Must exist in the account; otherwise the call fails with `InvalidParameter`.

integration_id.description: ID of the IM integration hosting the war room; obtain it from `POST /datasource/im/war-room-enabled/list`.

chat_id.description: Chat ID of the war-room group on the IM platform, as returned for the war room by `POST /incident/war-room/list`.

member_ids.description: Person IDs (member IDs, or the account ID for the owner) to add. Must not be empty.

AffectedStatusPageComponentItem.description: A status page component currently affected by an event, embedding component metadata plus its resulting status.

available_since_seconds.description: Time the component became available, as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Omitted when 0.

hide_all.description: When true, the component is hidden entirely from summary endpoints. Omitted when false.

hide_uptime.description: When true, uptime data is hidden from summary responses. Omitted when false.

name.description: Component display name.

order_id.description: Display order within its section. Omitted when 0.

section_id.description: Parent section ID. Omitted when the component sits at the top level.

status.description:
Current status of the component affected by the change. Severity increases: `operational` < `degraded` = `under_maintenance` < `partial_outage` < `full_outage`; incident-type changes may use the first four, maintenance-type changes only `operational` and `under_maintenance`.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `operational` | Operating normally. |
| `degraded` | Degraded performance. |
| `partial_outage` | Partial outage. |
| `full_outage` | Full outage. |
| `under_maintenance` | Under maintenance. |

AlertEventGlobalListRequest.description: Filter and pagination criteria for the global raw event list. Time range is required.

start_time.description: Start of the search window, Unix epoch seconds. Must be greater than 0.

end_time.description: End of the search window, Unix epoch seconds. Must be greater than `start_time`; the span must not exceed 31 days.

p.description: Page number, starting at 1. Used when `search_after_ctx` is not provided.

limit.description: Page size, max 100, default 20.

search_after_ctx.description: Pagination cursor: leave empty for the first page, then pass the `search_after_ctx` returned by the previous response.

channel_ids.description: Filter by channel IDs. At most 100 entries. Channels the caller cannot access are dropped; if none remain, the result is empty.

severities.description: Comma-separated filter on `event_severity`, e.g. `Critical,Warning`. Meaningful values: `Critical`, `Warning`, `Info`. Values are not validated; an unknown value (or `Ok`) matches nothing.

orderby.description: Sort field; only `event_time` is supported.

asc.description: Sort ascending when `true`.

has_next_page.description: Whether a next page exists (probed by fetching limit+1 rows).

items.description: Raw alert events on the current page.

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor for the next page — the ObjectID of the last event on this page; pass it back as `search_after_ctx`. Omitted when the page is empty; in cursor mode also omitted when there is no next page.

total.description: Total number of matching events, capped at 1000.

account_id.description: ID of the account that owns this record; the same for every record returned to one `app_key`.

channel_id.description: Channel ID the event is routed to.

integration_id.description: Integration that produced this event.

integration_type.description: Plugin type of the integration, such as `prometheus.alert`, `grafana.alert`, `zabbix.alert`, `monit.alert`, or `email.alert`. The set is open and grows with new integrations; `POST /integration/type/list` returns the full list.

alert_key.description: Deduplication key used to merge events into an alert.

event_severity.description: Severity of this event: `Critical`, `Warning`, or `Info`. An event never carries `Ok` as severity — `Ok` appears only as `event_status`.

event_status.description: Status carried by this event: `Critical`/`Warning`/`Info` for a firing event, `Ok` for a recovery event.

labels.description: Label key-value pairs.

updated_at.description: Record update time, Unix epoch seconds.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete time, Unix epoch seconds. Omitted when the event is not deleted.

limit.description: Page size. Defaults to 20 and cannot exceed 100.

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor returned by the previous page. When supplied, cursor pagination is used instead of page-number pagination.

has_next_page.description: Whether another page is available.

items.description: Raw alert events in the requested order.

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor to pass as `search_after_ctx` for the next page. Omitted when the page is empty; in cursor mode also omitted when there is no next page.

total.description: Total matching event count, capped at 1000.

alert_id.description: Alert ID (ObjectID hex string); obtain it from `POST /alert/list`.

asc.description: Sort ascending.

limit.description: Page size, max 100, default 20.

types.description: Filter by feed type codes — see the `type` field of the response items for the full list (e.g. `a_new`, `a_comm`, `a_merge`).

has_next_page.description: Whether a next page exists.

items.description: Alert feed records on the current page.

AlertFeedType.description:
Alert activity feed entry type. Each value identifies one alert lifecycle event; the matching `detail` payload shape is determined by this field.

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `a_new` | Alert triggered by an incoming event. |
| `a_update` | Alert severity or status changed on an incoming event. |
| `a_comm` | Comment added on the alert. |
| `a_merge` | Alert merged into an incident. |
| `a_m_silence` | Alert muted by a silence rule. |
| `a_m_inhibit` | Alert muted by an inhibit rule. |
| `a_m_flapping` | Alert muted by flapping detection (historical data only; no longer produced). |
| `a_ack` | Alert acknowledged (historical data only; alert-level acknowledgement has been removed). |
| `a_unack` | Alert acknowledgement revoked (historical data only). |
| `a_close` | Alert closed (historical data only; no longer produced). |

AlertImage.description: An image attachment on an alert or event.

last_time.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of the most recent event.

end_time.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the alert recovered. 0 if still active.

labels.description: Alert labels.

ever_muted.description: Whether this alert has ever been silenced.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp (seconds). Zero if not deleted.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp (seconds).

integration_type.description: Plugin type of the integration, such as `prometheus.alert`, `grafana.alert`, `zabbix.alert`, `monit.alert`, or `email.alert`. The set is open and grows with new integrations; `POST /integration/type/list` returns the full list.

channel_status.description: Status of the channel: `enabled`, `disabled`, or `deleted`. Empty string when the record has no channel or the channel no longer exists.

responder_email.description: Always an empty string in API responses; filled only when the alert is rendered for notifications.

detail_url.description: Console URL of this alert (`{console}/alert/detail/{alert_id}`). Empty when the deployment has no console base configured.

AlertItem.description: A single alert with full detail.

integration_id.description: ID of the integration that produced this alert.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel the alert belongs to.

account_id.description: ID of the account that owns the alert.

title_rule.description: Title template used to derive `title` from the event labels (e.g. `$service::$cluster`).

alert_severity.description: Current severity — the highest severity ever seen on this alert: `Critical`, `Warning`, or `Info`.

alert_status.description: Current status: `Critical`/`Warning`/`Info` while firing, `Ok` once recovered.

end_time.description: Resolution time, Unix epoch seconds. 0 if still active.

ever_muted.description: True if this alert has ever been silenced.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp, Unix epoch seconds.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp, Unix epoch seconds.

integration_type.description: Type key of the integration that produced the alert, e.g. `prometheus.alert` or `zabbix.alert`; same values as `plugin_type` from `POST /integration/type/list`.

integration_ref_id.description: Owner reference of the integration: `a_<account_id>` for an account-level integration, `c_<channel_id>` for a channel-owned one.

responder_name.description: Responder display name. Always empty in this response — responder tracking lives on the associated incident.

responder_email.description: Responder email. Always empty in this response — responder tracking lives on the associated incident.

events.description: Raw events of this alert. Omitted here; populated only by `POST /incident/alert/list`.

images.description: Images attached to the alert; `null` when there are none.

detail_url.description: Console URL of this alert (`{console}/alert/detail/{alert_id}`). Empty when the deployment has no console base configured.

data_source_type.description: Deprecated: use `integration_type` instead (same value, e.g. `prometheus.alert`). Omitted when empty.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete time, Unix epoch seconds. Omitted when the alert is not deleted.

alert_ids.description: Alert IDs (ObjectID hex strings) to fetch. A malformed ID fails the request; IDs not found in the account are left out of the result.

AlertListRequest.description: Filter and pagination criteria for alert list queries. Time range is required.

start_time.description: Start of the search window, Unix epoch seconds, applied to the alert's `start_time`. A value earlier than the account's data retention period is moved up to the retention start.

end_time.description: End of the search window, Unix epoch seconds. Must be greater than `start_time`; the span must not exceed 31 days (7 days with `by_updated_at`). A value before the start of the data retention period returns `InvalidParameter`.

p.description: Page number, starting at 1. Used when `search_after_ctx` is not provided; `p * limit` must stay within 10,000 records.

limit.description: Page size. Max 100, default 20.

search_after_ctx.description: Opaque cursor from the previous response for the next page.

is_active.description: Filter by lifecycle: `true` returns only firing alerts (status `Critical`/`Warning`/`Info`), `false` returns only recovered alerts (status `Ok`). Omit or pass `null` to return both.

ever_muted.description: Filter by whether the alert has ever been silenced.

alert_severity.description: Comma-separated filter on `alert_severity`, e.g. `Critical,Warning`. Allowed values: `Critical`, `Warning`, `Info`, `Ok`; other values return `InvalidParameter`. `Ok` matches nothing because `alert_severity` is never `Ok`.

alert_ids.description: Filter to specific alert IDs (ObjectID hex strings). Invalid IDs are ignored; if none are valid, the result is empty.

asc.description: Sort ascending by `start_time` when `true`; default is descending.

by_updated_at.description: When `true`, also require the alert's `updated_at` to fall within [`start_time`, `end_time`], in addition to the `start_time` filter; the span must then not exceed 7 days.

total.description: Number of matching alerts, capped at 1,000.

has_next_page.description: `true` when another page exists. Exact in both cursor mode (`search_after_ctx` sent) and page-number mode, including past the 1,000 cap of `total`.

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor for the next page — the ObjectID hex of the last alert on this page; pass it back as `search_after_ctx`. Omitted when the page is empty; in cursor mode also omitted when there is no next page.

items.description: Alerts on the current page.

alert_ids.description: Alert IDs to merge (ObjectID hex strings); obtain them from `POST /alert/list`. Every ID must belong to the caller's account.

incident_id.description: Target incident ID (ObjectID hex string); obtain it from `POST /incident/list`.

comment.description: Optional comment recorded on the merge feed entry. At most 1024 characters.

title.description: Optional new title for the target incident. At most 512 characters.

owner_id.description: Member ID of the new owner for the target incident; obtain it from `POST /member/list`.

kind.description:
Rule type. Rules run in array order; when the `if` condition matches, the event is processed according to `kind`.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `title_reset` | Rewrites the event title from the `settings.title` template. |
| `description_reset` | Rewrites the event description from the `settings.description` template. |
| `severity_reset` | Resets the event severity and status to `settings.severity` (`Critical`/`Warning`/`Info`). |
| `alert_drop` | Discards the matching event outright; no alert is created. |
| `alert_inhibit` | Discards the event (inhibition) when an active source alert matching `settings.source_filters` and correlated via `settings.equals` exists. |

if.description: AND-filter list — the rule applies only when every condition matches the incoming event. Keys: `severity` (aliases `alert_severity`, `event_severity`), `status`, `title`, `title_rule`, `description`, `alert_key`, `integration_id` (alias `data_source_id`), and `labels.<name>`; other keys return `InvalidParameter`. `null` or omitted means the rule applies to all events.

settings.description:
Kind-specific settings. Shape depends on `kind`:
- `title_reset`: `{ "title": "<string>" }`
- `description_reset`: `{ "description": "<string>" }`
- `severity_reset`: `{ "severity": "Critical"|"Warning"|"Info" }`
- `alert_drop`: `{}` (empty object)
- `alert_inhibit`: `{ "equals": ["<label_key>", ...], "source_filters": <OrFilterGroup> }`

integration_id.description: Integration ID. Must be greater than 0.

AlertPipelineItem.description: Alert processing pipeline for an integration.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp, Unix epoch seconds.

creator_id.description: Member ID who created the pipeline.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete time, Unix epoch seconds. Omitted when not deleted.

integration_id.description: Integration ID this pipeline applies to.

status.description: Pipeline status. Always `enabled` in these responses — deleted pipelines are filtered out.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp, Unix epoch seconds.

updated_by.description: Member ID who last updated the pipeline.

integration_ids.description: Integration IDs. At least one entry is required.

items.description: Alert pipeline configuration of each requested integration, one item per configured integration.

integration_id.description: ID of the integration to configure; account-level and channel-owned integrations are both accepted.

rules.description: Rules to apply, evaluated in array order. At most 50 entries; an empty array removes all rules.

account_id.description: Account ID. Filled by the server from the authenticated identity; do not provide.

annotations.description: Annotation key-value pairs delivered with alert events; keys must not start with `$` (reserved for query fields).

channel_ids.description: Channel IDs to send alerts to.

created_at.description: Creation time as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Generated by the server; do not provide.

creator_id.description: Creator user ID. Filled by the server from the current user; do not provide.

creator_name.description: Creator name. Filled by the server; do not provide.

cron_pattern.description: Schedule expression: a 6-field cron (with seconds) or an `@every 30s` interval descriptor. Must not start with `CRON_TZ=` or `TZ=`; use the `timezone` field instead.

debug_log_enabled.description: Whether to enable debug logging; the edge emits detailed evaluation logs, useful for troubleshooting rules that do not trigger as expected.

delay_seconds.description: Seconds to shift the evaluation query window backward, compensating for data ingestion latency.

description_type.description: Format for the description. Defaults to `text` when omitted or empty. `text` = plain text; `markdown` = Markdown, rendered as Markdown in alert details.

ds_ids.description: Datasource IDs, merged with `ds_list` to decide which datasources the rule monitors; IDs survive datasource renames. At least one of `ds_list` and `ds_ids` must be provided.

ds_list.description: Data source name patterns (supports wildcards). At least one of `ds_list` / `ds_ids` must be non-empty; the two are merged to decide which datasources the rule monitors.

enabled.description: Whether the rule is enabled. Updating to `false` makes the server clean up the rule's active alerts.

enabled_times.description: Time windows when the rule is active. Defaults to all days from 00:00 to 23:59 when omitted or empty.

folder_id.description: ID of the folder the rule belongs to. Obtainable via `POST /monit/folder/list`.

id.description: Rule ID. Required for update; omit for create (assigned by the server).

labels.description: Custom labels.

name.description: Rule name. Must be unique within the same folder.

rule_configs.description: Check configuration: query list plus trigger/recovery conditions. Structure see `RuleConfigs`.

timezone.description: Timezone in which the rule executes. Determines how the cron schedule and effective time windows are interpreted. Only IANA timezone names are accepted (e.g. `Asia/Shanghai`, `UTC`, `Europe/London`); shortcuts and offsets such as `Local`, `UTC+8`, or `CST` are rejected. Treated as `Asia/Shanghai` if empty.

updated_at.description: Last update time as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Generated by the server; do not provide.

updater_id.description: Last updater user ID. Filled by the server; do not provide.

updater_name.description: Last updater name. Filled by the server; do not provide.

AlertRuleAudit.description: An audit record capturing a rule snapshot at a point in time.

id.description: Audit record ID.

account_id.description: ID of the account that owns the rule.

alert_rule_id.description: ID of the alert rule this record belongs to.

action.description: Action performed: `create` = rule created; `update` = rule updated (covers full updates, field-batch updates, imports and moves).

content.description: JSON string of the full rule right after the change. Populated on `/monit/rule/audit/detail`, omitted on list responses. Records written by `/monit/rule/v2/create` and `/monit/rule/v2/update` use the `AlertRuleV2` shape; records written by `/monit/rule/update/fields` and `/monit/rule/move` use the stored rule shape, whose checker configs carry legacy recovery settings instead of `recovery_mode` / `end_mode`.

creator_id.description: ID of the user who made this change (taken from the rule's `updater_id` at change time).

creator_name.description: Name of the user who made this change (taken from the rule's `updater_name` at change time).

created_at.description: When this audit record was produced, as a Unix timestamp in seconds; equals the rule's `updated_at` at change time.

AlertRuleBasic.description: Basic alert rule information for list views. In `include_descendants: true` listings only `id`, `folder_id` and `name` are filled; the other fields carry zero values.

id.description: Unique rule ID.

account_id.description: ID of the account that owns the rule; `0` in `include_descendants: true` listings.

folder_id.description: ID of the folder that directly contains the rule; in `include_descendants: true` listings it can be a descendant of the requested folder.

name.description: Rule name, unique within its folder (at most 128 characters).

labels.description: Custom labels the rule adds to its alert events; `null` in `include_descendants: true` listings.

ds_type.description: Datasource type the rule queries. Types that support alerting: `prometheus`, `elasticsearch`, `loki`, `clickhouse`, `mysql`, `oracle`, `postgres`, `sls`, `tencent_cls`, `victorialogs`. Only enabled rules are checked against this list, so a disabled rule may carry another value; empty in `include_descendants: true` listings.

enabled.description: Whether the rule is enabled.

debug_log_enabled.description: Whether debug logging is on; when `true` the edge writes detailed evaluation logs for this rule.

cron_pattern.description: Schedule expression: a 6-field cron with seconds, e.g. `0 * * * * *`, or an `@every 30s` interval descriptor. Must not start with `CRON_TZ=` or `TZ=`; use the `timezone` field instead.

timezone.description: Timezone in which the rule executes. Determines how the cron schedule and effective time windows are interpreted. Only IANA timezone names are accepted (e.g. `Asia/Shanghai`, `UTC`, `Europe/London`); shortcuts and offsets such as `Local`, `UTC+8`, or `CST` are rejected. Treated as `Asia/Shanghai` if empty.

delay_seconds.description: Seconds the evaluation query window is shifted back to allow for data ingestion latency.

creator_id.description: ID of the user who created the rule.

creator_name.description: Name of the user who created the rule.

updater_id.description: ID of the user who last modified the rule.

updater_name.description: Name of the user who last modified the rule.

created_at.description: Creation time, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

updated_at.description: Last modification time, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

triggered.description: True if the rule currently has active alerts.

active_alert_count.description: Number of currently active (unrecovered) alerts fired by this rule. `triggered` equals `active_alert_count > 0`.

runtime_state.description:
Runtime evaluation state, derived from edge heartbeats and the edge-reported rule status. Omitted when the state is unavailable.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `disabled` | The rule is disabled. |
| `offline` | The edge instance or cluster owning this rule is offline. |
| `abnormal` | The edge reports evaluation errors. |
| `stale` | The edge's runtime status report is outdated. |
| `no_datasource` | No datasource currently matches the rule's `ds_list` / `ds_ids`. |
| `config_pending` | The latest rule config has not been delivered to the edge yet. |
| `waiting` | Enabled, but the edge has not reported runtime status yet. |
| `normal` | Evaluating normally. |

AlertRuleCounter.description: One historical snapshot of the account's alert rule total.

account_id.description: ID of the account this snapshot belongs to.

id.description: ID of this snapshot record.

num.description: Rule count at the sample time.

AlertRuleExport.description: Portable alert rule representation for import/export. Omits identifying fields like `id`, `account_id`, and audit metadata.

annotations.description: Custom annotation key-value pairs attached to alert events; keys must not start with `$` (reserved for query field references).

cron_pattern.description: Evaluation schedule as a 6-field cron expression (seconds included) or `@every <duration>` (an integral number of seconds, at least 1s); `CRON_TZ=`/`TZ=` prefixes are rejected — set the timezone in `timezone` instead.

debug_log_enabled.description: Whether to emit debug logs for this rule's evaluations; enable when troubleshooting.

delay_seconds.description: Query time offset in seconds: each evaluation reads data as of `schedule time − delay_seconds` to tolerate ingestion lag; `0` means no offset.

description.description: Rule description in the format given by `description_type`, shown with alert events.

description_type.description: Format of `description`, `text` or `markdown`; treated as `text` when omitted.

ds_ids.description: Datasource ID list, merged with `ds_list`; references by ID and is therefore immune to datasource renames.

ds_list.description: Datasource name list with wildcard support; merged with `ds_ids` to decide which datasources the rule monitors — must be maintained by hand if a datasource is renamed.

ds_type.description: Datasource type ident, e.g. `prometheus`; must be a datasource type (`ident`) that exists in the import target environment.

enabled.description: Whether the rule is enabled; rules imported as disabled are not evaluated.

enabled_times.description: Effective time windows; each entry has `days` (0–6, 0 = Sunday) and `stime`/`etime` (`HH:MM`), interpreted in the rule's `timezone`; an empty list disables the rule.

labels.description: Custom label key-value pairs attached to alert events produced by this rule.

name.description: Rule name, up to 128 characters when imported.

repeat_interval.description: Interval in seconds between repeated notifications for a firing alert; values below 1 fall back to the default of 3600.

repeat_total.description: Maximum number of repeated notifications for the same alert; values below 1 fall back to the default of 3.

timezone.description: Timezone in which the rule executes. IANA timezone name; defaults to `Asia/Shanghai`.

AlertRuleExportListResponse.description: List of exported rule configurations, compatible with `POST /monit/rule/import`.

title.description: Alert title, resolved at read time. Omitted when empty.

ApAlertDrop.description: Settings for `alert_drop`: no fields; send `{}`. A matching event is discarded and no alert is created or updated.

ApAlertInhibit.description: Settings for `alert_inhibit`: the current event is discarded when an active alert of the same integration, with a different `alert_key` and started within the 10 minutes before the event, matches `source_filters` and has the same value as the event for every `equals` key.

equals.description: Keys whose values must be equal on the source alert and the current event: `title`, `severity`, or `labels.<name>`. An empty list, any other key, or a label missing on the event means the rule never inhibits.

source_filters.description: AND-conditions a source alert must meet. Allowed keys: `severity`, `title`, and `labels.<name>`; other keys return `InvalidParameter`.

ApDescriptionReset.description: Settings for `description_reset`: replaces the event description with a rendered template.

description.description: Description template. Only a value starting with `[TPL]` takes effect: the rest is rendered as a Go template against the event and replaces the description. A value without the prefix leaves the description unchanged.

ApSeverityReset.description: Settings for `severity_reset`: sets the event severity, and its status, to a fixed value.

severity.description: Severity to set: `Critical`, `Warning` or `Info`. The event status is set to the same value.

ApTitleReset.description: Settings for `title_reset`: replaces the event title using a title rule.

title.description: Title rule. A value starting with `[TPL]` is a Go template rendered against the event, e.g. `[TPL]{{.Labels.service}}`. Otherwise it is a `::`-separated list in which each `$name` part is replaced by the value of label `name` and other parts are kept as written.

ArtifactFileStateItem.description: Live gallery state of one presented file. Matched by the file's source session and workspace path, so an older version of a republished file also reports the current artifact.

file_id.description: The requested presented-file ID this entry answers for.

artifact_id.description: Artifact ID (`art_` prefix). Also the key of the public-share link.

title.description: Gallery display title of the published artifact.

gallery_path.description: Console-relative path of the artifact page: `/ai-sre/artifacts/<artifact_id>`.

ArtifactFileStateRequest.description: Probe publish state for a batch of presented files.

file_ids.description: Presented-file IDs (`pf_` prefix) to check. At most 50 entries per call, counted before duplicates and empty strings are removed; more fails with `InvalidParameter`.

items.description: One entry per requested file whose session file path currently has a live gallery artifact; files without one, and unknown IDs, are omitted. An empty array when none match.

artifact_id.description: Artifact ID (`art_` prefix). Also the key of the public-share link.

ArtifactListRequest.description: Filter and paginate the artifact gallery.

scope.description: Visibility scope. `all` (default) lists the caller's own personal artifacts plus artifacts of every team the caller belongs to; `personal` lists only the caller's own; `team` lists only team-owned artifacts of the caller's teams.

team_ids.description: Restrict to artifacts owned by these team IDs, intersected with the `scope` filter. Non-positive IDs are ignored; teams the caller does not belong to return nothing, and personal artifacts are excluded whenever this is set.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the artifact title.

page.description: Page number, 1-based. Values below 1 are treated as 1.

limit.description: Number of artifacts per page. Values below 1 fall back to 20; values above 100 are capped at 100 (not rejected).

orderby.description: Sort field: `created_at` (publish time) or `updated_at` (last change). Empty sorts by `updated_at` descending. In every case the caller's pinned artifacts come first, and `artifact_id` breaks ties.

asc.description: Sort ascending when true, descending when false. Applies only when `orderby` is set.

items.description: Artifacts on this page; the caller's pinned artifacts come first. An empty array when nothing matches.

total.description: Total number of artifacts matching the filter across all pages.

ArtifactPublishFromFileRequest.description: Publish a session-produced file to the artifact gallery.

file_id.description: Presented-file ID (`pf_` prefix) of a file produced in a session, as shown on the file card in chat.

title.description: Gallery display title. Trimmed; must be non-empty.

ArtifactPublishResponse.description: Result of publishing a file to the gallery.

artifact_id.description: Artifact ID (`art_` prefix). Also the key of the public-share link.

gallery_path.description: Console-relative path of the artifact page: `/ai-sre/artifacts/<artifact_id>`.

artifact_id.description: Artifact ID (`art_` prefix). Also the key of the public-share link.

public_url.description: Anonymous public link, `<console origin>/share/artifact/<artifact_id>`. Anyone with the link can view the content without signing in. The link is the same on every enable.

shared_by.description: Person ID of the member who enabled sharing. A snapshot sync keeps the original value.

shared_at.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds of the last share enable or snapshot sync.

ArtifactSignRequest.description: Request signed download/preview URLs for a presented file.

share_token.description: Optional session share-link token. Needed only when the caller reaches the file through a shared session link rather than account membership.

ArtifactUpdateRequest.description: Partial update of a gallery artifact. Only provided fields change.

artifact_id.description: Artifact ID (`art_` prefix). Also the key of the public-share link.

title.description: New title. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed; a blank value fails with `InvalidParameter`. Omit or send `null` to keep the current title.

team_id.description: Transfer target. `0` moves the artifact to personal scope and only its creator may do that; a positive value moves it to that team, and the caller must be a member of the team; a negative value fails with `InvalidParameter`. Omit or send `null` to keep the current scope. The creator (`person_id`) never changes.

AssignIncidentRequest.description: Parameters for dispatching one or more incidents to a target. Provide `incident_id` or `incident_ids` but not both.

incident_id.description: Single incident ID. Ignored when `incident_ids` is also provided.

incident_ids.description: Incident IDs to assign in bulk; obtain them from `POST /incident/list`.

assigned_to.description: Assignment target. Set `person_ids`, `escalate_rule_id`, or `emails`; when none is set, the server re-runs the channel's escalation rule matching.

AssignedTo.description: Assignment target. In requests, set `person_ids`, `escalate_rule_id`, or `emails`; when none is set the server re-runs the channel's escalation rule matching. In responses the object is always present; an incident that was never assigned has empty `type`, `id`, and `assigned_at` of `0`.

escalate_rule_id.description: Escalation rule ID (MongoDB ObjectID) to drive assignment.

layer_idx.description: Zero-based escalation level within `escalate_rule_id` (`0` = first level). Responders are taken from this level.

type.description: How the assignment happened: `assign` first assignment; `reassign` reassignment of an already assigned incident; `escalate` moved by the escalation flow; `reopen` reassignment after the incident was reopened; empty string in responses when the incident was never assigned. Omit it in requests and the server derives it.

emails.description: Member emails; each is resolved to a member ID and merged into `person_ids`. Emails without a matching member are ignored.

notify.description: Override the notification channels used for this assignment.

follow_preference.description: `true`: notify each person through their personal notification preference. `false`: use `personal_channels`, which must then be non-empty. When omitted, `personal_channels` must be set.

personal_channels.description: Channels used when `follow_preference` is `false`: `sms`, `voice`, `email`, `push` (mobile app push), or an IM app channel written as `feishu_app:<integration_id>`, `dingtalk_app:<integration_id>`, `wecom_app:<integration_id>`, `slack_app:<integration_id>`, or `teams_app:<integration_id>`. Ignored when `follow_preference` is `true`.

template_id.description: Notification template ID (MongoDB ObjectID).

escalate_rule_name.description: Escalation rule name, filled by the server in responses; ignored in requests.

assigned_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the assignment was made; set by the server.

id.description: Assignment ID generated by the server for each assignment; set by the server.

effective_person_ids.description: Member IDs that actually received the assignment: `person_ids` plus the members of the selected escalation level, deduplicated and sorted. Set by the server; omitted when empty.

created_at.description: Timestamp of the operation in Unix epoch milliseconds.

account_id.description: ID of the account the entry belongs to.

member_id.description: ID of the member who performed the action. 0 when the action was performed by the account principal itself.

member_name.description: Display name of the member. Empty when `member_id` is 0.

ip.description: Client IP address of the caller.

operation_name.description: Human-readable Chinese label of the operation (e.g. `创建模板`).

body.description: JSON-encoded request body. Bodies containing sensitive fields are base64url-encoded instead; bodies over 10 KB are replaced by a truncation placeholder.

Key.description: Name of a URL path parameter (the `:xxx` placeholder in the route).

Value.description: The actual value of that path parameter in this request.

params.description: URL path parameters as an array of `Key`/`Value` pairs (an empty array when none). Some deployments return the same array as a JSON-encoded string.

is_dangerous.description: True if this is flagged as a high-risk operation.

is_write.description: True for mutating operations; false for read-only ones.

principal_kind.description: Kind of the caller. `member` — a member or account-owner session; `service` — an app key or a short-lived key issued to AI SRE.

credential_type.description: Credential type used for the call. `app_key` for a long-lived console app key, `ephemeral_app_key` for a short-lived key issued to AI SRE, and an empty string for member sessions.

credential_id.description: ID of the credential (the app key ID) when `credential_type` is `app_key`; 0 otherwise.

items.description: Array of all auditable operation types (only APIs flagged for audit); always an array, possibly empty.

name.description: Stable machine-readable operation name for use as a filter.

name_cn.description: Human-readable Chinese label shown in the console.

id.description: Audit record ID — the `id` of a row returned by `POST /monit/rule/audits`, not the rule ID. A rule ID is looked up as an audit record ID, which usually returns `InvalidParameter` (`alert rule audit not found`) or an unrelated record.

AuditSearchRequest.description: Filter criteria for audit log search. Time range is required.

start_time.description: Start of the search window, Unix epoch seconds. Exclusive — entries at exactly this second are not included.

end_time.description: End of the search window, Unix epoch seconds. Inclusive. Must be after `start_time`; maximum span 90 days.

limit.description: Page size, 0–99. Omit or set to 0 to let the server choose the page size (it may return every matching entry).

request_id.description: Filter to a single request by its unique request ID.

search_after_ctx.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned by the previous response. Leave empty for the first page.

operations.description: Filter to specific operation names. Use `POST /audit/operation/list` to get the valid set.

person_id.description: Filter by the operator's member ID (get IDs from `POST /member/list`). Pass the account ID to match actions performed by the account principal itself.

is_dangerous.description: When true, return only high-risk (dangerous) operations.

is_write.description: When true, return only write operations; when false, return only read operations.

docs.description: Audit log entries for this page, newest first. Omitted when the page is empty.

search_after_ctx.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Empty string when there are no more results.

total.description: Total matching entries in the search window.

name.description: Display name of the rule, 1–255 characters; leading and trailing spaces are trimmed.

team_id.description: Scope of the rule. `0` or omitted: a personal rule owned by the caller. `>0`: a team rule; the caller must be a member of that team. The scope cannot be changed after creation.

run_in.description: Where the rule's runs execute. `web` (default): in a web console session. `current-chat`: in the IM chat the rule is created from; accepted only from a live IM conversation with the AI SRE agent, so API calls that send it get `400`.

enabled.description: Whether the rule's automatic triggers (schedule, HTTP POST, On-call incident, war room) are armed after creation. Defaults to `false`. Manual runs work either way.

cron_expr.description: Schedule in local time of `timezone`. Accepts 4 fields (`hour day month weekday`, minute defaults to 0) or 5 fields (`minute hour day month weekday`). The minute must be one fixed integer; seconds (6 fields) are not supported; setting both day-of-month and day-of-week is rejected. Required even for rules that use only other triggers: send a valid expression with `schedule_trigger_enabled=false`.

timezone.description: IANA time zone name used to evaluate `cron_expr`, e.g. `Asia/Shanghai`. Ambiguous names such as `Local`, `CST`, `UTC+8`, and `GMT+8` are rejected. When omitted: the caller's member time zone, then the account time zone, then `Asia/Shanghai`.

schedule_trigger_enabled.description: Whether the schedule trigger is enabled. Defaults to `true` when omitted; send `false` for rules that should fire only from other triggers.

prompt.description: Task instruction sent to the AI SRE agent on every run. Must not be empty after trimming spaces.

environment_kind.description: Runtime environment kind. Omit or send an empty value for automatic selection. One of: `cloud` (platform-hosted cloud sandbox), `byoc` (a self-hosted BYOC runner in the account, used with `environment_id`); automatic selection prefers an online BYOC runner and falls back to the cloud sandbox.

environment_id.description: BYOC runner ID. Required when `environment_kind=byoc` and rejected for other kinds. A personal rule can only use account-scope runners; a team rule can use account-scope runners or runners of its own team.

http_post_trigger_enabled.description: Whether to create an enabled HTTP POST trigger. When `true`, the response carries `http_post_trigger_url` and the one-time `http_post_token`.

oncall_incident_trigger_enabled.description: Whether the On-call incident trigger is enabled. When the trigger is created (this is `true`, or channel IDs or severities are sent), both `oncall_incident_channel_ids` and `oncall_incident_severities` must be non-empty.

oncall_incident_channel_ids.description: Channel IDs to watch; incidents in these channels can start a run. Each ID must be positive.

oncall_incident_severities.description: Incident severities to watch: `Critical` (most severe), `Warning`, or `Info` (least severe) — the On-call incident severity levels.

oncall_incident_merge_similar.description: Whether to merge similar incidents into one analysis. When `true` (default), an incident that closely resembles one already being analyzed by this rule (a run in progress or finished within the last 10 minutes) joins that run's session instead of starting a new one; its own run is recorded as `skipped` with `joined_session_id` set. When `false`, every matching incident starts its own run.

war_room_trigger_enabled.description: Whether the war room trigger is enabled. It fires when a war room (IM group chat) is created for an incident in one of `war_room_channel_ids` with a severity in `war_room_severities`; the agent then runs inside that group chat. When the trigger is created (this is `true`, or `war_room_channel_ids` is sent), both lists must be non-empty.

war_room_channel_ids.description: Channel IDs whose war rooms start a run. Each ID must be positive.

war_room_severities.description: Incident severities that start a run when their war room is created: `Critical` (most severe), `Warning`, or `Info` (least severe) — the On-call incident severity levels.

rule_id.description: Rule ID, from the list returned by `POST /safari/automation/rule/list`.
Rule ID (prefix `arule_`). Pass it as `rule_id` to get, update, delete, run, and list-runs calls.

account_id.description: ID of the account that owns the rule.

team_id.description: Scope team ID; `0` means a personal rule. Fixed at creation.

owner_id.description: Person ID of the member who created the rule. For a personal rule, the only person who can manage it.

name.description: Display name of the rule.

enabled.description: Whether the rule's automatic triggers are armed. A disabled rule can still be run manually. A personal rule is disabled automatically when its owner leaves the account.

run_scope.description: Hidden session run scope. One of: `person` (personal rule, team_id=0, runs as the creator; disabled when the creator leaves the account), `team` (team rule, team_id>0, owned by the team and shared with its members; survives the creator leaving). Derived from the rule's team_id.

cron_expr.description: Normalized 5-field cron expression (`minute hour day month weekday`), evaluated in `timezone`.

timezone.description: IANA timezone `cron_expr` is evaluated in. Always populated for rules created after this field shipped; empty on legacy rows created before it, which still resolve to UTC when scheduled.

prompt.description: Task instruction sent to the AI SRE agent on every run.

environment_kind.description: Runtime environment kind. Omit or send an empty value for automatic selection. One of: `cloud` (platform-hosted cloud sandbox), `byoc` (self-hosted BYOC runner in the account); an empty value means automatic selection (prefers an online BYOC runner, falls back to the cloud sandbox).

environment_id.description: BYOC runner ID when `environment_kind=byoc`; empty string otherwise.

schedule_trigger_id.description: Schedule trigger ID. Omitted if the rule has no schedule trigger.

schedule_trigger_enabled.description: Whether the schedule trigger is enabled.

http_post_trigger_id.description: HTTP POST trigger ID. Omitted when the rule has no HTTP POST trigger.

http_post_trigger_url.description: Path to fire the HTTP POST trigger, `/safari/automation/triggers/{trigger_id}/fire`, relative to the API base URL. Send `POST` with `Authorization: Bearer <http_post_token>`. Omitted when the rule has no HTTP POST trigger.

http_post_trigger_enabled.description: Whether the HTTP POST trigger is enabled.

oncall_incident_trigger_id.description: On-call incident trigger ID. Omitted when the rule has no On-call incident trigger.

oncall_incident_trigger_enabled.description: Whether the On-call incident trigger is enabled.

oncall_incident_channel_ids.description: Channel IDs the On-call incident trigger watches. Omitted when the rule has no such trigger.

oncall_incident_severities.description: Incident severities the On-call incident trigger watches: `Critical` (most severe), `Warning`, or `Info` (least severe) — the On-call incident severity levels. Omitted when the rule has no such trigger.

oncall_incident_merge_similar.description: Whether similar incidents are merged into one analysis (see the create request). `true` when the rule has no On-call incident trigger.

war_room_trigger_id.description: War room trigger ID. Omitted when the rule has no war room trigger.

war_room_trigger_enabled.description: Whether the war room trigger is enabled.

war_room_channel_ids.description: Channel IDs whose war rooms start a run. Omitted when the rule has no war room trigger.

war_room_severities.description: Incident severities whose war rooms start a run: `Critical` (most severe), `Warning`, or `Info` (least severe) — the On-call incident severity levels. Omitted when the rule has no war room trigger.

execution_place.description: Where runs started by the schedule, HTTP POST, On-call incident, and manual triggers execute: `web_console` (a web console session) or `im` (the IM chat the rule was created from). War room runs always execute in the war room's group chat. Fixed at creation.

execution_location.description: Read-only description of where the rule runs.

place.description: Same as the rule's `execution_place`: `web_console` runs in a web console session, `im` runs in the bound IM chat.

run_scope.description: `person`: runs as the owner; `team`: runs under the team in `team_id`.

team_id.description: Team the runs belong to; `0` for a personal rule.

platform.description: IM platform of the bound chat: `feishu` (Feishu/Lark), `dingtalk` (DingTalk), `wecom` (WeCom), `slack` (Slack), `teams` (Microsoft Teams). Present only when `place=im`.

conversation_mode.description: Conversation type of the bound chat: `direct` (one-to-one chat with the bot), `group_chat` (a group chat), `group_thread` (a thread in a group chat), `war_room_chat` (an incident war room). Present only when `place=im`.

chat_name.description: Name of the bound chat. Present only when `place=im` and the name is known.

description.description: Human-readable destination label: `Web console` for web console rules, otherwise the chat name or platform and conversation type.

last_run.description: The rule's most recent run. Returned only by List Automation rules, and only when the rule has run at least once.

run_id.description: Run ID, as in List Automation runs.

status.description: Run status, same meanings as `status` in List Automation runs: `queued`, `running`, `retrying` (in progress); `succeeded`, `partial`, `failed`, `skipped` (did not execute or merged into another run), `abandoned` (never completed), `blocked` (ended waiting on a connector authorization).

http_post_token.description: HTTP POST trigger token. Returned only in the response that issues it: create with `http_post_trigger_enabled=true`, an update that creates the trigger, or an update with `rotate_http_post_trigger_token=true`. Save it; it cannot be read again.

can_edit.description: `true` when the caller can manage (get, update, delete, run) this rule: the owner of a personal rule, or a member of a team rule's team. Account owners and admins get no exemption.

created_at.description: Creation time, Unix milliseconds.

updated_at.description: Last update time, Unix milliseconds.

schedule_next_fire_at_ms.description: Next scheduled fire time, Unix milliseconds. 0 means no future scheduled fire is available.

AutomationRuleListRequest.description: List Automation rules visible to the caller: their own personal rules plus rules of teams they belong to. Account owners and admins are bounded the same way.

limit.description: Page size. Values below 1 fall back to 20; values above 200 are capped at 200.

scope.description: Scope filter: `all` (default) your personal rules plus rules of your teams; `personal` only your personal rules; `team` only rules of your teams.

team_ids.description: Filter to these team IDs; this narrows results and does not expand access.

include_person.description: Legacy switch. Only read when `scope` is empty: `false` behaves like `scope=team`; otherwise ignored.

enabled.description: Filter by enabled state: `true` returns only enabled rules, `false` only disabled; omit or pass null for no filter.

keyword.description: Returns rules whose name contains this text. At most 64 characters.

total.description: Number of rules matching the filters across all pages.

rules.description: Array of automation rules for the current page, used with `total` for pagination.

AutomationRuleUpdateRequest.description: Update an Automation rule. Omit or send null on a field to leave it unchanged.

rule_id.description: Target rule ID, from the list returned by `POST /safari/automation/rule/list`.

name.description: New display name, at most 255 characters. An empty string after trimming is rejected.

team_id.description: The rule's scope cannot be changed. Omit this field, or send the current value; any other value returns `400`.

enabled.description: Whether the rule's automatic triggers are armed. Omit to keep the current value.

cron_expr.description: New schedule, same format as on create: 4 fields (`hour day month weekday`) or 5 fields (`minute hour day month weekday`), fixed-integer minute, no seconds, not both day-of-month and day-of-week. Omit to keep the current expression.

timezone.description: New IANA time zone for `cron_expr`. An empty string stores `UTC`. Omit or send `null` to keep the current time zone.

schedule_trigger_enabled.description: Whether the schedule trigger is enabled. Omit to keep the current value.

prompt.description: New task instruction for the agent. Omit to keep the current one.

environment_kind.description: New runtime environment: `""` automatic selection (prefers an online BYOC runner, falls back to the cloud sandbox), `cloud` platform-hosted cloud sandbox, `byoc` the runner in `environment_id`. Sending this without `environment_id` clears the stored `environment_id`.

environment_id.description: BYOC runner ID; required when the resulting `environment_kind` is `byoc`, rejected otherwise.

http_post_trigger_enabled.description: Enable or disable the HTTP POST trigger. `true` on a rule without one creates it and returns its token in this response.

oncall_incident_trigger_enabled.description: Enable or disable the On-call incident trigger. Creating it on a rule that has none also needs `oncall_incident_channel_ids` and `oncall_incident_severities`.

oncall_incident_channel_ids.description: Replaces the watched channel IDs when non-empty; an empty or omitted list keeps the stored IDs.

oncall_incident_severities.description: Replaces the watched severities when non-empty (`Critical` (most severe), `Warning`, or `Info` (least severe) — the On-call incident severity levels); an empty or omitted list keeps the stored values.

oncall_incident_merge_similar.description: Whether to merge similar incidents into one analysis (see the create request). Omit to keep the current value.

war_room_trigger_enabled.description: Enable or disable the war room trigger. Creating it on a rule that has none also needs `war_room_channel_ids` and `war_room_severities`. Omit to keep the current value.

war_room_channel_ids.description: Replaces the channel IDs whose war rooms start a run when non-empty; an empty or omitted list keeps the stored IDs.

war_room_severities.description: Replaces the war room severities when non-empty (`Critical` (most severe), `Warning`, or `Info` (least severe) — the On-call incident severity levels); an empty or omitted list keeps the stored values.

rotate_http_post_trigger_token.description: When `true`, issues a new HTTP POST trigger token and invalidates the old one. The trigger must exist and be enabled. The new token is returned only in this response.

session_id.description: AI SRE session the run executed in. Omitted when the run has not started a session, when it joined another run (see `joined_session_id`), or when it executed in an IM chat.

session_name.description: Display name of the run's session, stamped via a batch lookup. Omitted when empty or when the lookup fails.

joined_session_id.description: For an On-call incident run merged into a similar incident's analysis (`status=skipped`): the session it joined. Omitted otherwise.

joined_session_name.description: Display name of `joined_session_id`. Omitted when empty or when the name lookup fails.

kind.description: Run kind; runs listed for a rule are always `automation_rule`.

account_id.description: ID of the account that owns the run.

rule_id.description: ID of the rule this run belongs to.

trigger_kind.description:
Trigger kind. One of:
| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `schedule` | Fired by the rule's schedule trigger |
| `debug` | Debug run (reserved; current rule runs never carry this kind) |
| `manual` | Started with Run Automation rule |
| `http_post` | Fired via the rule's HTTP POST trigger |
| `oncall_incident` | Fired by a matching On-call incident |
| `war_room_created` | Fired when a war room was created for a matching incident; runs in that group chat |

execution_place.description: Where this run executed: `web_console` (a web console session; `session_id` links to it) or `im` (an IM chat; session details are withheld). `war_room_created` runs are always `im`.

occurrence_key.description: Idempotency key of this occurrence: `manual:<run_id>` for manual runs, `<trigger_id>:<scheduled fire time in Unix ms>` for schedule runs, `oncall_incident:<trigger_id>:<incident_id>` for On-call incident runs.

status.description:
Run status. One of (the first three are in-flight, the rest terminal):
| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `queued` | Enqueued, waiting for a worker |
| `running` | Executing |
| `retrying` | An attempt failed and a retry is scheduled |
| `succeeded` | Completed successfully |
| `partial` | Partially succeeded (currently only produced by memory-consolidation runs; rule runs never reach it) |
| `failed` | Terminal failure, no further retries |
| `skipped` | Not executed (e.g. grace period expired, trigger or rule invalid); the reason is kept on the run record. Also used for an On-call incident run merged into a similar incident's analysis (see `joined_session_id`) |
| `abandoned` | Still in-flight past the stale threshold and swept as never-completed (e.g. worker died) |
| `blocked` | Terminal: the run produced output but ended with a connector waiting on a human to complete authorization (distinct from `failed`) |

attempts.description: Number of execution attempts made for this run.

completed_at.description: Completion time, Unix milliseconds. 0 means not completed.

error_code.description: Error code; empty when the run did not fail.

error_message.description: Error message; empty when the run did not fail.

stats_json.description: Raw run statistics JSON; null when empty.

result_json.description: Raw run result JSON (carries `session_id` once a session started). `null` when empty or when the run executed in an IM chat.

created_at.description: Creation time, Unix milliseconds.

updated_at.description: Last update time, Unix milliseconds.

rule_id.description: Target rule ID, from the list returned by `POST /safari/automation/rule/list`.

limit.description: Page size. Values below 1 fall back to 20.

status.description: Run status filter: `queued`, `running`, `retrying`, `succeeded`, `partial` (partially succeeded), `failed`, `skipped` (e.g. rule or trigger no longer valid), `abandoned` (stale run terminated by the system), `blocked` (terminal; produced output but a connector is waiting on a human authorization); omit for no filter.

trigger_kind.description: Trigger filter: `schedule` schedule trigger, `debug` debug run, `manual` manual run, `http_post` HTTP POST trigger, `oncall_incident` On-call incident trigger, `war_room_created` war room trigger; omit for no filter.

started_after_ms.description: Start-time lower bound, Unix milliseconds. Values below the 180-day run-history retention floor are clamped to it (that floor is also the default when omitted).

started_before_ms.description: Start-time upper bound, Unix milliseconds. Must be greater than or equal to the effective `started_after_ms`; a value below the retention floor yields an empty result.

total.description: Number of runs matching the filters across all pages.

runs.description: Array of run records for the given `rule_id`, filtered by the request's status/trigger-kind/time-range and paginated.

AutomationRunView.description: Reference to the run started by a manual trigger.

run_id.description: Run ID, always populated once a run is created.

session_id.description: AI SRE session started for this run. Omitted when the rule executes in an IM chat (`execution_place=im`).

name.description: Localized template name; use it as the rule `name`.

key.description: Stable, locale-independent template ID (lowercase letters, digits, underscores). Present only on templates that other console pages link to directly; omitted otherwise.

description.description: Localized explanation of what a rule created from this template does.

icon.description: Icon identifier the console displays for the template, e.g. `siren`.

category.description: Free-text, localized name of the group the template is shown under in the console, e.g. `Incident Response`. Groups appear in the order of their first template.

enabled.description: Prefill for the create request's `enabled`.

schedule_trigger_enabled.description: Prefill for `schedule_trigger_enabled`; `true` exactly when `cron_expr` is present.

cron_expr.description: Prefill for `cron_expr`. Omitted when the template does not use the schedule trigger; the create request still needs a valid `cron_expr`.

oncall_incident_trigger_enabled.description: Prefill for `oncall_incident_trigger_enabled`; when `true`, add `oncall_incident_channel_ids` before creating.

oncall_incident_severities.description: Prefill for `oncall_incident_severities` (`Critical` (most severe), `Warning`, or `Info` (least severe) — the On-call incident severity levels). Omitted when the template does not use the On-call incident trigger.

war_room_trigger_enabled.description: Prefill for `war_room_trigger_enabled`; when `true`, add `war_room_channel_ids` before creating.

war_room_severities.description: Prefill for `war_room_severities` (`Critical` (most severe), `Warning`, or `Info` (least severe) — the On-call incident severity levels). Omitted when the template does not use the war room trigger.

locale.description: Template language. A value containing `zh` returns Chinese, one containing `en` returns English, any other non-empty value returns Chinese. When omitted, the `locale`/`lang` query parameter or the `Accept-Language` header decides, defaulting to Chinese.

templates.description: Built-in templates in the resolved language, in display order.

BindWorkItemPostMortemRequest.description: Parameters for bulk-binding an incident's unbound follow-ups to a post-mortem.

post_mortem_id.description: Post-mortem ID (32-character hex string) to bind the follow-ups to.

incident_id.description: Incident ID (MongoDB ObjectID) whose converted, unbound items are bound. It must be linked to `post_mortem_id`.

idempotency_key.description: Client-generated idempotency key (max 128 characters; letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `.`, `:` only).

CalEventIDRequest.description: Calendar event delete request. Provide event_id, or both start_at and end_at.

event_id.description: ID of the event to delete. Omit when clearing a date range.

start_at.description: Start date of the range to clear, in YYYY-MM-DD. Pass together with end_at instead of event_id.

end_at.description: End date of the range to clear, in YYYY-MM-DD (exclusive). Must be later than start_at.

account_id.description: Account ID. Only present for private events.

creator_id.description: Creator person ID. Only present for private events.

cal_id.description: Calendar ID. For public events this is a locale key such as zh-cn.china.official.

event_id.description: Event ID. `cale.<id>` for the calendar's own events, `non_work.YYYYMMDD` for generated non-working weekdays, and `<holiday cal_id>.<id>` for events inherited from a holiday calendar.

is_off.description: Whether the event marks a non-working day.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp (Unix seconds); `0` for generated `non_work.*` entries.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp (Unix seconds); `0` for generated `non_work.*` entries.

CalEventListRequest.description: Calendar event list request. When day > 0 month must also be specified. month and day accept 0 to mean "not filtered".

year.description: Year. Defaults to the current year when omitted.

items.description: Calendar events sorted by start_at.

total.description: Total number of events returned.

days.description: Resolved state of every day in the requested scope, keyed by date (YYYY-MM-DD). The highest layer holding any event decides a day: the calendar's own events (custom), then the linked holiday calendars (holiday), then the weekly workdays (weekly). Inside one layer a working-day event beats a day off, so a make-up workday from a holiday calendar wins over holiday rest days. A day no event covers is a working day.

CalDay.description: Resolved state of one calendar day.

event_id.description: ID of the event that decided the day. Absent when no event covers the day.

is_off.description: Whether the day is a day off.

layer.description: Layer that decided the day: custom = the calendar's own events, holiday = a linked holiday calendar, weekly = the weekly workdays. Absent when no event covers the day.

CalEventUpsertRequest.description: Calendar event upsert request. Provide event_id to update an existing event; omit it to create a new one.

is_off.description: Whether the event marks a non-working day. true = day off, false = working day override.

CalendarCreateRequest.description: Create calendar request. cal_name is required.

cal_name.description: Calendar display name; must be unique within the account.

timezone.description: IANA timezone, e.g. `America/New_York`. Defaults to `Asia/Shanghai` when empty; an invalid name returns `InvalidParameter`.

team_id.description: Owning team ID; `0` or omitted means no team. A nonzero ID must be a team of the account.

workdays.description: Weekly working days, `0` = Sunday … `6` = Saturday. Days not listed are non-working days. When empty, no weekday is treated as non-working.

extra_cal_ids.description: Additional public-holiday calendar IDs to inherit events from (for example zh-cn.china.official).

cal_id.description: ID of the newly created calendar (format cal.<uuid>).

team_id.description: Owning team ID (0 when not assigned).

workdays.description: Weekly working days, `0` = Sunday … `6` = Saturday. Days not listed are non-working days. When empty, no weekday is treated as non-working. Omitted when empty.

extra_cal_ids.description: Inherited public-holiday calendar IDs. Omitted when empty.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp (Unix seconds).

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp (Unix seconds).

creator_id.description: Creator person ID.

updated_by.description: Last updater person ID.

status.description: Calendar status. `enabled` means usable; `deleted` means removed and never returned by list endpoints.

no_locale.description: Disable locale filtering when listing public-holiday calendars.

items.description: Calendar items.

total.description: Total number of calendars returned.

CalendarUpdateRequest.description: Update calendar request. cal_id is required; all other fields are optional and only applied when provided.

cal_name.description: New calendar name; must be unique within the account.

timezone.description: New IANA timezone, e.g. `Asia/Shanghai`; an invalid name returns `InvalidParameter`.

team_id.description: New owning team ID; obtain it from `POST /team/list`. `0` removes the team; a nonzero ID must be a team of the account.

workdays.description: Weekly working days, `0` = Sunday … `6` = Saturday. Days not listed are non-working days. When empty, no weekday is treated as non-working. When sent, replaces the stored list; omit to keep it.

extra_cal_ids.description: Public holiday calendar IDs to inherit events from (see `POST /calendar/list` with `kind` = `region.official.holiday`). When sent, replaces the stored list; an empty array removes them all; omit to keep it.
