channel_id.description: Owning channel ID; obtain it from `POST /channel/list`.

filters.description: Alert event conditions (OR of AND groups). A matching event is discarded entirely: no alert, incident or notification. Keys: `title`, `description`, `severity` (alias `alert_severity`, `event_severity`), `status`, `alert_key`, `title_rule`, `integration_id` (alias `data_source_id`), or any `labels.<name>`. When omitted or empty, the rule matches nothing.

CreateEscalationRuleRequest.description: Parameters for creating an escalation rule.

channel_id.description: Owning channel ID; obtain it from `POST /channel/list`.

priority.description: Evaluation order from `0` to `200`; lower values are evaluated first. Omit to place the rule after all existing rules (current highest priority + 1).

aggr_window.description: Delay in seconds, 0–3600, before the first notification for a newly assigned incident; `0` notifies immediately.

template_id.description: Notification template ID (24-character hex); obtain it from `POST /template/list`. Must exist.

layers.description: Escalation levels in order; the incident starts at the first level.

time_filters.description: Recurring time windows during which the rule can match; omit or leave empty to match at any time.

filters.description: Incident conditions (OR of AND groups), matched against the incident the alert was grouped into, not against the alert. Keys: `title`, `description`, `severity` (alias `incident_severity`, `alert_severity`), `status` (alias `incident_status`, `alert_status`), `dedup_key`, `integration_id` (alias `data_source_id`), or any `labels.<name>`. Omit or leave empty to match every incident in the channel.

field_name.description: Machine name: 1–39 characters of `[a-zA-Z0-9_]`, starting with a letter or underscore. Immutable after creation.

display_name.description: Human-readable name. Must be unique within the account.

field_type.description:
Field type, immutable after creation.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `text` | Free text; `value_type` must be `string`, no `options`. |
| `single_select` | Single choice from `options`; `value_type` must be `string`. |
| `multi_select` | Multiple choices from `options`; `value_type` must be `string`. |
| `checkbox` | Boolean checkbox; `value_type` must be `bool`, no `options`. |

value_type.description: Value type. `checkbox` requires `bool`; all other types require `string`. Immutable after creation. `float` is a reserved value currently rejected for every `field_type`.

options.description: Required and non-empty for `single_select`/`multi_select` (unique strings, each 1–200 chars). Must be omitted or empty for `checkbox`/`text`.

default_value.description: Optional default value. Type must match `field_type`: `bool` for checkbox; one of `options` for single_select; subset of `options` for multi_select; string ≤3000 chars for text.

field_id.description: Newly assigned field ID — 24-character hex ObjectID.

CreateIncidentCommentTypeRequest.description: Parameters for creating a comment type. At most 10 comment types per account.

name.description: Display name. Trimmed before storing; must be unique within the account (case-insensitive). At most 40 characters. Must not contain control or text-direction characters.

color.description: Label color as a hex value in #RRGGBB format. Normalized to uppercase.

CreateIncidentCommentTypeResponse.description: Result of creating a comment type.

comment_type_id.description: ID of the created comment type (24-character hex ObjectID).

CreateIncidentRequest.description: Parameters for manually creating an incident.

title.description: Incident title, up to 512 characters. Required (non-blank) when the account has a create form.

channel_id.description: Channel to file the incident into; must exist in the account. Optional unless the account has a create form; leave it unset for a standalone incident.

assigned_to.description: Who to assign. When omitted or empty, the channel's escalation rules decide (a standalone incident gets no responders); required when the account has a create form. `person_ids`, `escalate_rule_id` and `emails` can be combined — responders are the union. Assignment runs after creation, and its failure does not undo the incident.

person_ids.description: Member IDs to assign directly (1–100). Can be combined with `escalate_rule_id`.

escalate_rule_id.description: Escalation rule ID (MongoDB ObjectID); assigns the people at the rule's `layer_idx` layer.

layer_idx.description: Zero-based escalation-rule layer to assign (default 0, the first layer). Used only with `escalate_rule_id`; an out-of-range value leaves the incident without responders instead of failing the request.

type.description:
Assignment type. Normally omitted: the server then sets `assign`, because a manual create is always a first assignment. A value you send is stored as-is.
- `assign`: first assignment of the incident.
- `reassign`: assignment replacing an earlier one.
- `escalate`: assignment triggered by escalation to the next layer.
- `reopen`: assignment restarted from the first layer after the incident is reopened.

emails.description: Recipients to assign by email (1–100): resolved to account members and merged into `person_ids`; emails with no matching member are ignored.

notify.description: Override the notification channels used for this assignment.

follow_preference.description: When false, use `personal_channels`; when true or omitted, use each responder's personal preference.

personal_channels.description: Channels to use when `follow_preference` is false: `sms`, `voice`, `email`, `push`, or an IM app channel prefixed `feishu_app:`, `dingtalk_app:`, `wecom_app:`, `slack_app:` or `teams_app:`.

template_id.description: Notification template ID (MongoDB ObjectID).

fields.description: Custom field values keyed by field name. When a create form applies, only its visible fields are accepted.

CreateIncidentResponse.description: Result of manually creating an incident.

title.description: Incident title as sent in the request; empty when the request had no title.

CreateInhibitRuleRequest.description: Parameters for creating an inhibit rule.

channel_id.description: Owning channel ID; obtain it from `POST /channel/list`.

equals.description: Keys whose values must be equal on the source alert and the incoming event. Only `title`, `severity` and `labels.<name>` take effect; any other key (for example `data_source_id`) is accepted but makes the rule never fire. Must be present; an empty array also makes the rule inert.

source_filters.description: Conditions the source (inhibiting) alert must match, evaluated against active alerts already stored in the channel. Keys: `title`, `description`, `severity` (alias `incident_severity`, `alert_severity`), `status` (alias `incident_status`, `alert_status`), or any `labels.<name>`. Empty makes the rule inert.

target_filters.description: Conditions the incoming target alert event must match to be inhibited; empty means every incoming event is a target. Keys: `title`, `description`, `severity` (alias `alert_severity`, `event_severity`), `status`, `alert_key`, `title_rule`, `integration_id` (alias `data_source_id`), or any `labels.<name>`.

is_directly_discard.description: When true, matching alert events are discarded entirely; when false, alerts are still recorded but marked as muted by this rule.

CreateSilenceRuleRequest.description: Parameters for creating a silence rule. Exactly one of `time_filter` or `time_filters` must be provided, and `filters` must be non-empty.

channel_id.description: Owning channel ID; obtain it from `POST /channel/list`.

from_incident_id.description: ID of the incident this rule is created from (24-character hex). The incident must exist, and only one enabled silence rule may exist per incident.

time_filters.description: Recurring silence windows. Set exactly one of `time_filters` or `time_filter`.

time_filter.description: One-off silence window. Set exactly one of `time_filter` or `time_filters`.

filters.description: Alert event conditions (OR of AND groups); matching events are silenced while the time window is active. Required, with at least one condition. Keys: `title`, `description`, `severity` (alias `alert_severity`, `event_severity`), `status`, `alert_key`, `title_rule`, `integration_id` (alias `data_source_id`), or any `labels.<name>`.

is_directly_discard.description: When true, matching alert events are discarded entirely; when false, alerts are still recorded but marked as muted by this rule.

is_auto_delete.description: When true, a rule with a one-off `time_filter` is permanently removed about 24 hours after `end_time` (or after its last update, whichever is later). Rules created with `from_incident_id` are cleaned up the same way. Rules with recurring `time_filters` are never removed automatically. Defaults to `false`.

CreateStatusPageChangeRequest.description: Parameters for creating a status page incident or maintenance event. The first update must contain `component_changes` to define affected components; retrospective events require at least 2 updates.

page_id.description: Status page ID; obtain it from `GET /status-page/list`.

type.description: Change type: `incident` unplanned incident, `maintenance` planned maintenance.

description.description: Event description (Markdown). Must not be empty.

status.description: Initial event status. `investigating`/`identified`/`monitoring`/`resolved` apply to incidents; `scheduled`/`ongoing`/`completed` apply to maintenances.

start_at_seconds.description: Event start time in Unix seconds. Maintenances store this value as the scheduled start (with `auto_update_by_schedule`, the time the event switches to `ongoing`); when it is omitted or 0, and always for incidents, the start time is the first update's `at_seconds`.

responders.description: Member IDs responsible for the event.

linked_changes.description: Linked change IDs (related incidents, deployments, etc.).

close_at_seconds.description: Event close time in Unix seconds; must be greater than or equal to the first update's `at_seconds`. For maintenances this is the scheduled end; with `auto_update_by_schedule` the event switches to `completed` at this time, which must be within 30 days from now. For a retrospective event in a terminal status, omitting it uses the latest update's time.

items.description: One timeline update entry.

update_id.description: Update ID. Server-assigned on create; supply when replaying historical updates.

at_seconds.description: Update timestamp in Unix seconds. When omitted or 0 on the first update, defaults to the current time.

status.description:
Change status after this update. May be omitted (or null) when the overall status does not change. The first four values apply to incident-type changes, the last three to maintenance-type changes.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `investigating` | Investigating (incident). |
| `identified` | Root cause identified (incident). |
| `monitoring` | Fix deployed, monitoring (incident). |
| `resolved` | Resolved (incident). |
| `scheduled` | Scheduled (maintenance). |
| `ongoing` | In progress (maintenance). |
| `completed` | Completed (maintenance). |
New component status. `operational`/`degraded`/`partial_outage`/`full_outage` apply to incidents; `operational`/`under_maintenance` apply to maintenances.

component_changes.description: Component status transitions applied by this update.

updates.description: Timeline updates in non-decreasing `at_seconds` order. At least one update is required, and at least one of them must contain `component_changes`. Immediate events normally pass one update; retrospective events must pass at least 2.

notify_subscribers.description: Notify subscribers about this event. On creation one notification is sent for the last update; later timeline entries also notify while this is `true`.

auto_update_by_schedule.description: Maintenance only: automatically advance the status based on the scheduled window.

is_retrospective.description: Mark the event as retrospective (a past event recorded afterwards). Requires at least 2 entries in `updates`.

draft_id.description: ID of a draft created by `POST /status-page/draft/create` to publish with this event. The draft must be pending, target this `page_id` and `type`, and have no `change_id`; it is marked published once the event is created. Omit when not publishing a draft.

CreateStatusPageChangeTimelineRequest.description: Parameters for appending an update to a status page event timeline.

page_id.description: Status page ID; obtain it from `GET /status-page/list`.

change_id.description: Target change ID; obtain it from `GET /status-page/change/list`.

at_seconds.description: Update time in Unix seconds; must not be earlier than the event's latest timeline entry. Defaults to the current time when omitted or 0.

status.description:
Event status after this update; must be valid for the event type. Pass the current status to post an update without a status change. When moving to `resolved` or `completed`, all affected components must be back to `operational`.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `investigating` | Investigating (incident). |
| `identified` | Root cause identified (incident). |
| `monitoring` | Fix deployed, monitoring (incident). |
| `resolved` | Resolved (incident). |
| `scheduled` | Scheduled (maintenance). |
| `ongoing` | In progress (maintenance). |
| `completed` | Completed (maintenance). |

description.description: Update description (Markdown). Must not be empty.

status.description: New component status. `operational`/`degraded`/`partial_outage`/`full_outage` apply to incidents; `operational`/`under_maintenance` apply to maintenances.

component_changes.description: Component status transitions applied by this update. Component IDs must be unique.

draft_id.description: ID of a pending draft created by `POST /status-page/draft/create` whose `change_id` is this event; it is marked published when the update is stored. Omit when not publishing a draft.

CreateStatusPageDraftRequest.description: Parameters for storing a status page draft. The `draft` payload is stored verbatim; only the validated fields listed below are interpreted.

draft.description: Draft payload, stored verbatim (at most 64 KB serialized). The server validates the fields below and keeps any other fields unchanged for the console.

v.description: Payload format version chosen by the producer; stored, not interpreted.

page_id.description: Target status page ID; must belong to the caller's account.

page_name.description: Page name for display in the console; not validated.

type.description: Event type the draft creates or updates: `incident` unplanned incident, `maintenance` planned maintenance.

name.description: Event title, 1 to 255 characters.

message.description: Event or update description (Markdown). Must not be empty.

change_id.description: Event to append an update to; it must be an event of the same `type` on `page_id`. Omit or pass 0 to draft a new event.

status.description: Proposed event status; when set, it must be valid for `type` (`investigating`/`identified`/`monitoring`/`resolved` for incidents, `scheduled`/`ongoing`/`completed` for maintenances).

component_id.description: Component ID; must exist on the page.

name.description: Component name for display; not validated.

status.description: Proposed component status; when set, it must be valid for `type` (`operational`/`degraded`/`partial_outage`/`full_outage` for incidents, `operational`/`under_maintenance` for maintenances).

start_time.description: Scheduled start in Unix seconds, for a new maintenance.

end_time.description: Scheduled end in Unix seconds, for a new maintenance; must be greater than `start_time` when both are set.

source.description: Free-form text recording where the draft came from, such as an AI session reference; stored and shown with the draft, not interpreted. Up to 64 characters.

name.description: Display name of the status page.

url_name.description: URL-safe slug; normalized to lowercase with non-alphanumeric characters replaced by hyphens, and must be unique among the account's pages of the same type.

type.description: Visibility type: `public` accessible to anyone, `internal` restricted to logged-in members of this account.

custom_domain.description: Custom domain; allowed only for public pages and must not be used by another status page.

page_title.description: Accepted for compatibility but not stored; it has no effect.

page_header.description: Header content shown on the status page.

page_footer.description: Footer content shown on the status page.

date_view.description: How change dates are displayed: `calendar` calendar view, `list` list view.

display_uptime_mode.description: Uptime display mode: `chart_and_percentage` chart plus percentage, `chart` chart only, `none` hidden.

custom_links.description: Custom navigation links shown on the status page.

key.description: Link text shown on the page.

value.description: URL the link text points to, such as `https://www.example.com`.

contact_info.description: Get-in-touch contact, such as a mailto or website URL.

subscription.description: Subscription channel toggles; both default to `false`. A public page can enable only `email` and an internal page only `im`.

page_id.description: Created status page ID.

page_url_name.description: Final URL-safe slug assigned to the status page.

CreateWarRoomRequest.description: Parameters for opening an incident war room in an IM integration.

integration_id.description: IM integration ID with war room enabled; obtain it from `POST /datasource/im/war-room-enabled/list`. Feishu, DingTalk, WeCom (self-built app only), and Slack are supported.

member_ids.description: Member IDs to invite into the group; every ID must be a valid member of the account.

add_observers.description: When true, also invite members who were assigned or added as responders earlier but are no longer current responders.

CreateWorkItemRequest.description: Parameters for creating an incident work item.

item_type.description:
Work item type.
- `action`: a to-do on an incident that is not closed yet; must not set `post_mortem_id`.
- `follow_up`: a post-mortem follow-up on a closed incident; `post_mortem_id` is optional.

title.description: Item title, at most 512 characters; leading and trailing spaces are trimmed and it must not be blank.

status.description: Initial status. One of `open`, `in_progress`, `done`, `cancelled`; defaults to `open` when omitted or blank.

priority.description: Optional free-form priority, at most 64 characters. The console uses `high`, `medium` and `low`; any other string is stored as-is.

incident_id.description: Incident ID (MongoDB ObjectID) the item is anchored to.

post_mortem_id.description: Post-mortem ID (32-character hex string). Forbidden for `action`. Optional for `follow_up`: when set, the incident must be linked to that report; when omitted, the incident's post-mortem is used if it exists.

assignee_ids.description: Legacy alias for the initial assignees. Equivalent to `assignees` with every entry `type` `person`. Mutually exclusive with `assignees`: sending both returns an error. Assignees must be active members who can already read the anchor; assignment never grants access.

assignees.description: Initial assignees. Each entry is `{type, id?}`. `type` is `person` or `ai_sre`; an `ai_sre` entry omits `id`. Mutually exclusive with `assignee_ids`: sending both returns an error. `assignee_ids` is the legacy alias and is equivalent to an all-`person` list. At most 20 entries. Person assignees must be active members who can already read the anchor; assignment never grants access.

idempotency_key.description: Client-generated idempotency key (max 128 characters; letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `.`, `:` only).

CustomFieldValues.description: Values keyed by account custom field name. The active form determines the allowed keys, types, and required fields.

DSClickHouseConfig.description: ClickHouse datasource configuration. TLS fields are inherited from TLSClientConfig.

idle_conns.description: Maximum number of idle connections in the pool; `0` or omitted uses the default of 4.

lifetime_seconds.description: Maximum connection lifetime in seconds; `0` or omitted uses the default of 600 (10 minutes).

max_execution_seconds.description: Max query execution time in seconds.

open_conns.description: Maximum number of open connections in the pool; `0` or omitted uses the default of 32.

timeout_mills.description: Per-query timeout in milliseconds; `0` or omitted uses the default of 10000 (10 seconds).

tls_ca.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate used to verify the server certificate.

tls_cert.description: PEM-encoded client certificate for mutual TLS; must be configured together with `tls_key`.

tls_enabled.description: Whether TLS is enabled; when `false`, all `tls_*` fields are cleared before saving.

tls_key.description: PEM-encoded client private key; must be configured together with `tls_cert`.

tls_max_version.description: Maximum TLS version, one of `1.0`, `1.1`, `1.2`, `1.3`; empty means no constraint.

tls_min_version.description: Minimum TLS version, one of `1.0`, `1.1`, `1.2`, `1.3`; empty means no constraint and it must not exceed `tls_max_version`.

tls_server_name.description: Server name used for TLS SNI and certificate verification; defaults to the host from the connection address when empty.

tls_skip_verify.description: Whether to skip server certificate verification (insecure, for self-signed setups only).

deployment.description: Deployment type; required. `cloud` uses Elastic Cloud (`address` is not needed); `self-managed` uses a self-hosted cluster (`address` is required).

timeout_mills.description: Per-query timeout in milliseconds; `0` or omitted uses the default of 10000 (10 seconds).

cloud_id.description: Elastic Cloud deployment ID. Only for `cloud` deployment.

api_key.description: Elastic Cloud API key. Only for `cloud` deployment.

password.description: Authentication password for self-managed clusters; ignored when `service_token` is set.

service_token.description: Service token; overrides username/password if set.

tls_ca.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate used to verify the Elasticsearch server certificate.

certificate_fingerprint.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the Elasticsearch CA certificate, used to verify the server chain (the recommended check for ES 8 default security).

headers.description: Custom HTTP headers added to every request, each entry formatted as `Key: Value`.

password.description: Authentication password; supports ${env:NAME}. Required with `username` for SASL authentication and must be empty when `sasl_mechanism` is `none`. On update, omit to keep the stored password; explicitly send an empty string to clear. Literal passwords are omitted from responses.

sasl_mechanism.description: SASL mechanism: none (default, no credentials), plain, scram-sha-256, scram-sha-512 (require username and password).

timeout_ms.description: Connection timeout in milliseconds; defaults to 5000 when omitted.

tls_ca.description: PEM CA certificates or an ${env:NAME} reference.

tls_cert.description: PEM client certificate or ${env:NAME}; configure both tls_cert and tls_key.

tls_enabled.description: Whether TLS is enabled; defaults to false. When false, all `tls_*` fields are cleared on save.

tls_key.description: PEM client private key or ${env:NAME}; configure both tls_cert and tls_key. Omit on update to preserve; an empty string clears it. Literal keys are omitted from responses.

tls_max_version.description: Maximum TLS version: 1.2 or 1.3; empty means no constraint. Must not be below the minimum.

tls_server_name.description: Server name used for TLS SNI and certificate verification; defaults to the host from the connection address when empty.

tls_skip_verify.description: Skip server certificate verification when TLS is enabled.

username.description: Authentication username; an ${env:NAME} reference is supported. Required when `sasl_mechanism` is `plain`, `scram-sha-256` or `scram-sha-512`; must be empty when it is `none`.

tencent_cls.description: Tencent CLS credentials. Required when `type_ident` is `tencent_cls`.

type_ident.description:
Datasource type.

Alerting types (can evaluate alert rules):
- `prometheus`: Prometheus-compatible metrics.
- `loki`: Grafana Loki logs.
- `mysql`: MySQL.
- `oracle`: Oracle Database.
- `postgres`: PostgreSQL.
- `clickhouse`: ClickHouse.
- `elasticsearch`: Elasticsearch.
- `sls`: Alibaba Cloud Simple Log Service.
- `tencent_cls`: Tencent Cloud Log Service (CLS).
- `victorialogs`: VictoriaLogs.

Diagnostic-only types (cannot evaluate alerts, `alerting_enabled` is always `false`):
- `redis_node`: a single Redis node.
- `redis_sentinel`: Redis Sentinel.
- `mongodb_mongod`: a MongoDB mongod instance.
- `mongodb_mongos`: a MongoDB mongos router.
- `kafka`: a Kafka cluster.

The `payload` key that holds the type-specific settings has the same name as the type.

name.description: Datasource name, unique within the account across all types.

enabled.description: Whether business execution is enabled. Disabled datasources reject business queries and tools; enabling does not change alerting_enabled.

note.description: Free-text note; an empty string when not set.

address.description: Connection address as stored, after normalization. The format depends on `type_ident`; see the `address` field of the create request for each type. At most 4096 characters.

payload.description: Type-specific configuration block; must contain the key matching `type_ident`. Always `null` in `/monit/datasource/list` responses (the list query does not read the payload column); populated in create/update/info responses. For `tencent_cls`, `secret_key` is masked to an empty string unless it is an `${env:...}` reference. For diagnostic types, password and Kafka tls_key are omitted from responses unless they are ${env:...} references. On update, omit those fields to preserve stored secrets; explicitly send an empty string to clear. Other configuration fields retain their existing behavior.

edge_cluster_name.description: Monitors edge cluster name responsible for evaluating rules using this datasource.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp, Unix epoch seconds.

alerting_enabled.description: Whether alert evaluation is allowed. Alerting also requires enabled=true and an alerting-capable type. Always false for diagnostic-only types; false does not block non-alerting queries or tools.

manage_team_id.description: ID of the managing team. Its members can edit, delete, enable or disable the datasource and view its full configuration. `null` means no managing team: any caller with the Datasources Manage permission can manage it. The creator, the account owner and Admin members can always manage.

readonly_team_ids.description: IDs of the teams allowed to query and reference the datasource, in addition to the managing team, the creator, the account owner and Admin members. `null` or an empty array means every member of the account can query it.

creator_id.description: ID of the member who created the datasource; `null` when not recorded. The creator can always manage the datasource.

my_perm.description:
The caller's access level on this datasource. Only present in list responses.
- `manage`: can edit, delete, enable or disable the datasource, view its configuration and query it.
- `readonly`: can query and reference the datasource but not change it or read its configuration.

type.description:
Return only datasources of this type; omit or leave empty to return all types. An unrecognized value matches nothing and returns an empty array.

Alerting types (can evaluate alert rules):
- `prometheus`: Prometheus-compatible metrics.
- `loki`: Grafana Loki logs.
- `mysql`: MySQL.
- `oracle`: Oracle Database.
- `postgres`: PostgreSQL.
- `clickhouse`: ClickHouse.
- `elasticsearch`: Elasticsearch.
- `sls`: Alibaba Cloud Simple Log Service.
- `tencent_cls`: Tencent Cloud Log Service (CLS).
- `victorialogs`: VictoriaLogs.

Diagnostic-only types (cannot evaluate alerts, `alerting_enabled` is always `false`):
- `redis_node`: a single Redis node.
- `redis_sentinel`: Redis Sentinel.
- `mongodb_mongod`: a MongoDB mongod instance.
- `mongodb_mongos`: a MongoDB mongos router.
- `kafka`: a Kafka cluster.

name.description: Return only the datasource whose name equals this value exactly (names are unique within the account, so at most one item). Omit or leave empty for no name filter.

DataSourceListResponse.description: Datasources of the account that the caller can query, sorted by name; an empty array when nothing matches. `payload` is `null` in every item because the list does not read it; each item also carries `my_perm`.

DataSourceUpsertRequest.description: Request body for creating or updating a datasource. `id` is required for update and ignored on create. An update replaces `type_ident`, `name`, `note`, `address`, `payload` and `edge_cluster_name` with the values sent, so resend them all; only `enabled`, `alerting_enabled`, `manage_team_id` and `readonly_team_ids` keep their current value when omitted. `address` is required for all types except Elasticsearch with `deployment=cloud`.

id.description: Datasource ID. Required for update (an unknown ID, or one in another account, fails with `ResourceNotFound`); ignored on create.

type_ident.description:
Datasource type.

Alerting types (can evaluate alert rules):
- `prometheus`: Prometheus-compatible metrics.
- `loki`: Grafana Loki logs.
- `mysql`: MySQL.
- `oracle`: Oracle Database.
- `postgres`: PostgreSQL.
- `clickhouse`: ClickHouse.
- `elasticsearch`: Elasticsearch.
- `sls`: Alibaba Cloud Simple Log Service.
- `tencent_cls`: Tencent Cloud Log Service (CLS).
- `victorialogs`: VictoriaLogs.

Diagnostic-only types (cannot evaluate alerts, `alerting_enabled` is always `false`):
- `redis_node`: a single Redis node.
- `redis_sentinel`: Redis Sentinel.
- `mongodb_mongod`: a MongoDB mongod instance.
- `mongodb_mongos`: a MongoDB mongos router.
- `kafka`: a Kafka cluster.

The `payload` key that holds the type-specific settings has the same name as the type.

name.description: Datasource name; required and unique within the account across all types. This is the name referenced as `ds_name` in query APIs. Duplicates fail with `InvalidParameter`.

note.description: Free-text note. On update, an omitted or empty value clears the stored note.

address.description:
Connection address, required for every type except `elasticsearch` with `deployment: cloud`. At most 4096 characters after normalization. Format by type:
- `prometheus`, `loki`, `victorialogs`: HTTP URL; `http://` is prepended when the value does not start with `http`.
- `mysql`, `oracle`, `postgres`: `host:port`.
- `clickhouse`: one or more comma-separated `host:port` endpoints; duplicates are rejected.
- `elasticsearch` with `self-managed`: one or more comma-separated HTTP(S) URLs (scheme defaults to `http://`) that share identical query parameters; duplicates are rejected. Not needed for `cloud`.
- `sls`: endpoint without the `http://` or `https://` prefix.
- `tencent_cls`: exactly `cls.tencentcloudapi.com` or `cls.internal.tencentcloudapi.com` (requires Monitors edge >= v0.66.0).
- `redis_node`, `redis_sentinel`, `mongodb_mongod`, `mongodb_mongos`: a single `host:port` (bracket IPv6) with no URI, userinfo or query.
- `kafka`: 1-32 unique comma-separated `host:port` bootstrap addresses (the payload has no broker list).

payload.description: Type-specific configuration block; must include the key named by `type_ident`. An update replaces the whole payload, so resend every setting you want to keep (including credentials of non-diagnostic types, which the info endpoint returns). Exceptions: for the diagnostic types, omit the password (and the Kafka `tls_key`) to keep the stored value or send an empty string to clear it; for `tencent_cls`, an omitted or empty `secret_key` keeps the stored key. Stored secrets are not carried over when `type_ident` changes.

edge_cluster_name.description: Name of the Monitors edge cluster that evaluates rules and runs queries for this datasource. It must be an existing edge cluster of the account, otherwise the call fails with `InvalidParameter`. Changing it on update closes open alerts of rules that use this datasource.

enabled.description: Whether business execution is enabled. Omitted on create: true; omitted on update: preserve the current value. Explicit false disables execution; null is invalid. Does not change alerting_enabled.

alerting_enabled.description: Whether this datasource may evaluate alerts. Omitted on create: true for alerting types, false for diagnostic-only types; omitted on update: preserve current value. null is invalid. redis_node, redis_sentinel, mongodb_mongod, mongodb_mongos and kafka reject true. Disabling is rejected with conflict when enabled rules reference the datasource.

manage_team_id.description: ID of the managing team (see the response field of the same name). On create, omitted means no managing team. On update, omitted keeps the current value, while `null` or `0` clears it. Required whenever `readonly_team_ids` is non-empty.

readonly_team_ids.description: IDs of the teams allowed to query and reference the datasource (see the response field of the same name). On create, omitted means unrestricted. On update, omitted keeps the current value, while `null` or an empty array clears it (everyone can query). Duplicates and `0` are dropped. Requires `manage_team_id`: a non-empty list without a managing team fails with `InvalidParameter`.

kind.description: Execution mode: `instant` evaluates at a single timestamp, `range` evaluates a stepped series, and `window` evaluates one bounded time window.

from_ms.description: Window or range start as a Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds. Required for `range`, `window`, and every VictoriaLogs execution; optional for Loki `instant`; rejected by Prometheus `instant`.

to_ms.description: Query end time as a Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds; for `instant` it is the evaluation timestamp.

max_data_points.description: `range` only, required: maximum returned data points; the server computes the effective step from the window.

min_step_seconds.description: `range` only, optional: positive lower bound in seconds for the computed step.

PendingUserMessage.description: A queued user message that the agent has not consumed yet, as carried by `pending_messages`.

invocation_id.description: Invocation ID of the queued message.

client_msg_id.description: Client-supplied message ID, echoed back for de-duplication. Omitted when absent.

steering.description: True when the message was sent as a mid-turn steering instruction. Omitted when false.

query.description: Message text.

parts.description: Request parts passed through verbatim (text, file, ref, or skill entries). Omitted when the original message carried none.

expr.description: Query expression evaluated by the datasource; dialect depends on the datasource type.

powersql.description: Whether to run the query with SLS PowerSQL. Omitted keeps the executor default; explicit null is invalid.

SLSQueryParams.description: sls.query parameters for Alibaba Cloud SLS. `execution.kind` must be `window`.

expr.description: Query expression evaluated by the datasource; dialect depends on the datasource type.

account_id.description: Optional consistency check; must equal the authenticated account.

datasource_id.description: ID of the datasource to run the tool against, from `/monit/datasource/list`. The caller needs query access to it. For query tools (`<type>.query`) the ID must not exceed 9007199254740991.

params.description: Tool-specific JSON parameters; omitted means {}. Explicit null is invalid. Query tools (`<type>.query`) use the per-datasource params schemas named in the `tool` description.

tool.description: Single tool name prefixed by the datasource type. Diagnostic tools are defined by the executing Edge (e.g. `mysql.overview`). Query tools are `<type>.query` where `<type>` is one of `prometheus`, `mysql`, `postgres`, `oracle`, `clickhouse`, `elasticsearch`, `loki`, `victorialogs`, `sls`, `tencent_cls`; their `params` follow `PrometheusQueryParams`, `MySQLQueryParams`, `PostgresQueryParams`, `OracleQueryParams`, `ClickHouseQueryParams`, `ElasticsearchQueryParams`, `LokiQueryParams`, `VictoriaLogsQueryParams`, `SLSQueryParams`, or `TencentCLSQueryParams` respectively.

data.description: Tool-specific JSON evidence, preserved without conversion; never null. No nested legacy diagnose envelope.

tool.description: Executed tool name matching the request.

reason.description: Why the result was truncated, as reported by the executing Edge; treat it as an opaque string. The object is present only when the result was truncated.

DeleteWarRoomRequest.description: Parameters for deleting an incident war room.

integration_id.description: IM integration ID; obtain it from `POST /datasource/im/war-room-enabled/list`.

unlink_only.description: When true, only remove the link between the incident and the war room without dissolving the group. Allowed only for account owners and admins, only when the IM integration is disabled or deleted, and requires `chat_id`.

DeleteWorkItemRequest.description: Parameters for soft-deleting a work item.

work_item_id.description: Work item ID (opaque string, max 128 characters).

version.description: The item's current `version` (≥ 1) for optimistic locking.

allOf.description: Aggregated incident + alert metrics for an account/team/channel bucket.

acknowledgement_pct.description: Acknowledgement rate (%): acknowledged incidents ÷ total incidents × 100, rounded to two decimals and capped at 100; 0 when the bucket has no incidents.

mean_seconds_to_ack.description: Mean time to first acknowledgement in seconds; 0 when no incident in the bucket was acknowledged.

mean_seconds_to_close.description: Mean time to close in seconds; 0 when no incident in the bucket was closed.

noise_reduction_pct.description: Noise reduction ratio (%): 100 − incidents ÷ alert events × 100, rounded to two decimals; 0 when there is no alert-event data or alert events do not exceed incidents.

total_engaged_seconds.description: Total engaged time in seconds: each incident contributes the sum of close time minus acknowledgement time across its acknowledged responders.

total_incidents_acknowledged.description: Incidents that were acknowledged at least once.

total_incidents_auto_closed.description: Incidents closed automatically because all alerts recovered.

total_incidents_escalated.description: Incidents that were escalated at least once.

total_incidents_manually_escalated.description: Incidents escalated manually at least once.

total_incidents_reassigned.description: Incidents that were reassigned at least once.

total_incidents_timeout_escalated.description: Incidents escalated on timeout at least once.

total_interruptions.description: Total interruptions: notifications sent via app push, SMS, or voice call; consecutive notifications to the same responder within 60 seconds count as one.

total_seconds_to_ack.description: Total time to first acknowledgement in seconds.

total_seconds_to_close.description: Total time to close in seconds.

items.description: Metric rows, newest bucket first. Buckets or dimension values without incidents produce no row; an empty array means no incidents matched.

DisableIncidentMergeRequest.description: Parameters for disabling automatic merging on incidents.

incident_ids.description: Incident IDs whose automatic merge should be disabled.

DoIncidentCustomActionRequest.description: Parameters for invoking a custom action integration on an incident.

integration_id.description: Custom action integration ID. Must be enabled and associated with the incident's channel.

DoIncidentCustomActionResponse.description: `null` when the action's HTTP request succeeded; an object with `message` when it failed.

message.description: Error returned by the HTTP request to the action's URL (for example, a timeout after 2 seconds).

DutyError.description: Error payload inside the response envelope. Present only on non-2xx responses.

message.description: Human-readable error message in the response language (`locale` / `lang` query parameter or `Accept-Language` header). May name the offending field; do not parse it.
message.example: The specified parameter template_id is not valid.

reason.description: Optional machine-readable rejection reason, including datasource tool failures. Inspect alongside HTTP status and code.

EmptyObject.description: An empty object. Returned as the `data` payload by operations whose success signal is simply the absence of an error.

EmptyResponse.description: No payload. Depending on the operation, `data` is `{}` or omitted from the envelope; rely only on the HTTP 200 status and the absence of `error`.

EnabledTime.description: Time window in which the rule is active.

days.description: Days of week the window applies to, `0` = Sunday through `6` = Saturday; non-empty, no duplicates.

key.description: Event key to match on: `title`, `description`, `labels.<name>` or another alert/change event key. A `labels.<name>` key must use a valid label name.

oper.description:
Match operator.
- `IN`: matches when the key's value matches any of `vals`. A key missing from the event never matches.
- `NOTIN`: matches when the value matches none of `vals`. A key missing from the event always matches.

vals.description: Values to match (at least one). Each value is one of: an exact string; `/regex/` for a regular expression; a wildcard pattern with `*` and `?`; `cidr:<CIDR>` (e.g. `cidr:203.0.113.0/24`) for an IP range; `num:lt:<n>`, `num:le:<n>`, `num:gt:<n>` or `num:ge:<n>` for a numeric comparison.

EnrichRule.description: An enrichment rule with an optional condition and type-specific settings.

if.description: Optional AND-filter list; the rule is skipped unless every filter matches. `null` when the rule has no condition. Filter keys come from the alert/change event vocabulary (e.g. `title`, `labels.severity`).

kind.description:
Rule type.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `extraction` | Extract a value from the alert's `title`, `description`, or a `labels.*` key via regex or GJson, and write it to a label. |
| `composition` | Render a Go `text/template` against the event and write the result to a label. |
| `mapping` | Look up labels from a mapping schema or an external mapping API. |
| `drop` | Remove the listed labels from the alert. |

settings.description: Rule-kind–specific settings. The shape depends on `kind`.

integration_id.description: Integration ID to query enrichment rules for. Must be greater than 0.

EnrichmentItem.description: Enrichment rule set for an integration.

integration_id.description: ID of the integration this rule set belongs to; one integration has at most one rule set.

rules.description: Rules in execution order; each rule sees the labels written by the rules before it.

status.description: Rule set status: `enabled` (active) or `deleted` (soft-deleted). Read endpoints exclude soft-deleted rule sets, so responses always carry `enabled`.

updated_by.description: Last updater member ID.

creator_id.description: Creator member ID.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp, Unix seconds.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp, Unix seconds.

deleted_at.description: Deletion time, Unix seconds. Omitted when the rule set is not deleted; read endpoints never return soft-deleted rule sets, so this is effectively always omitted.

integration_ids.description: List of integration IDs to query. Must contain at least one ID.

items.description: Enrichment rule sets.

integration_id.description: Integration ID to configure enrichment rules for.

rules.description: Ordered rule list that replaces the integration's whole rule set; send `[]` to remove all rules. Rules run in this order.

EnvironmentBinding.description: The runner or cloud sandbox the session is bound to. Returned by `POST /safari/session/get` only; omitted until the session has been bound (after its first message).

kind.description: Environment kind bound to the session: `cloud` (managed sandbox) or `byoc` (self-hosted runner).

id.description: Environment identifier: a cloud sandbox ID for `cloud` bindings, a runner/environment ID for `byoc` bindings.

name.description: Human-readable environment name; empty for cloud bindings using the default allowlist.

team_id.description: Team that owns the bound environment; 0 for account-scope environments.

status.description:
Live health of the binding. Omitted when unknown.

For `byoc`:
- `online`: runner connected and ready
- `degraded`: runner connected but its executor is unhealthy; messages are still accepted
- `pending`: runner has never connected
- `offline`: runner heartbeat lost; messages cannot be served
- `deleted`: the environment no longer exists; choose another

For `cloud`:
- `available`: the sandbox can serve the next message (paused or starting sandboxes resume automatically)
- `rebuilding`: the sandbox is being resumed or recreated
- `expired`: the sandbox failed permanently and cannot recover by itself
- `deleted`: the selected cloud environment template was deleted

ErrorCode.description:
Error code. Every failed response sets `error.code` to one of these stable strings; branch on it rather than on the HTTP status.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `OK` | 200 | Reserved; never returned on a failed request. |
| `InvalidParameter` | 400 | A parameter is missing, has the wrong type, or failed validation; `message` usually names the field. |
| `BadRequest` | 400 | The request breaks a business rule or conflicts with the current state of an object; `message` says which. |
| `InvalidContentType` | 400 | The body is not sent as `application/json`. |

ErrorResponse.description: Response envelope for errors. `error` is required; `data` is absent.

request_id.description: Unique trace ID of this request; include it when reporting issues so logs can be located.

result_label.description: Destination label key the composed value is written to. Must match `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`.

template.description: Go `text/template` string (1–500 characters) rendered against the event struct — e.g. `{{.Title}}`, `{{.Description}}`, `{{.Labels.key}}`. Example: `{{.Labels.region}}-{{.Labels.env}}`.

override.description: When `false` (default) the rule is skipped if `result_label` already exists on the event; when `true` the existing value is overwritten.

drop_labels.description: Label names to remove from the event (at least one), given without the `labels.` prefix.

source_field.description: Source field to extract from. Must be `title`, `description`, or a label key prefixed with `labels.` (e.g. `labels.env`).

result_label.description: Destination label key the extracted value is written to. Must match `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`.

pattern.description: Regular expression (RE2) applied to the source value; may be wrapped in `/.../`. All capture groups are joined with a space and written to `result_label`. Nothing is written when the expression does not match, has no capture group, or the first group is empty. Exactly one of `pattern` and `g_json` must be set.

g_json.description: GJSON path (a leading `$.` is ignored) used when the source value is a JSON string, e.g. `host.name`. If the source value is not valid JSON the rule is skipped; if the path does not exist an empty string is written. Exactly one of `pattern` and `g_json` must be set.

override.description: When `false` (default) the rule is skipped if `result_label` already exists on the event; when `true` the existing value is overwritten.

result_labels.description: Label keys to fill from the lookup result (at least one). For `schema` they are normally the schema's `result_labels`; for `api` they are sent to the API as `result_label_keys`.

mapping_type.description:
Lookup source.
- `schema` (default): look up a row in the mapping schema `schema_id` using the event's values of the schema's `source_labels`; the rule does nothing if any source label is missing or no row matches.
- `api`: call the mapping API `api_id` with the event; runs for alert events only.

schema_id.description: Mapping schema ID (MongoDB ObjectID hex). Required when `mapping_type` is `schema`.

api_id.description: Mapping API ID (MongoDB ObjectID hex). Required when `mapping_type` is `api`.

override.description: When `false` (default) the rule is skipped if every label in `result_labels` already exists, and otherwise only the missing labels are filled. When `true` all `result_labels` are overwritten with the lookup result.

max_times.description: Total notifications sent in this level, including the first, 0–6; `0` and `1` both notify once.

notify_step.description: Minutes between repeat notifications in this level, 0.5–120, kept to one decimal place. Used only when `max_times` is greater than 1.

escalate_window.description: Minutes to wait after this level's first notification before escalating to the next level, 0–720. Ignored on the last level.

force_escalate.description: When true, escalate even after the incident has been acknowledged (`Processing`). When false, escalation stops once the incident is acknowledged. Closed or snoozed incidents never escalate.

account_id.description: Owning account ID.

channel_id.description: Channel the rule belongs to.

priority.description: Evaluation order from `0` to `200`: lower values are evaluated first, ties broken by creation time. The first enabled rule whose time windows and filters match a new incident takes it.

aggr_window.description: Delay in seconds, 0–3600, before the first notification for a newly assigned incident is sent; `0` notifies immediately.

time_filters.description: Recurring time windows during which the rule can match; empty means at any time.

filters.description: Incident conditions (OR of AND groups), matched against the incident the alert was grouped into. Empty means the rule matches every incident in the channel.

status.description: Rule status: `enabled` means active, `disabled` means paused, `deleted` is soft-deleted (possible only from the detail endpoint; lists never return deleted rules).

template_id.description: Notification template ID (24-character hex); see `POST /template/list`.

rule_id.description: Escalation rule ID (MongoDB ObjectID).

updated_by.description: Member ID that last updated the rule.

deleted_at.description: Deletion time, Unix timestamp in seconds. Omitted unless the rule is soft-deleted; deleted rules are excluded from list responses.

created_at.description: Creation time, Unix timestamp in seconds.

updated_at.description: Last update time, Unix timestamp in seconds.

EscalateTarget.description: Notification target. At least one of `person_ids`, `team_ids`, `schedule_to_role_ids`, or `emails` must be set, together with either `by` or `webhooks`.

person_ids.description: Member IDs to notify directly; obtain them from `POST /member/list`. Every ID must exist.

team_ids.description: Team IDs whose members are notified; obtain them from `POST /team/list`. Each team must have at least one member.

schedule_to_role_ids.description: Notify whoever is on call: keys are schedule IDs (from `POST /schedule/list`) written as strings, values are the role IDs on that schedule. Each value must be non-empty.

emails.description: Email addresses of account members; each address is resolved to the member who owns it when the level fires.

by.description: Personal notification channels for the people in this target, per incident severity. Required unless `webhooks` is set; returned as `null` when not set.

follow_preference.description: When true, each person is notified through the channels in their own notification preferences for the incident's severity, and `critical`, `warning` and `info` are ignored.

critical.description: Channels used when the incident severity is `Critical`: `sms`, `voice`, `email`, `push`, or a direct message through an IM app integration written as `<app>:<integration_id>`, where `<app>` is `feishu_app`, `dingtalk_app`, `wecom_app`, `slack_app` or `teams_app` and `<integration_id>` is the ID of that IM integration. Other values return `InvalidParameter`.

warning.description: Channels used when the incident severity is `Warning`; same values as `critical`.

info.description: Channels used when the incident severity is `Info`; same values as `critical`.

webhooks.description: Group chats to notify through robots or IM apps. Required unless `by` is set; returned as `null` when not set.

type.description:
Delivery type:
- `feishu`, `dingtalk`, `wecom`, `slack`, `telegram`, `zoom`: a group robot (incoming webhook) of that IM.
- `feishu_app`, `dingtalk_app`, `slack_app`, `teams_app`: group chats reached through the corresponding IM app integration.

settings.description: Type-specific settings, such as the robot's webhook token or the app's chat IDs; `feishu_app` and `dingtalk_app` require it. To see the exact shape for a type, configure one in the console and read it back with `POST /channel/escalate/rule/info`.

EventGroup.description: Alert event merge configuration. When enabled, repeated incoming events of the same alert are merged into the existing alert within the time window instead of creating new alerts.

is_enabled.description: When true, repeated events of the same alert merge into the existing alert; when false, every event creates a separate alert. If you send `event_group`, set this explicitly: an omitted value means `false`. When the whole `event_group` is omitted on create, merging is enabled.

time_window.description: Merge window in minutes, required when `is_enabled` is true. The range is 1–1440 by default; accounts with the extended merge window enabled can set up to 10080 (7 days). Ignored when merging is disabled.

EventItem.description: One persisted session event. content/actions/usage_metadata carry the raw ADK envelope; treat them as opaque structured payloads.

invocation_id.description: ID of the invocation (one agent turn) that wrote this event. Omitted when empty.

root_invocation_id.description: Invocation ID of the top-level user turn this event belongs to, linking events written by nested subagent invocations back to it. Omitted when empty.

delivery_mode.description: Delivery mode negotiated for the IM request that produced this event. `reply_only`: the IM client shows only explicit replies, not the agent's final text. Omitted for normal delivery.

is_error.description: True when this is an assistant event recording a runtime failure whose message is safe to show to users. Omitted when false.

author.description: Event author (e.g. user, the agent name).

person_id.description: Member ID of the person who sent this user message. Omitted on assistant and tool events and when no member is recorded (automation runs, some IM turns).

branch.description: ADK branch path for nested agents.

actions.description: ADK actions envelope (state deltas, transfers, escalation).

partial.description: True for a streaming partial chunk.

turn_complete.description: True on the terminal event of a turn.

error_code.description: Error code when the event represents a failure.

status.description: Event status. One of: `normal` (a live event included in the context fed to the model), `compressed` (folded into a compaction summary boundary event; no longer loaded for the model, kept as history only).

created_at.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the event was written.

ExploreField.description: One column of a frame. Values are columnar and may contain nulls.

name.description: Column name, at most 1 MiB of UTF-8.

type.description: Column type. `string` is rejected inside a `time_series` frame; `float` holds numbers and `time` holds UTC RFC3339Nano strings.

labels.description: Label set of this column. Only `time_series` value fields may carry labels; a `table` field must not.

items.description: One cell. `time` cells are UTC RFC3339Nano strings; `float` cells may be the strings `NaN`, `+Inf`, and `-Inf`; any cell may be null except a time value inside a `time_series` frame.

ExploreFrame.description: One columnar frame. Every field in the frame has the same number of values.

kind.description: Frame shape. `table` is an unlabeled table. `time_series` carries exactly one time field and one float field; its time values are strictly increasing and never null.

fields.description: Log fields as raw JSON values. Integer literals outside JavaScript's safe integer range are returned as decimal strings.

timestamp_ns.description: Entry time as a canonical unsigned decimal string of Unix epoch nanoseconds, at most 20 digits.

ExploreResponseExecution.description: Execution actually used, present when the data source returned a stepped result.

effective_step_seconds.description: Step, in seconds, the query was executed with after applying `max_data_points` and `min_step_seconds`.

kind.description: Execution kind; always `range` when this object is present.

ExploreResult.description: Result body. Exactly one of `frames`, `samples`, or `entries` is present and matches `kind`.

kind.description: Result shape. `frames` returns columnar tables or time series, `samples` returns instant values with labels, and `logs` returns log entries.

frames.description: Columnar frames. Present when `kind` is `frames`; at most 1,000 frames, 1,000 table rows in total, and 100,000 values in total.

samples.description: Instant samples. Present when `kind` is `samples`; at most 1,000 samples.

entries.description: Log entries. Present when `kind` is `logs`; never longer than `applied_limit`.

applied_limit.description: Entry limit applied to a logs result: 1 to 1000 (1 to 100 for `sls` data sources). Present only when `kind` is `logs`.

has_more.description: Whether a logs result was truncated by `applied_limit`.

labels.description: Label set of the sample. May be empty but never null.

value.description: Sample value: a number, or one of the strings `NaN`, `+Inf`, and `-Inf`. Never null.

PrometheusLabelValuesResponse.description: Native Prometheus HTTP API response returned by the queried data source. This endpoint does not wrap the payload in the Flashduty response envelope.

data.description: Label values, present when `status` is `success`.

items.description: One label value.

error.description: Human-readable Prometheus error message, present when `status` is `error`.

errorType.description: Prometheus error class, present when `status` is `error`.

status.description: Prometheus result status. `success` carries `data`; `error` carries `errorType` and `error`.

QueryExploreExecution.description: Time semantics of the query. The accepted companion fields depend on `kind`: `instant` takes `to_ms` (and optionally `from_ms`), `range` requires `from_ms`, `to_ms`, and `max_data_points`, and `window` takes only `from_ms` and `to_ms`. When both times are present, `from_ms` must be less than `to_ms`. `step_seconds` is never accepted over HTTP.

kind.description:
Execution kind.

- `instant`: evaluate at a single point in time.
- `range`: evaluate a series over `from_ms` to `to_ms`, with a step derived from `max_data_points` and `min_step_seconds`.
- `window`: query the interval from `from_ms` to `to_ms` with no step.

from_ms.description: Start of the interval as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds; non-negative and less than `to_ms`. Required for `range` and `window`; optional for `instant`.

to_ms.description: End of the interval (or the evaluation time for `instant`) as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds; non-negative. Required for every execution kind.

max_data_points.description: Maximum number of points to return. Required for `range` and rejected for `instant` and `window`.

min_step_seconds.description: Lower bound, in seconds, for the step derived from `max_data_points`. Optional and only accepted for `range`.

QueryExploreRequest.description: Explore query request. All four top-level fields are required and unknown fields are rejected.

datasource_id.description: Data source ID from `/monit/datasource/list`. Must be a positive JavaScript-safe integer for an enabled data source of the authenticated account that the caller may query.

expr.description: Query expression in the data source's native language (PromQL, LogsQL, SQL, and so on). Non-empty UTF-8 of at most 64 KiB; `mysql` allows at most 16 KiB and `tencent_cls` at most 12 KiB.

args.description: Macro substitutions keyed by variable name, used for Grafana-style variables. Keys are at most 256 bytes, values at most 64 KiB, with a 128 KiB total budget.

ExportStatusPageSubscribersRequest.description: Parameters for exporting a status page subscriber list.

component_ids.description: Optional component IDs to filter subscribers by.

page_id.description: Status page ID; obtain it from `GET /status-page/list`.

ExportedStatusPageSubscriberItem.description: A status page subscriber, as returned by the subscriber list and export endpoints.

recipient.description: Subscriber recipient: email address for public pages, user ID for internal pages.

method.description: Subscription notification method. `email` is email subscription (public pages); `im` is IM subscription (internal pages). Determined by the page type.

components.description: Components the subscriber follows; each item carries only `component_id` and `name`. Empty when `all` is `true`.

all.description: Whether the subscriber is subscribed to all components.

locale.description: Preferred locale for notifications. Omitted when empty.

FacetCountItem.description: A facet value and its occurrence count.

count.description: Number of events with this facet value in the time range.

facet_value.description: The facet value. Type matches the field's `value_type`.

comment.description: Comment recorded with the merge. Omitted when empty.

owner_id.description: New owner member ID set on the target incident. Omitted when unchanged.

source_alerts.description: Source alerts merged into the target incident. Omitted when empty.

target_incident.description: Incident the alerts were merged into. Omitted when not recorded.

title.description: New title set on the target incident. Omitted when unchanged.

mute_secs.description: Mute duration in seconds. Omitted when zero.

rule_id.description: Inhibit rule ID that muted the alert. Omitted when empty.

rule_name.description: Inhibit rule name, resolved at read time. Omitted when empty.

source_alert_id.description: ID of the source alert that triggered the inhibition. Omitted when empty.

source_alert_title.description: Title of the source alert, resolved at read time. Omitted when empty.

progress.description: `Processing` when this acknowledgement moved the incident from `Triggered` to `Processing`; omitted when the incident was already `Processing`.

comment.description: Form summary recorded as a timeline comment. Omitted when no acknowledgement form summary was submitted.

images.description: Images from the acknowledgement form, recorded on the timeline entry only. Omitted when none were submitted.

to.description: Member IDs that received the assignment.

FeedDetailIncidentAssign.description: Detail payload for `i_assign`. Extends `AssignedTo` with the set of target member IDs.
FeedDetailIncidentAssign.title: i_assign

mute_reply.description: Whether replies to this comment are muted.

comment_type_id.description: ObjectID of the account-level comment type attached to the comment.

comment_type.description: Name and color of the attached comment type, resolved at read time; omitted when no comment type is attached or it no longer exists.

integration_id.description: Integration ID that executed the action.

source_incidents.description: Incidents merged into the target; present on the target incident's entry.

target_incident.description: Incident this incident was merged into; present on each source incident's entry.

owner_id.description: Not set by incident merges, which never change the owner; present only on older entries.

title.description: New title the merge set on the target incident; present only on the target's entry and only when the title changed.

remove_source_incidents.description: `true` when the source incidents were permanently deleted after the merge.

source_responders.description: Member IDs that were responders on the source incidents, for reference; they are not added to the target's responders.

max_changes.description: Maximum state changes allowed within the window.

mute_mins.description: Mute duration in minutes once flapping is detected.

severity.description: Severity of the incident when it was created.

reporter_email.description: Email of the reporter when the incident was created externally.

fire_type.description: Whether this is the first fire or a refire. `fire`: the first notification for this escalation layer; `refire`: a repeat notification to the same layer when the incident remains unhandled, sent at the layer's notify interval and capped by the layer's maximum refire count.

msg_id.description: Upstream message ID returned by the delivery channel.

reason.description: Free-text reason passed as `reason` to `POST /incident/reopen`; omitted when none was given.

field_name.description: Name of the custom field that was updated.

to.description: New value of the custom field. Type depends on the field definition.

comment.description: Form summary recorded as a timeline comment on resolution. Omitted when no resolve form summary was submitted.

from.description:
Source that triggered the resolve.

| `voice` | Phone-call (voice DTMF) action. |
| `console` | Console (Web UI) action. |
| `card` | IM notification card button (DingTalk/Feishu/Slack/Teams). |

| `autorefresh` | Card auto-refresh (reserved; never appears on resolve feeds). |
| `escalation` | Escalation flow (reserved; never appears on resolve feeds). |

images.description: Images from the resolve form, recorded on the timeline entry only. Omitted when none were submitted.

progress.description: `Triggered` when removing this acknowledgement returned the incident to `Triggered` (no responder still acknowledged); omitted otherwise.

snoozedBefore.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) at which the cancelled snooze would have ended.

plugin_type.description: Plugin type of the IM integration: `feishu_app` (Feishu), `dingtalk_app` (DingTalk), `wecom_app` (WeCom), or `slack_app` (Slack).

share_link.description: Shareable join link for the war room.
