item_type.description: Work item type. `action`: an action item anchored to the incident itself; `follow_up`: an improvement item anchored to a post-mortem.

from_status.description: Status before the update; present only when the status changed. Usually one of `open`, `in_progress`, `done`, `cancelled`; items created before these statuses existed may carry other text.

to_status.description: Status after the update; present only when the status changed. `open` not started; `in_progress` being worked on; `done` completed; `cancelled` no longer needed.

from_priority.description: Priority before the update. Free-text priority label defined by the client (up to 64 characters); present only when the priority changed.

to_priority.description: Priority after the update. Free-text priority label defined by the client (up to 64 characters); present only when the priority changed.

FeedDetailWorkItemUpdated.title: i_wi_updated

FeedItem.description: A single alert activity feed entry. The `detail` field is discriminated by `type`; see the per-type `FeedDetailAlert*` schemas.

ref_id.description: ObjectID of the alert this entry references.

detail.description: Type-specific payload; the concrete shape is determined by `type`. May be `null` for entries stored without detail.

account_id.description: ID of the account that owns the alert.

creator_id.description: Member ID of the creator. 0 for system-generated entries.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp in Unix epoch milliseconds.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp in Unix epoch milliseconds.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete time, Unix epoch milliseconds. Omitted when not deleted.

via.description: Surface that wrote the entry on a user's behalf; currently only `ai_sre`. Omitted when a user created the entry directly.

agent_session_id.description: AI SRE session that produced the entry. Omitted when no agent wrote it.

FieldDeleteReference.description: Custom form that still references the field.

kind.description: Referenced resource kind. Always `custom_form` for this response.

name.description: Human label of the referencing custom form's type (a Chinese label, e.g. `解决故障` for the resolve form).

href.description: Console URL for the referencing custom form.

FieldDeleteReferenceError.description: Error response returned when a custom form still references the field.

data.description: Supplementary error payload; for this error it always contains the `refs` field.

refs.description: Custom forms that still reference the field, each with `kind`/`name`/`href`; all references must be removed before the field can be deleted.

request_id.description: Trace ID of this request, identical to the `Flashcat-Request-Id` response header.

account_id.description: Owning account ID.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp, Unix seconds.

creator_id.description: Creator member ID.

default_value.description: Default value. Type depends on `field_type`: `bool` for checkbox; `string` for single_select/text; `string[]` for multi_select; may be `null` if no default.

deleted_at.description: Deletion timestamp, Unix seconds. Only present for soft-deleted fields.

display_name.description: Human-readable name shown in the UI.

field_name.description: Machine name used in incident payloads under `fields.<field_name>`. Immutable.

field_type.description:
Field type.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `checkbox` | Checkbox; value is a bool, options are not supported. |
| `multi_select` | Multi-select; value is a string array, each element must be one of options. |
| `single_select` | Single-select; value is a string from options. |
| `text` | Free text; value is a string. |

options.description: Allowed choices for `single_select`/`multi_select` (non-empty unique string array). `null` or empty for `checkbox`/`text`.

status.description: Field status: `enabled` (active), `disabled` (set only via internal helpers, not via the API), or `deleted` (soft-deleted). `/field/list` excludes `deleted`; `/field/info` may return it.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp, Unix seconds.

updated_by.description: Last updater member ID.

value_type.description: Value type. `checkbox` is always `bool`; `single_select`/`multi_select`/`text` are always `string`. `float` is reserved and never occurs today.

asc.description: Sort ascending when `true`; descending otherwise.

creator_id.description: Filter by creator member ID. Omit or send `null` to skip.

orderby.description: Sort key. Defaults to `created_at` when omitted.

query.description: Regex filter matched against `field_name` only. An invalid regex is auto-escaped to a literal substring match.

items.description: All non-deleted custom fields for the account. No pagination.

key.description: Field to match. Which built-in keys are allowed depends on the rule type and is listed on the field that holds the conditions; any `labels.<name>` key (for example `labels.env`) is always accepted. An unknown key returns `InvalidParameter`. When the alert or incident has no value for the key, `IN` does not match and `NOTIN` matches.

oper.description: Match operator, case-sensitive. `IN`: matches when the field value matches any entry in `vals`. `NOTIN`: matches when it matches none of them.

vals.description: Values to compare, at least one. Each entry is matched as: an exact string; a wildcard pattern when it contains `*` or `?` (must match the whole value); a regular expression when wrapped in slashes, such as `/^db-/` (may match anywhere in the value); an IP range written `cidr:<network>`, such as `cidr:203.0.113.0/24`; or a numeric comparison `num:<op>:<number>` with `lt`, `le`, `gt` or `ge`, such as `num:gt:90`.

is_disabled.description: When true, flapping detection is turned off.

max_changes.description: Max state changes allowed within `in_mins`, 2–100. When omitted or `0`, all three values fall back to the defaults: 4 changes, `in_mins` 60, `mute_mins` 120.

mute_mins.description: Mute duration in minutes after flapping is detected.

application_id.description: RUM application ID. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

GetRemoteConfigResponse.description: Live remote configuration and its version.

config.description: The live configuration (the newest published version). `null` when the application has never been configured.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds - when the current version was published. 0 when never configured.

version.description: Version the live configuration is stored under. 0 means the application has never been configured.

observers.description: Suggested observers, in timeline order. Empty array when there are none.

GetWarRoomDetailRequest.description: Parameters for retrieving a war room's live detail.

chat_id.description: Chat ID of the IM group hosting the war room; obtain it from `POST /incident/war-room/list`.

integration_id.description: IM integration ID that hosts the war room.

GetWebhookHistoryDetailRequest.description: Lookup parameters for a single webhook delivery record.

event_id.description: `event_id` of a record returned by `POST /webhook/history/list`. It starts with the delivery date (`YYYYMMDD`); an ID without that prefix fails the request.

integration_id.description: Integration ID the event belongs to; available in the items returned by `POST /webhook/history/list`.

method.description:
Grouping method:
- `n`: no grouping; every new alert opens its own incident.
- `p`: rule-based grouping by the keys in `equals` and `cases`; requires the Standard license or higher.
- `i`: intelligent grouping by content similarity (see `i_keys`, `i_score_threshold`); requires the Pro license.

equals.description: Key sets for rule-based (`p`) grouping, up to 5 sets. A new alert joins an active incident when every key of any one set has the same value on both. Keys: `title`, `description`, `severity`, or `labels.<name>`; each set must be non-empty. With `p`, at least one of `equals` or `cases` is required.

items.description: Conditional grouping override: stored alerts matching `if` are grouped by `equals` instead of the top-level grouping keys.

if.description: AND-ed match conditions evaluated against stored alert fields.

equals.description: Grouping keys for matching alerts. Supported values: `title`, `description`, `severity`, or any `labels.<name>`.

all_equals_required.description: When true, a key set matches only if every key in it is present on the alert. When false, missing keys compare as empty, but at least one key of the set must be present.

time_window.description: Grouping time window in minutes. Default max is 1440 minutes (24 h); extended accounts may allow up to 43200 minutes (30 days).

window_type.description: Window type, default `tumbling`. `tumbling` is a fixed window counted from incident creation — once it expires, new alerts open a new incident; `sliding` is a sliding window counted from the incident's most recent alert, extended each time a new alert merges in.

storm_threshold.description: Legacy single storm threshold; used only when `storm_thresholds` is empty and the value is greater than 1. `0` disables it.

storm_thresholds.description: Alert counts at which an incident storm event fires: when the number of alerts merged into one incident reaches a threshold, a storm notification is sent. Up to 5 values, each at least 2; duplicates are removed and values are sorted.

i_keys.description: Fields used by intelligent (`i`) grouping, up to 10: `title`, `description`, `severity`, or `labels.<name>`. Empty uses `title`, `description`, `labels.service` and `labels.resource`.

i_score_threshold.description: Minimum similarity, 0.5–1, for intelligent grouping to merge an alert into an existing incident. Omitted or `0` uses 0.9.

IDRequest.description: Request with a single numeric ID.

id.description: Numeric ID of the target resource; the exact meaning depends on the API being called (e.g. datasource ID, ruleset ID).

src.description: Image source. Either an `img_` upload token or an `http(s)` URL.

href.description: Optional link the image points to.

alt.description: Alternative text shown when the image cannot be displayed; empty when not set.

recipient.description: Email address (for public pages) or user ID (for internal pages).

component_ids.description: Component IDs the subscriber should receive notifications for.

change_ids.description: Specific event IDs the subscriber should receive notifications for.

all.description: When `true`, the subscriber receives notifications for all components and events, and `component_ids`/`change_ids` are ignored. Must be `true` when both lists are empty.

locale.description: Preferred locale for notifications. Defaults to the request locale when omitted.

ImportStatusPageSubscribersRequest.description: Parameters for bulk-importing subscribers. Each subscriber must have a non-empty `recipient` (≤255 chars) and subscribe to at least one component, change, or set `all: true`.

page_id.description: Target status page ID; obtain it from `GET /status-page/list`.

method.description: Subscription method. `email` is only valid for public pages; `im` is only valid for internal pages.

subscribers.description: Subscribers to import. Each recipient's existing subscriptions on this page are replaced; an empty or omitted list does nothing.

Triggered.description: Incidents started in the last 30 days that are still `Triggered` (not yet acknowledged).

Processing.description: Incidents started in the last 30 days that are `Processing` (acknowledged, not yet closed).

IncidentActionImage.description: Image attached to an acknowledgement or resolution timeline entry.

href.description: Optional link that the image points to.

src.description: Image source. Accepts an `img_` upload token, an `http(s)` URL, or an object-storage key beginning with `/`.

IncidentCardHiddenFields.description: Incident-card fields to hide, keyed by IM app type. Only supported IM app types and field names are accepted.

additionalProperties.description: Fields to hide on this app's incident cards: `channel` (channel name), `snoozed_before` (snooze end time), `severity`, `responders`, `aggregate_alert_count` (number of merged alerts), `detail` (Detail button), `ai_analysis` (AI Analysis button).

IncidentCommentTypeDisplay.description: Resolved display of an account-level comment type, populated at read time from the current type definition.

id.description: Comment type ID (MongoDB ObjectID).

name.description: Display name of the comment type.

IncidentCommentTypeItem.description: An account-level comment type that can be attached to incident comments.

account_id.description: Account ID that owns the comment type.

color.description: Label color as a hex value in #RRGGBB format (stored uppercase).

created_at.description: Creation time as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

creator_id.description: ID of the user who created the comment type.

name.description: Display name of the comment type. Unique within the account (case-insensitive, trimmed).

position.description: 1-based display position of the comment type.

updated_at.description: Last update time as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

updated_by.description: ID of the user who last updated the comment type.

IncidentFeedItem.description: Single incident timeline entry. The `detail` field is discriminated by `type`; see the per-type `FeedDetail*` schemas.

ref_id.description: ID of the incident the entry belongs to; equals the requested `incident_id`.

detail.description: Type-specific payload. The concrete shape is determined by `type`; `null` when the entry has no structured detail.

count.description: Number of action items converted to follow-ups.

work_item_ids.description: IDs of the converted work items.

titles.description: Titles of the converted work items, in the same order as `work_item_ids`.

post_mortem_id.description: ID of the post-mortem the follow-ups are bound to; empty when the incident has no post-mortem.

account_id.description: ID of the account that owns this record; the same for every record returned to one `app_key`.

creator_id.description: User ID of the actor. `0` means system-generated.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp in milliseconds. Zero if not deleted.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp in milliseconds.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp in milliseconds.

via.description: `ai_sre` when AI SRE performed the action on behalf of `creator_id`; omitted for direct actions.

agent_session_id.description: ID of the AI SRE session that performed the action; present only when `via` is `ai_sre` and a session was recorded.

IncidentFeedType.description:
Incident timeline entry type. Each value identifies one lifecycle event; the matching `detail` payload shape is determined by this field. Incident types are prefixed with `i_`.

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `i_new` | Incident Created: A new incident was created automatically or manually. |
| `i_assign` | Assigned: Incident was assigned to responders. |
| `i_a_rspd` | Responder Added: Additional responders joined the incident. |
| `i_notify` | Notification dispatched through a channel at a specific escalation level. |
| `i_storm` | Alert storm threshold reached on the incident. |
| `i_snooze` | Notifications snoozed for a given duration. |
| `i_wake` | Snooze cancelled and notifications resumed. |
| `i_ack` | Acknowledged: Responder confirmed they are working on the incident. |
| `i_unack` | Acknowledgement removed. |
| `i_comm` | Comment: Responder logged progress or key information. |
| `i_rslv` | Resolved: Incident was marked as resolved. |
| `i_reopen` | Reopened: Resolved incident was reopened, possibly due to recurrence. |
| `i_merge` | Merged: Multiple related incidents were merged into one. |
| `i_r_title` | Title updated. |
| `i_r_desc` | Description updated. |
| `i_r_impact` | Impact updated. |
| `i_r_rc` | Root cause updated. |
| `i_r_rsltn` | Resolution updated. |
| `i_r_severity` | Severity Changed: Incident severity level was adjusted. |
| `i_r_field` | Custom field value updated. |
| `i_m_flapping` | Incident muted by flapping detection. |
| `i_m_reply` | Mute reply marker on a comment. |
| `i_custom` | Action: Automated action or script was triggered. |
| `i_wr_create` | War Room Created: Chat group was created for collaborative response. |
| `i_wr_delete` | War room chat group deleted. |
| `i_auto_refresh` | Card auto-refresh event posted back to the timeline. |
| `i_wi_created` | Work Item Created: An Action or Follow-up was created. |
| `i_wi_updated` | Work Item Updated: Title, description, status, or priority was changed. |
| `i_wi_assignees` | Work Item Assignees Changed: Assignees were updated. |
| `i_wi_completed` | Work Item Completed: An assignee marked the work item complete. |
| `i_wi_converted` | Work Item Converted: An Action was converted to a Follow-up. |
| `i_wi_bound` | Work Item Bound: A converted Follow-up was bound to a post-mortem. |
| `i_wi_deleted` | Work Item Deleted: An Action or Follow-up was soft-deleted. |
| `i_wi_auto_converted` | Work Items Auto-converted: Closing the incident converted its unfinished action items to follow-ups. |
| `a_merge` | Alert Merged: An alert was merged into an existing incident. |

account_id.description: Account ID that owns the incident.

channel_id.description: Channel ID. 0 for standalone incidents.

team_id.description: ID of the team that owns the incident's channel. 0 when the channel has no team.

integration_id.description: First integration associated with the incident.

integration_ids.description: IDs of all integrations contributing alerts to this incident; `null` for incidents without integrations, such as manually created ones.

integration_types.description: Plugin types of all contributing integrations (see `integration_type`); `null` when there are none.

dedup_key.description: Deduplication key used to coalesce alerts.

equals_md5.description: MD5 hash used for content-equality checks.

start_time.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the incident started.

end_time.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the incident ended. 0 if still active.

last_time.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of the most recent update.

ack_time.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the incident was first acknowledged. 0 if unacknowledged.

close_time.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the incident was closed. 0 if still open.

creator_id.description: Member ID that created the incident. 0 if auto-created by the system.

closer_id.description: Member ID that closed the incident. 0 if auto-closed.

owner_id.description: Primary owner member ID. 0 if none.

incident_status.description: Current incident status, derived from alert statuses.

progress.description: Incident progress. `Triggered` means fired and unacknowledged; `Processing` means acknowledged and being handled (un-acknowledging moves it back to `Triggered`); `Closed` means resolved.

num.description: Short display identifier; not guaranteed unique.

frequency.description: Frequency bucket for recurrence analysis: `frequent` or `rare`.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp (seconds). Zero if not deleted.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp (seconds).

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp (seconds).

snoozed_before.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) until which notifications are snoozed. 0 if not snoozed.

group_method.description: Alert grouping method: `i` intelligent, `p` pattern, `n` none.

ever_muted.description: Whether the incident has ever been silenced.

has_unfinished_work_item.description: `true` when the incident still has at least one action item or follow-up that is neither `done` nor `cancelled`.

labels.description: Labels propagated from alerts.

fields.description: Custom field values keyed by field name.

assigned_to.description: Current assignment target. Always present; for an incident that was never assigned, `type` and `id` are empty and `assigned_at` is `0`.

reporter_email.description: Reporter email for manually created incidents.

alert_cnt.description: Total count of alerts merged into this incident.

active_alert_cnt.description: Count of alerts currently in Critical/Warning/Info state.

alert_event_cnt.description: Total raw alert event count across all merged alerts.

alerts.description: Not returned by the incident endpoints; present only in notification template and custom action payloads.

owner.description: Owner member info. May be deprecated.

account_name.description: Always an empty string in API responses; filled only when the incident is rendered for notifications.

account_locale.description: Always an empty string in API responses; filled only when the incident is rendered for notifications.

account_time_zone.description: Always an empty string in API responses; filled only when the incident is rendered for notifications.

channel_status.description: Status of the channel: `enabled`, `disabled`, or `deleted`. Empty string when the record has no channel or the channel no longer exists.

detail_url.description: Web console URL for the incident.

links.description: Channel-level link integrations rendered for this incident.

integration_type.description: Plugin type of the incident's first integration (see `integration_types` for all). Open set, for example `prometheus.alert` or `monit.alert`; `POST /integration/type/list` returns the full list. Omitted when the incident has no integration or the endpoint does not fill it.

post_mortem_id.description: Associated post-mortem ID, if any. One incident can only link to a single post-mortem.

images.description: Images attached to the incident; `null` when there are none. Tokens starting with `img_` are returned as download URLs.

manual_overrides.description: Fields edited manually and therefore no longer overwritten by merged alerts: `title`, `description`, `incident_severity`. `null` when none.

IncidentInfoRequest.description: Lookup parameters for a single incident. Supply either incident_id or num.

num.description: Short incident ID (the 6-character uppercased id shown in the UI). Not unique — resolves to the most recent match. Supply either incident_id or num.

items.description: Incident list for the current page.

total.description: Number of matching incidents, capped at 1,000. For `POST /incident/list-by-ids`, the number of incidents found.

has_next_page.description: Whether another page exists. Reflects the real data with both `p`/`limit` and `search_after_ctx` paging, including past the 1,000 cap of `total`. Always `false` for `POST /incident/list-by-ids`.

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor pointing at the last item of this page; pass it as `search_after_ctx` on the next request to continue past the 1,000-item page limit. Returned for every non-empty page in `p`/`limit` mode, and in cursor mode only when `has_next_page` is `true`. Omitted by `POST /incident/list-by-ids`.

IncidentRawItem.description: Raw incident row returned by the analytics incident list, with per-incident handling metrics attached.

active_alert_cnt.description: Number of alerts still active (not recovered).

alert_cnt.description: Total number of alerts aggregated into the incident.

alert_event_cnt.description: Total number of alert events associated with the incident; each report of an alert counts as one event.

assigned_to.description: Current assignment target for the incident; `null` when the incident has no assignment record.

assigned_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when this assignment was made.

escalate_rule_id.description: Escalation rule ID (MongoDB ObjectID) driving the assignment.

escalate_rule_name.description: Display name of the escalation rule.

id.description: Internal assignment record ID.

layer_idx.description: Current level index within the escalation rule.

person_ids.description: Member IDs assigned directly to this incident.

type.description:
Assignment type.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `assign` | Initial assignment when the incident is created manually. |
| `reassign` | Re-assignment of an existing incident. |
| `escalate` | Assignment triggered by escalation policy advancement. |
| `reopen` | Assignment restarted from the first layer after the incident is reopened. |

channel_id.description: ID of the channel the incident belongs to.

channel_name.description: Name of the channel the incident belongs to.

closed_by.description: How the incident was closed: `auto`, `timeout`, or `manually`. Empty string while the incident is still open.

closer_id.description: Member ID of the person who closed the incident. Omitted when 0 (not closed manually).

closer_name.description: Display name of the person who closed the incident. Omitted when empty.

created_at.description: Incident creation time, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

creator_id.description: Person ID of the incident creator.

creator_name.description: Display name of the incident creator.

engaged_seconds.description: Total engaged time in seconds across acknowledged responders, each contributing close time minus their acknowledgement time; 0 if not closed.

escalations.description: Total escalations, the sum of `timeout_escalations` and `manual_escalations`.

ever_muted.description: Whether the incident was ever muted by noise reduction. Omitted when false.

fields.description: Custom fields of the incident. Always omitted in this response (reserved for export).

frequency.description: Frequency classification: `frequent` or `rare`. Omitted when not classified.

hours.description: Time-of-day bucket of the creation time in the account timezone: `work` = Mon–Fri 08:00–19:00, `sleep` = 23:00–08:00 daily, `off` = all other times.

incident_id.description: Incident ID, unique within the account.

interruptions.description: Number of interruptions: notifications sent via app push, SMS, or voice call; consecutive notifications to the same responder within 60 seconds count as one.

labels.description: Incident labels as key-value pairs. Always omitted in this response (reserved for export).

owner_id.description: Member ID of the incident owner. Omitted when 0 (no owner).

owner_name.description: Display name of the incident owner. Omitted when empty.

responders.description: Responders with per-person assignment and acknowledgement times.

acknowledged_at.description: Acknowledgement time, as a Unix timestamp in seconds; 0 if not acknowledged.

as.description: Responder's identity in an external chat tool (e.g. Slack); only present when backfilled by an external system.

assigned_at.description: Assignment time, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

person_name.description: Responder display name. Omitted when empty.

seconds_to_ack.description: Seconds from incident creation to the first acknowledgement; 0 if never acknowledged.

seconds_to_close.description: Seconds from incident creation to close; 0 if not closed.

snoozed_before.description: Unix timestamp in seconds until which the incident is snoozed. Omitted when the incident is not snoozed.

team_id.description: ID of the team that owns the incident.

team_name.description: Name of the team that owns the incident.

IncidentShort.description: Brief incident reference embedded in an alert.

progress.description: Incident progress: `Triggered` not yet acknowledged; `Processing` acknowledged and being handled; `Closed` resolved.

account_id.description: ID of the account the rule belongs to.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel the rule belongs to.

source_filters.description: Conditions the source alert must match, evaluated against stored active alerts. Supported keys: `status`, `incident_status`, `alert_status`, `severity`, `incident_severity`, `alert_severity`, `title`, `description`, or any `labels.<name>`. Empty makes the rule inert.

target_filters.description: Conditions the incoming target alert event must match to be inhibited; empty means every incoming event is a target. Keys: `title`, `description`, `severity` (alias `alert_severity`, `event_severity`), `status`, `alert_key`, `title_rule`, `integration_id` (alias `data_source_id`), or any `labels.<name>`.

equals.description: Keys whose values must be equal on the source alert and the incoming event. Only `title`, `severity` and `labels.<name>` take effect; with any other key the rule never fires.

is_directly_discard.description: When true, matching alert events are discarded entirely; when false, alerts are still recorded but marked as muted by this rule.

status.description: Rule status: `enabled` or `disabled`; deleted rules never appear in the list.

rule_id.description: Rule ID (MongoDB ObjectID).

updated_by.description: ID of the user who last updated the rule.

created_at.description: Creation time, Unix timestamp in seconds.

updated_at.description: Last update time, Unix timestamp in seconds.

deleted_at.description: Deletion time, Unix timestamp in seconds. Omitted unless the rule is soft-deleted; deleted rules are excluded from list responses.

InitPostMortemRequest.description: Parameters for initializing a post-mortem report from incidents.

incident_ids.description: Incident IDs (MongoDB ObjectIDs) to link to the report, 1–10. All must exist in the account. The same set always maps to the same report.

template_id.description: Template ID from `POST /incident/post-mortem/template/list`, e.g. the built-in `post_mortem_default_tmpl_en-us` or `post_mortem_default_tmpl_zh-cn`, or a custom template ID.

hours.description: Hour bucket when `split_hours` is enabled: `work`, `sleep`, or `off`. Omitted when `split_hours` is false.

label.description: Aggregation key value (check name or resource identifier).

total_alert_cnt.description: Total number of alerts in this label-value bucket.

total_alert_event_cnt.description: Total number of raw alert events in this label-value bucket.

items.description: Top-K statistic rows aggregated by the requested label's values.

InsightFilter.description: Shared filter envelope for insight and export endpoints. Severities accept up to 3 values; team/channel/responder/incident filters accept up to 100 IDs each. The time range cannot exceed one year.

start_time.description: Start time, Unix seconds. Must be greater than 0.

end_time.description: End time, Unix seconds. Must be greater than `start_time`.

team_ids.description: Filter by team IDs. At most 100 entries.

channel_ids.description: Filter by channel IDs. At most 100 entries.

responder_ids.description: Filter by responder member IDs. Used by `/insight/responder` (which responders to return) and the incident list/export (incidents any of them responded to); ignored by the account/team/channel and top-K endpoints. At most 100 entries.

severities.description: Filter by severity: `Critical`, `Warning`, `Info`, or `Ok`. At most 3 entries.

incident_ids.description: Filter by incident IDs (24-character hex). Used only by the incident list and export. At most 100 entries.

query.description: Substring match on the incident title (SQL `LIKE %query%`).

labels.description: Label filters (exact match).

orderby.description: Sort field of the incident list; only `created_at` (incident creation time, the default). Used by `/insight/incident/list` and `/insight/incident/export`.

asc.description: Sort ascending when `true`, descending (default) otherwise. Used by the incident list and export; `/insight/alert/topk-by-label` has its own `asc`.

is_my_team.description: Restrict results to the caller's teams (intersected with `team_ids` when both are set). When that intersection is empty, or the caller belongs to no team, the result is empty.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone (for example `Asia/Shanghai` or `UTC`) used to cut `aggregate_unit` buckets; abbreviations such as `EST` and `Etc/GMT±N` are rejected. Defaults to UTC. `/insight/incident/export` uses it to render times, falling back to the account time zone and then `Asia/Shanghai`.

seconds_to_close_from.description: Lower bound (inclusive) on time-to-close, in seconds.

seconds_to_close_to.description: Upper bound (exclusive) on time-to-close, in seconds. Must be greater than `seconds_to_close_from` when both are set.

seconds_to_ack_from.description: Lower bound (inclusive) on time-to-acknowledge, in seconds.

seconds_to_ack_to.description: Upper bound (exclusive) on time-to-acknowledge, in seconds. Must be greater than `seconds_to_ack_from` when both are set.

export_fields.description: CSV column keys to include in the export, in the given order; unknown or duplicate keys are rejected. The valid key set differs per export endpoint — see each export operation's description. Only used by the export endpoints; at most 50 entries.

description_html_to_text.description: Strip HTML markup from the description column when exporting.

include_ever_muted.description: Include incidents that have ever been muted. By default, they are excluded.

allOf.description: Paged incident list request. Extends InsightFilter with pagination.

limit.description: Page size, max 100, default 20.

p.description: Page number, starting at 1. Used when `search_after_ctx` is not provided; `p * limit` must stay within 10,000 records.

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor token returned by a previous page (the incident ID of its last row). Pass it back to fetch the next page.

total.description: Number of matching incidents. When the request carried `search_after_ctx`, only incidents after the cursor are counted.

has_next_page.description: Whether another page of results is available.

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor token to fetch the next page — the incident ID of the last row on this page. Present only when `has_next_page` is true.

items.description: Incidents on this page; an empty array when none match.

allOf.description: Insight dimension-aggregation request. Extends InsightFilter with aggregation controls.

split_hours.description: When `true`, each bucket is further split into `work`, `sleep` and `off` hours, returned as separate rows with `hours` set.

aggregate_unit.description:
Split the range into time buckets; omit for a single bucket covering the whole range. Requires a range of at least 24 hours, and `day` allows at most 31 days.
- `day`: calendar days in `time_zone` (the first bucket runs from `start_time` to the next midnight).
- `week`: consecutive 7-day buckets starting at `start_time` (not aligned to Monday).
- `month`: calendar months in `time_zone` (the first bucket runs from `start_time` to the 1st of the next month).

label.description: Aggregation dimension. `check` aggregates by the event's `labels.check` label (monitoring check); `resource` aggregates by the `labels.resource` label (monitored resource identifier).

k.description: Number of label values to return, between 1 and 100 (default 20). With `split_hours`, applied per hour bucket.

orderby.description: Sort field. `total_alert_cnt` sorts by alert count; `total_alert_event_cnt` sorts by raw alert event count (default).

asc.description: Sort ascending when `true`, descending otherwise.

InviteMemberItem.description: A member to invite. Identify the invitee by `email` alone, or by `member_name` + `phone` together.

member_name.description: Display name, 2–39 characters. Required when `email` is not provided; derived from the email prefix when omitted.

email.description: Email address, stored in lower case. Required when `phone` is not provided.

phone.description: Phone number. Required when `email` is not provided.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code for `phone` (e.g. "CN"). Validated and normalized to upper case before storage; invalid values are rejected with a 400. Also the parsing hint when `phone` has no "+" prefix (defaults to "CN").

role_ids.description: Role IDs to assign: built-in `2` (Admin), `6` (Responder), `8` (Viewer), or custom role IDs from `POST /role/list`. Defaults to Viewer (`8`) when omitted; an ID that does not exist returns `400`.

locale.description: Locale: `zh-CN` (Simplified Chinese) or `en-US` (English); other values are rejected with a 400. Defaults to the account's locale when omitted.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone name such as `Asia/Shanghai`. Omit it to have the member follow the account's time zone; an invalid name returns `400`.

ref_id.description: External reference ID (for example an employee ID in an HR system), usable later as a lookup key in `POST /member/delete` and `POST /member/info/reset`.

pack_id.description: Knowledge ID; defaults to the caller's account-scope knowledge.

rel_path.description: Path of the file relative to the knowledge root. Same path rules as `POST /safari/knowledge/file/put`.

force.description: Delete even when other knowledge files reference this file; the referrers are then returned as warnings instead of blocking the delete.

expected_version.description: Optimistic-concurrency guard. `0` or omitted: delete unconditionally. A positive value: delete only if the knowledge's current `version` equals it; otherwise nothing is deleted and the call returns HTTP 200 with `status` = `conflict` and the current `version`.

status.description:
Outcome of the delete.
- `ok`: the file was deleted, or did not exist.
- `conflict`: `expected_version` did not match the current knowledge version, so nothing was deleted.

warnings.description: Non-blocking warnings; `still_referenced_by` means `force` deleted a file that other files still reference (`refs` lists them). Omitted when there are no warnings.

version.description: Knowledge `version` after the delete (unchanged if the file did not exist). When the file did not exist and `expected_version` was not sent, this is `0`. On `conflict`, the current version.

message.description: Explanation of the conflict. Present only when `status` is `conflict`.

pack_id.description: Knowledge ID; defaults to the caller's account-scope knowledge.

rel_path.description: Path of the file relative to the knowledge root. If no file exists at this path, the call still succeeds with `file` set to `null` and an empty `content_b64`.

KnowledgeFileGetResponse.description: File metadata, its base64-encoded content, and the current knowledge version.

file.description: Metadata of the file; `null` when no file exists at `rel_path`.

content_b64.description: Base64-encoded file content. Empty string when the file does not exist (or is empty).

version.description: Current `version` of the knowledge. Pass it as `expected_version` to `POST /safari/knowledge/file/put` or `POST /safari/knowledge/file/delete` to reject the write if someone else changed the knowledge in between.

KnowledgeFileItem.description: Metadata of one knowledge file. Content is fetched separately via file/get.

pack_id.description: ID of the knowledge that contains the file.

rel_path.description: Path relative to the knowledge root, using `/` separators, e.g. `runbooks/restart.md`. Unique within the knowledge.

content_type.description: MIME type stored with the file. Open set: when `content_type` is omitted on write it is derived from the extension of `rel_path` — `.md` → `text/markdown`, `.yaml`/`.yml` → `text/yaml`, `.json` → `application/json`, `.sh` → `text/x-sh`, anything else → `text/plain`; a value passed explicitly is stored as given.

checksum.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the file content.

updated_by.description: Person ID of the member who last modified the file.

updated_at_ms.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the file was last modified.

limit.description: Page size. Accepted but currently ignored — the response always contains the full file list.

p.description: Page number, 1-based. Accepted but currently ignored — the response always contains the full file list.

pack_id.description: Knowledge ID; defaults to the caller's account-scope knowledge.

KnowledgeFileListResponse.description: All files in the knowledge plus the current knowledge version.

files.description: Array of files in the specified knowledge; empty array when it has no files.

total.description: Number of files in `files` — always the full file count of the knowledge, since this endpoint does not paginate.

version.description: Current `version` of the knowledge; usable as `expected_version` for file writes.

KnowledgeFilePutRequest.description: File to create or overwrite. The body is base64 text in `content_b64`, not a multipart upload.

pack_id.description: Knowledge ID; defaults to the caller's account-scope knowledge.

rel_path.description: Destination path relative to the knowledge root; an existing file at this path is overwritten. Must use `/` separators, must not start with `/`, must already be in normalized form, and no segment may be empty, `.`, `..`, or start with `.` (dotfiles are rejected).

content_b64.description: Base64-encoded (standard alphabet) file content. The decoded bytes must be UTF-8 text with no NUL bytes and at most 1 MiB (`DUTY.md`: at most 32 KiB). Omit or send an empty string to write an empty file.

content_type.description: MIME type to store with the file. Optional: when omitted it is derived from the extension of `rel_path` (`.md` → `text/markdown`, `.yaml`/`.yml` → `text/yaml`, `.json` → `application/json`, `.sh` → `text/x-sh`, otherwise `text/plain`). Any value passed is stored as given.

expected_version.description: Optimistic-concurrency guard. `0` or omitted: write unconditionally. A positive value: write only if the knowledge's current `version` equals it; otherwise nothing is written and the call returns HTTP 200 with `status` = `conflict` and the current `version`.

KnowledgeFilePutResponse.description: Write result. On success carries the written file; on a version conflict carries only `status`, `version` and `message`.

status.description:
Outcome of the write.
- `ok`: the change was committed.
- `conflict`: `expected_version` did not match the current knowledge version, so nothing was changed; re-read the file and retry with the returned `version`.

file.description: The file as stored after the write. Omitted when `status` is `conflict`.

warnings.description: Non-blocking warnings; `unresolved_reference` means an @ref in the written content points to a path that does not exist in the knowledge. Omitted when there are no warnings.

version.description: Knowledge `version` produced by this write when `status` is `ok`; the current version when `status` is `conflict`. Use it as `expected_version` for the next write.

message.description: Explanation of the conflict (`this knowledge was updated by someone else`). Present only when `status` is `conflict`.

KnowledgeGetRequest.description: No request fields — the account-scope knowledge is always targeted.

KnowledgeGetResponse.description: Account-scope knowledge metadata plus its file list.

files.description: Array of files in this knowledge; empty array when it has no files.

ok.description: Always `true` on success; a failed delete returns an error instead.

KnowledgePackEnsureRequest.description: Scope at which to ensure knowledge exists.

scope.description:
Scope of the knowledge to ensure.
- `account`: the account knowledge. `scope_id` is replaced by the caller's account ID; only the account owner and admins may call this, even when the knowledge already exists. If the knowledge has no `DUTY.md`, a default one is written.
- `team`: the knowledge of the team in `scope_id`. `scope_id` is required and the caller must be a member of that team.

scope_id.description: Team ID. Required (non-zero) for `team` scope, otherwise the request fails with `InvalidParameter`; ignored for `account` scope.

KnowledgePackItem.description: Knowledge — a versioned file tree staged into every AI SRE sandbox at session start. One knowledge exists per (account, scope, scope_id).

account_id.description: Account that owns the knowledge.

scope.description:
Knowledge scope.
- `account`: account-level knowledge shared by the whole account; `scope_id` is the account ID.
- `team`: knowledge owned by one team; `scope_id` is the team ID.
- `channel`: legacy scope. It cannot be created or moved into through this API and is never returned by `POST /safari/knowledge/pack/list`; it can only appear when such knowledge is addressed directly by `pack_id`.

scope_id.description: Scope owner: the account ID for `account` scope, the team ID for `team` scope.

team_name.description: Display name of the owning team (team scope only). Omitted when empty (account scope, or the team name could not be resolved).

file_count.description: Number of files currently in the knowledge.

total_bytes.description: Total size of all files in bytes. Capped at 5 MiB per knowledge.

version.description: Knowledge version. Starts at 0 and increases by 1 on every file write or file deletion. Moving the knowledge to another scope does not change it.

duty_version.description: The `version` at which `DUTY.md` was last written. Writing `DUTY.md` sets it to the new `version`; when `version` is greater, files were added, changed or deleted after `DUTY.md` was last updated, so `DUTY.md` may no longer index every file.

created_by.description: Person ID of the member whose request created the knowledge. Account knowledge is created automatically by the first request that needs it, so this can be any member of the account.

created_at_ms.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the knowledge was created.

updated_at_ms.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the knowledge was last modified.

can_edit.description: Whether the caller can change this knowledge and its files: for `account` scope, `true` only for the account owner and admins; for `team` scope, `true` only when the caller is a member of that team (owners and admins are not exempt).

KnowledgePackListRequest.description: Filter and pagination for the knowledge list.

p.description: Page number, 1-based. When both `p` and `limit` are omitted (or ≤ 0), all matching knowledge is returned without paging; when only `limit` is set, `p` defaults to 1.

limit.description: Page size. Defaults to 20 when `p` is set and `limit` is omitted; no upper bound is enforced.

scope.description:
Which scopes to return:
- `all` (default): account knowledge (unless `include_account` is `false`) plus the visible team knowledge.
- `account`: only the account knowledge; `include_account` and `team_ids` are ignored.
- `team`: only team knowledge, optionally narrowed by `team_ids`; `include_account` is ignored.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring filter over knowledge ID, scope, scope ID, account ID and team name. Account knowledge also matches `账户`/`账号` and team knowledge also matches `团队`. Leading and trailing spaces are ignored.

team_ids.description: Restrict team knowledge to these team IDs. IDs of teams the caller does not belong to are silently dropped — this applies to every caller, including owners and admins.

include_account.description: Whether to include the account knowledge when `scope` is `all` or omitted. Defaults to `true`.

KnowledgePackListResponse.description: Visible knowledge and the total after filtering.

packs.description: Array of visible knowledge after filtering (current page), used with `total` for pagination.

total.description: Total number of knowledge entries after filtering, before pagination.

KnowledgePackUpdateRequest.description: Move knowledge to a different scope.

scope.description:
Destination scope. Omit to leave the knowledge unchanged and get it back.
- `account`: make it the account knowledge (only the account owner and admins).
- `team`: move it to the team in `scope_id` (the caller must be a member of that team).
Any other value returns `InvalidParameter`. If the destination already has knowledge, the request fails with `ReferenceExist`.

scope_id.description: Destination team ID. Required (non-zero) when `scope` is `team`; ignored when `scope` is `account` (the account ID is used).

KnowledgeWarning.description: Non-blocking annotation returned by file uploads and deletions, e.g. references that point at a removed file.

code.description: Warning code. One of: `unresolved_reference` (an @ref in the written file's content points to a file that does not exist in the knowledge; `ref` carries it), `still_referenced_by` (the deleted file is still @ref-referenced by other files in the knowledge; `refs` lists the referrers).

ref.description: Set only for `unresolved_reference`: the referenced path that does not exist in the knowledge.

refs.description: Set only for `still_referenced_by`: `rel_path` of every other file that still references the deleted file.

target_page_id.description: Flashduty target status page ID that will receive the imported subscribers.

MigrateStatusPageStructureRequest.description: Parameters for starting an Atlassian Statuspage structure and history migration job.

api_key.description: Atlassian Statuspage API key with access to the source page.

source_page_id.description: Atlassian Statuspage source page ID; only letters, digits, `_`, and `-` are accepted.

url_name.description: Target URL name for the new status page, normalized to a URL-safe slug (max 255 characters). Omit or pass null to derive it from the source page name; an explicitly empty string is rejected.

NameMessage.description: Per-item result for batch rule operations.

name.description: Name of the rule this result belongs to; `id: <id>` when the rule ID does not exist.

message.description: Outcome for this rule. On success it is empty for `/monit/rule/update/fields` and a localized success text (`Move successfully` / `移动成功`) for `/monit/rule/move`; on failure it carries the error message.

member_id.description: ID of the newly created member.

member_name.description: Display name stored for the member; derived from the email prefix when `member_name` was omitted.

NotifyChat.description: Notification delivery record for a chat group recipient.

data_source_id.description: Integration data source ID used to send the notification.

failed_reason.description: Localized, human-readable reason the delivery failed, as reported by the delivery channel; omitted when delivery succeeded or no failure was reported. The text is not a fixed code set.

NotifyPerson.description: Notification delivery record for a single person recipient.

failed_reason.description: Localized, human-readable reason the delivery failed, as reported by the delivery channel; omitted when delivery succeeded or no failure was reported. The text is not a fixed code set.

sms_content.description: SMS text delivered to the recipient; present on SMS deliveries.

NotifyRobot.description: Notification delivery record for a robot webhook recipient.

failed_reason.description: Localized, human-readable reason the delivery failed, as reported by the delivery channel; omitted when delivery succeeded or no failure was reported. The text is not a fixed code set.

OnceTimeFilter.description: One-off time window defined by unix seconds.

end_time.description: Window end, Unix timestamp in seconds. Must be greater than 0.

start_time.description: Window start, Unix timestamp in seconds. Must be greater than 0 and less than `end_time`.

OrFilterGroup.description: OR-of-AND filter tree. Outer array is a list of AND groups; the condition passes if **any** AND group matches. Within each AND group, **all** conditions must match.

items.description: AND group — all conditions in this array must match.

score.description: Similarity score from the vector search.

factor_type.description: Factor type. `api`: backend API factor — `factor_name` is the API name (e.g. `skill:write:upload`), enforced at the gateway; `button`: UI action factor, used by the role-config page to render action toggles; `visit`: page-visit factor (custom menu pages use this type); `menu`: menu-visibility factor (legacy, no current seed data); `url`: page route-path factor (legacy, no current seed data).

source.description: Origin of the factor. `system` — seeded built-in factor; `account` — dynamic factor created for this account (e.g. custom menus).

source_ref.description: Primary key of the source object (e.g. the custom menu ID) for account-scoped factors. Omitted when empty.

account_id.description: Owning account ID. Omitted when 0, i.e. for system-level permissions.

id.description: Unique permission ID.

is_granted.description: Whether this permission is granted to the roles given in `role_ids`. Always present in this endpoint's response; `false` entries only appear when `with_all` is true.

permission_type.description: Whether this is a read or manage permission. `read`: view-only permission (read/list/query); `manage`: administrative permission covering mutations (create, update, delete, configure).

scope.description:
Functional scope the permission applies to.

| value | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `account` | Account settings and API keys |
| `organization` | Members, teams, roles, audit |
| `on-call` | On-call incident management |
| `monit` | Monitoring |
| `rum` | Real user monitoring |
| `ai-sre` | AI SRE features |
| `custom_menu` | Account-defined custom menu pages (on-premises only) |

source.description: Origin of the permission. `system` — seeded built-in permission; `account` — dynamic permission created for this account (e.g. custom menus).

source_ref.description: Primary key of the source object (e.g. the custom menu ID) for account-scoped permissions. Omitted when empty.

status.description: Permission status. `enabled` — active; `deleted` — removed (deleted permissions are filtered out and never returned).

PersonInfosRequest.description: Get person info by IDs request

person_ids.description: Person IDs to look up — these are member IDs (get them from `POST /member/list`). Passing the account ID returns the account principal; unknown IDs are ignored

items.description: Person profiles

account_id.description: ID of the account the person belongs to.

person_id.description: Person ID: the account ID for the account owner, otherwise the member ID.

locale.description: Locale preference (`zh-CN` or `en-US`). Omitted when unset.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone setting: the member's own setting, or the account's for the account owner. Omitted when unset (a member without a setting follows the account's time zone).

phone.description: Phone number. Omitted when empty — this endpoint never populates it.

phone_verified.description: Whether the phone is verified. Always false in this endpoint's response.

email_verified.description: `true` when the email address is verified; for the account owner, `true` whenever an email is set.

as.description: Principal kind: `account` — the account owner principal; `member` — an organization member.

status.description: Person status. `enabled` — active; `pending` — invited but not yet accepted; `deleted` — removed. Omitted when empty.

person_id.description: Member ID; the same ID that `POST /member/list` returns.

as.description: Role label for this member in the context of the current object.

PlatformEmptyObject.description: Empty object returned on success for operations with no meaningful payload.

PostMortemContentResetResponse.description: Result of a successful full post-mortem content reset.

generation.description: New collaboration document generation after the reset.

markdown_bytes.description: UTF-8 byte length of the accepted Markdown content.

markdown_sha256.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the accepted Markdown content.

post_mortem_id.description: ID of the reset post-mortem report.

previous_generation.description: Collaboration document generation before the reset.

revision.description: New content revision after the reset.

PostMortemItem.description: Full post-mortem report including basics, content and follow-ups.

incidents_highest_severity.description: Highest severity among linked incidents: `Critical`, `Warning`, or `Info`; `Ok` only when it was set manually.

incidents_earliest_start_seconds.description: Earliest start time among linked incidents (Unix seconds).

incidents_latest_close_seconds.description: Latest close time among linked incidents (Unix seconds); an incident not yet closed contributes its `end_time`.

incidents_total_duration_seconds.description: Seconds from the earliest start to the latest close among linked incidents (not the sum of each incident's duration).

basics.description: Basics aggregated automatically from the linked incidents: highest severity, earliest start / latest close time, total duration, and responders.

content.description: Post-mortem body; the object holds a single `content` field whose value is a BlockNote JSON string.

follow_ups.description: Follow-up action items rendered as a single string.

has_active_incident.description: `true` when at least one linked incident is not closed yet; follow-ups stay locked until all are closed. Computed per request.

PostMortemMeta.description: Post-mortem metadata (lightweight shape used in lists).

account_id.description: ID of the account that owns this record; the same for every record returned to one `app_key`.

status.description: Post-mortem status. `drafting` means still being edited; `published` means published.

post_mortem_id.description: Post-mortem ID: a 32-character hex string derived from the account ID and the linked incident IDs.

template_id.description: Template used to initialize the report.

author_ids.description: Member IDs that contributed to the report.

team_id.description: Owning team ID. 0 if none.

channel_id.description: Owning channel ID. 0 if none.

is_private.description: When true, only team members and admins can view.

generation.description: Collaboration document generation. Incremented by each full content reset; 0 for legacy documents.

revision.description: Content revision for optimistic concurrency. Monotonically increases on collaborative saves and full content resets.

channel_name.description: Channel name, filled by the server.

account_id.description: Account ID that owns the template; 0 for the built-in template.

template_id.description: Template ID: `post_mortem_default_tmpl_zh-cn` or `post_mortem_default_tmpl_en-us` for the built-in templates, a server-generated ID for custom ones.

name.description: Template name shown in the console.

content.description: Template body as BlockNote editor JSON (an array of blocks), serialized as a string.

content_markdown.description: Markdown version of the template content, used by AI generation.

team_id.description: Managing team ID; 0 for the built-in template.

created_at_seconds.description: Creation time, Unix timestamp in seconds; 0 for the built-in template.

updated_at_seconds.description: Last update time, Unix timestamp in seconds; 0 for the built-in template.

PreflightResult.description: Readiness checks computed before a manual run is allowed to start.

ok.description: Whether all readiness checks passed. Always `true` in a 200 response; a failed preflight returns an error instead.

checks.description: Names of the readiness checks performed, in order. Current fixed set: rule_loaded, actor_authorized, app_allowed, runtime_scope_resolved, rule_config_valid.

scope.description: Resolved run scope for this run; mirrors the rule's run_scope. One of: `person` (personal rule, runs as its creator), `team` (team rule, runs under the owning team).

team_id.description: Rule's scope team ID; 0 means a personal rule.

app_name.description: App the rule is scoped to. Currently always ai-sre; manual runs are only supported for that app.

warnings.description: Non-fatal warnings from preflight. Currently never populated, so the field is omitted.

PreviewRemoteConfigRequest.description: Preview request. Omit `config` to preview the currently live configuration.

app_version.description: App version the simulated client reports, compared exactly with rules' `match.app_version` (no range or prefix matching). Omitted = not reported.

application_id.description: RUM application ID. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

config.description: Draft configuration to evaluate, validated like `POST /rum/application/remote-config/update`. Omit to evaluate the live configuration.

env.description: Environment the simulated client reports, compared exactly with rules' `match.env`. Omitted = not reported, so rules that test `env` cannot match.

sdk.description: SDK identifier the simulated client reports, e.g. `web@2.4.1`, compared exactly with rules' `match.sdk`. Omitted = not reported.

PreviewRemoteConfigResponse.description: Values the simulated client would receive.

hit_rule_index.description: 0-based index into `config.rules` of the first rule that matched, or `-1` when no rule matched (only `default` applied) or the configuration is disabled or absent.

values.description: `default` merged with the matching rule's `set`. Fields set by neither are omitted; an empty object means the client keeps all its init values.

content.description: Template source to render for the channel `type`. Empty or omitted previews the channel's built-in preset content. Ignored for `push`.

type.description:
Channel to preview; other values return `InvalidParameter`.
- `email`: email body (HTML template).
- `sms`, `voice`: SMS text and voice call script.
- `push`: mobile app push (fixed content; `content` is ignored).
- `dingtalk`, `wecom`, `feishu`, `zoom`, `telegram`, `slack`: robot (webhook) messages.
- `feishu_app`, `dingtalk_app`, `wecom_app`, `slack_app`, `teams_app`: IM app cards.

incident_id.description: Incident whose data is rendered (24-character hex ID from `/incident/list`); must exist in the account, otherwise `InvalidParameter`. When omitted a mock incident is used.

incident_card_hidden_fields.description: Incident card fields to hide per IM app when previewing.

feishu_app_card_v2_table_enabled.description: Render Markdown tables in `feishu_app` content as native Feishu card tables, as the template setting of the same name does.

feishu_app_card_v2_preserve_blank_lines.description: Keep blank lines in the body of the Feishu app card v2 preview.

wecom_markdown_v2_enabled.description: Preview `wecom` content as a `markdown_v2` message, as the template setting of the same name does (size limit 4,096 bytes).

success.description: Whether the template rendered without errors.

content.description: Rendered template output; an empty string when `success` is `false`.

message.description: Why rendering failed, in the caller's language; an empty string when `success` is `true`.

card.description: Message frame around the rendered template, in the account language. Returned for `email`, `feishu_app`, `dingtalk_app`, `wecom_app`, `slack_app` and `teams_app`; omitted otherwise.

type.description:
Element kind.
- `template`: where the rendered template (`content`) appears.
- `markdown`: fixed text in the channel's Markdown, in `content`.
- `divider`: a horizontal rule.
- `actions`: a row of buttons, in `actions`.

content.description: Markdown text of a `markdown` element; omitted for other kinds.

actions.description: Buttons of an `actions` element; omitted for other kinds.

style.description: Button style: `primary` (highlighted), `danger` (destructive), `select` (a drop-down menu). Omitted for a plain button.

blocks.description: How the recipient's client shows `content`, split into blocks. Omitted for channels that show the text as is.

type.description: Block kind: `markdown` (text in `content`) or `table` (a table in `columns`/`rows`).

native.description: `true` when a `table` block is shown as a native card table; omitted otherwise.

rows.description: Cell values of a `table` block, one array per row.

page_size.description: Rows shown per page in a native table; omitted when not set.

notices.description: Warnings about how the content will be delivered. Omitted when there are none.

code.description:
Warning kind.
- `table_not_rendered`: the channel cannot show Markdown tables; they are sent as text.
- `native_table_fallback`: a table cannot be a native card table and is sent as Markdown; `reason` says why (`too_many_tables`, `too_many_columns`, `too_many_rows`, `cell_too_long`, `unsupported_cell`, `card_too_large`).
- `content_too_large`: the content exceeds `size_limit_bytes`; `reason` is `truncated` (cut to fit), `compact_fallback` (sent in a compact form) or `rejected` (the channel will refuse it).

reason.description: Detail for `code`, as listed there; omitted for `table_not_rendered`.

size_bytes.description: Size of the rendered content in bytes, measured before any truncation.

size_limit_bytes.description: Size limit the channel applies in bytes: 4,000 for robot channels (and `wecom` without `markdown_v2`), 4,096 for `wecom` with `markdown_v2`, 15,000 for `slack_app`, 30,720 for `feishu_app`; `0` when the channel has no limit.

PublishedArtifactItem.description: One published artifact in the gallery. Time fields are Unix timestamps in milliseconds.

artifact_id.description: Artifact ID (`art_` prefix). Also the key of the public-share link.

team_id.description: Owning scope. `0` means a personal artifact: it appears only in its creator's list, and can be managed by the creator or by anyone who can manage the source session. A positive value is the owning team ID: the artifact appears in that team's members' lists and any team member can manage it. Set from the source session at first publish; change it with `/safari/artifact/gallery/update`.

team_name.description: Owning team's display name. Omitted for personal artifacts.

person_id.description: Person ID of the artifact's creator: the owner of the source session at first publish. It never changes on republish or scope transfer.

is_mine.description: `true` when the caller (for an `app_key` call, the key owner) is the creator, i.e. `person_id` equals the caller's person ID.

can_edit.description: Whether the caller may manage this artifact (rename, transfer, delete, share): the creator, any member of the owning team, or a manager of the source session.

session_id.description: Source session ID (`sess_` prefix) that produced the file.

session_title.description: Source session's title. Omitted when the session has been deleted.

file_id.description: Presented-file ID (`pf_` prefix) currently holding the artifact's bytes. Changes on every republish.

name.description: Underlying file name including extension. Empty when the underlying file record is missing.

content_type.description: MIME type, derived from the file-name extension when the file was produced: `text/html` (.html/.htm), `text/markdown` (.md), `text/plain` (.txt/.log), `text/csv`, `text/yaml` (.yaml/.yml), `text/x-python`, `text/x-go`, `text/x-sh`, `application/json`, `application/xml`, `application/pdf`, `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/svg+xml`, `image/webp`, `application/zip`, `application/gzip` (.tar/.gz/.tgz); any other extension is `application/octet-stream`. Empty when the underlying file record is missing.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the artifact was published.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds of the last change to the artifact row (rename, transfer, republish, or share state change).

pinned_at.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the caller pinned this artifact in the console gallery. Pins are per member; omitted when the caller has not pinned it. Pinned artifacts are listed first by `/safari/artifact/gallery/list`.

share_enabled.description: Whether anonymous public sharing is on. Omitted when false.

public_url.description: Anonymous public link — a console `/share/artifact/<artifact_id>` page served entirely from CDN. Present only while shared; anyone with the link can view it, no login required.

shared_by.description: Person ID of the member who enabled sharing; a later snapshot sync does not change it. Present only while shared.

shared_at.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds of the last share enable or snapshot sync. Present only while shared.

share_file_id.description: Presented-file ID the public snapshot was materialized from. When `share_enabled` is true and `file_id` differs from `share_file_id`, the public snapshot is stale — call `/safari/artifact/gallery/share/sync` to refresh it.

QueryDataRequest.description: Request body of the structured query endpoint.

format.description: Public result-contract version. It is independent of the internal monit-edge query protocol version. Fixed at `query_result.v1`, which defines the structure of the `result` field.

QueryField.description: One typed column. `string` fields contain string or null values; `time` fields contain RFC 3339 Nano strings or null; `float` fields contain numbers, null, or the special strings `NaN`, `+Inf`, and `-Inf`.

labels.description: Series labels. Present on the float field of a time-series frame.

name.description: Column name; on a time-series float field, series are distinguished by `labels` and `name` is usually the metric name.

type.description: Value type governing `values` encoding: `string` = strings or null, `float` = numbers or `NaN`/`±Inf` strings or null, `time` = RFC 3339 Nano strings or null.

values.description: All values of this column in row order; length matches the other fields in the frame.

QueryFrame.description: A typed, columnar table or time-series frame. All fields in one frame have the same number of values. A `time_series` frame contains one time field and one float field; labels belong to the float field.

fields.description: Columns of the frame; all fields share the same `values` length and row i is composed of each field's `values[i]`.

kind.description: Frame type: `table` for a generic table, `time_series` for a series (exactly one time field and one float field).

frames.description: Typed table or time-series frames. A response can contain more than one frame.

kind.description: Result-kind discriminator, always `frames`, indicating the `frames` payload of typed table/time-series frames.
Result-kind discriminator, always `records`, indicating the `records` payload of schemaless record objects.

records.description: Schema-flexible records. Records may have different fields, contain nested JSON, or be null. Integers outside JavaScript's safe range are encoded as decimal strings.

QueryResult.description: Exactly one natural result shape, selected by `kind`.

account_id.description: Optional consistency check. When supplied it must equal the authenticated account, otherwise the request fails with `AccessDenied`. The query always runs as the authenticated account.

ds_type.description:
Data source type. Together with `ds_name` it must match an enabled data source of the account.

- `prometheus`: Prometheus-compatible data source; `expr` is PromQL.
- `loki`: Grafana Loki; `expr` is LogQL.
- `victorialogs`: VictoriaLogs.
- `sls`: Alibaba Cloud Log Service (SLS).
- `tencent_cls`: Tencent Cloud Log Service (CLS); requires monit-edge v0.66.0 or later.
- `elasticsearch`: Elasticsearch.
- `mysql`: MySQL; `expr` is SQL.
- `postgres`: PostgreSQL; `expr` is SQL.
- `oracle`: Oracle Database; `expr` is SQL.
- `clickhouse`: ClickHouse; `expr` is SQL.

Other data source types (for example MongoDB, Redis, or Kafka) are rejected.

ds_name.description: Data source name, as returned by `/monit/datasource/list`. The data source must be enabled; a name that matches no data source of the account returns HTTP 400.

expr.description: Query expression in the language of `ds_type` (PromQL for `prometheus`, LogQL for `loki`, SQL for SQL sources, and so on). Required, at most 64 KiB (12 KiB for `tencent_cls`). Loki's `$__auto` is not supported here; use a fixed duration such as `[5m]`. Prometheus expressions are syntax-checked before dispatch.

delay_seconds.description: Look-back offset in seconds, from 0 to 86400. Applied to point-in-time queries (Prometheus, Loki stats, VictoriaLogs stats); ignored for raw and detail queries. When `args` carries an absolute `<source>.time` and the Edge is v0.74.0 or later, the absolute time takes precedence and this offset is not applied.

args.description:
Extra query parameters as string key/value pairs; keys are namespaced by data source (for example `sls.project`, `loki.type`). At most 128 entries, keys up to 256 bytes, values up to 64 KiB, and 128 KiB in total. What is accepted depends on `ds_type`:

- `prometheus`: optional `prometheus.time`, the evaluation time as Unix seconds, not in the future.
- `loki`, `victorialogs`: `<source>.type` is `stats` (default) or `raw`. `stats` accepts an optional `<source>.time` (Unix seconds, not in the future). `raw` requires a time range, either `<source>.start` + `<source>.end` (Unix seconds) or `<source>.timespan.value` + `<source>.timespan.unit` (`s`, `m`, `h`, or `d`), spanning at most 6 hours, and accepts `<source>.limit` from 1 to 1001.
- `sls`: `sls.project` and `sls.logstore` are required. Optional: `sls.lines` (1 to 100), `sls.offset` (0 or more), and a time range of at most 6 hours given as `sls.from` + `sls.to` (Unix seconds) or `sls.timespan.value` + `sls.timespan.unit`.
- `tencent_cls`: `tencent_cls.region`, `tencent_cls.topic_id`, `tencent_cls.query_mode` (`raw` or `analysis`), and `tencent_cls.syntax` (`cql` or `lucene`) are required. Optional: `tencent_cls.limit` (1 to 100, `raw` mode only, needs monit-edge v0.67.0 or later) and a time range given as `tencent_cls.from` + `tencent_cls.to` (Unix seconds) or `tencent_cls.timespan.value` + `tencent_cls.timespan.unit`, at most 6 hours in `raw` mode and 24 hours in `analysis` mode. Any other key is rejected.
- `elasticsearch`: `es.type` may be `sql` or omitted; any other value is rejected.
- `mysql`, `postgres`, `oracle`, `clickhouse`: no arguments are defined.

An absolute `<source>.time` is only valid for its own data source type. Edges older than v0.74.0 approximate it with a look-back offset and accept only times within the last 86,400 seconds.

QueryRowsRequest.description: Query to run. `ds_type` and `ds_name` together select the data source; `expr` and `args` are interpreted by that data source type.

labels.description: The sample's full label set; may be an empty object but is always present.

value.description: Finite numeric value or a JSON-safe representation of a non-finite float.

kind.description: Result-kind discriminator, always `samples`, indicating the `samples` payload of labeled instant samples.

samples.description: Instant samples with their complete label sets.

RemoteConfig.description: The whole per-application remote configuration. A change reaches an SDK asynchronously and is applied when that SDK creates its next session, so a running session never flips a decision mid-flight.

activation.description: How a change lands on a client that is already running: `next_session` (the default, and what an empty value means) leaves running sessions untouched and applies the change to new sessions; `immediate` ends the running session as soon as the change arrives so a new session starts under the new configuration.

additionalProperties.description: Any JSON value: string, number, boolean, array or object.

custom.description: Free-form key/value map that SDKs hand to the host app verbatim; the platform does not interpret it. At most 5 keys, each key 1–64 bytes, each value valid JSON of at most 4 KB nested at most 3 levels, 16 KB in total. Anyone holding the public client token can read it. Omitted from responses when empty.

default.description: Values every client receives unless a matching rule overrides them.

enabled.description: Kill switch. When `false` the SDK config endpoint returns no values and SDKs fall back to their init values; `default` and `rules` are kept. Treated as `false` when omitted.

refresh_on_foreground.description: If `true`, clients re-check the configuration when they return to the foreground instead of waiting for the next poll. Default `false`; omitted from responses when `false`.

rules.description: Targeting rules, evaluated in order; the first match wins. At most 20. Can be `null` when the configuration was saved without rules.

config.description: The configuration content that went live under this version.

content_hash.description: Fingerprint of the stored configuration: the first 16 hex characters of its SHA-256. Versions with equal hashes have identical content. Can be empty for older versions.

equivalent_to.description: Earliest retained version with the same `content_hash`, e.g. the version a revert restored. Omitted when this version is itself the earliest.

reason.description: Free-text note (not an enum) sent as `reason` when the version was published or reverted; `""` when none was given.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds - when the version was published.

updated_by.description: ID of the member who published the version.

updated_by_name.description: Name of the member who published the version at publish time, truncated to 128 characters.

version.description: Version number, unique within the application.

RemoteConfigRule.description: One targeting rule: when every `match` condition holds, `set` overrides `default`. The first matching rule wins and evaluation stops there; rule order is the priority. `set` must set at least one value.

match.description: Conditions on what the SDK reports in its config request, combined with AND and compared as exact strings. Keys are limited to `env`, `app_version` and `sdk`; values are 1–256 bytes. A key the SDK does not report never matches.

RemoteConfigValues.description: The SDK knobs a configuration can set. Every field is optional: a value absent from both rule and default is omitted from the SDK response, which tells the SDK to keep its init value.

defaultPrivacyLevel.description:
How Session Replay masks a page by default:

- `mask`: replaces text and hides input values.
- `mask-user-input`: keeps page text but hides what users type.
- `allow`: records the page as it is; content already uploaded cannot be masked later.

sessionOnError.description: Keep sessions the session sample rate did not draw when they report an error; applies only to sessions that rate missed, so it does nothing alongside a rate of 100.

sessionReplayOnError.description: The same switch for Session Replay: un-sampled sessions still record and upload their recording only when the session errors.

sessionReplaySampleRate.description: Percentage of sessions that record Session Replay (0–100).

traceSampleRate.description: Percentage of sessions that inject trace headers into their requests (0–100). Decided per session: a session traces all of its requests or none.

incident_ids.description: Incident IDs to remove. At most 100 per call. The caller must have access to every channel the incidents belong to.

ReopenIncidentRequest.description: Parameters for reopening one or more closed incidents.

incident_ids.description: Incident IDs to reopen. At most 100 per call.

reason.description: Optional free-text reason, recorded on the `i_reopen` timeline entry. At most 1,024 characters.

comment_type_ids.description: IDs of every comment type of the account in the desired order (24-character hex ObjectIDs).

ResetIncidentFieldRequest.description: Parameters for updating a custom field value on an incident.

field_name.description: Custom field name (the field's `field_name`, not its display name). The field must exist and be enabled; list fields with `POST /field/list`.

field_value.description: New value. Its type must match the field: `checkbox` takes a boolean, `single_select` one of the options, `multi_select` an array of options, `text` a string. Omit it or send `null` to clear the field.
