ResetPostMortemBasicsRequest.description: Basic incident facts to write back to a post-mortem report.

incidents_highest_severity.description:
Highest severity among the linked incidents.
- `Critical`: critical.
- `Warning`: warning.
- `Info`: informational.
- `Ok`: recovered.

incidents_earliest_start_seconds.description: Unix timestamp in seconds for the earliest linked incident start time.

incidents_latest_close_seconds.description: Latest close time among the linked incidents, Unix timestamp in seconds. 0 (also when omitted) means still open.

incidents_total_duration_seconds.description: Total incident duration in seconds; 0 when omitted.

responder_ids.description: Member IDs to store as the report's responders. Replaces the stored list; omit or send `[]` to clear it. IDs that do not resolve to a person are dropped.

ResetPostMortemContentRequest.description: Parameters for fully replacing a drafting post-mortem report body.

expected_revision.description: Current content revision expected by the caller. Pass 0 for the first write to a document that has never been saved.

idempotency_key.description: Non-blank key for safely retrying this exact reset request.

markdown.description: Replacement Markdown content. Limited to 4 MiB.

post_mortem_id.description: ID of the post-mortem to reset; obtain it from `POST /incident/post-mortem/list`.

ResetPostMortemFollowUpsRequest.description: Parameters for replacing post-mortem follow-up action items.

follow_ups.description: Follow-ups as free text, replacing the stored string. A JSON array in the console's follow-up format (objects with `title`, `status`, `priority`, `assignee_ids`, …) is also synced into structured follow-up work items.

ResetPostMortemStatusRequest.description: Parameters for changing a post-mortem report status.

status.description:
Target report status.
- `drafting`: being edited; the body can still be replaced with a content reset.
- `published`: published; media files no longer referenced by the body are deleted.

ResetPostMortemTitleRequest.description: Parameters for changing a post-mortem report title.

title.description: New report title, at most 256 characters.

ResetWorkItemAssigneesRequest.description: Full replacement of a work item's assignee set. Exactly one of `assignees` or `assignee_ids` must be sent.

work_item_id.description: Work item ID (opaque string, max 128 characters).

version.description: The item's current `version` (≥ 1) for optimistic locking.

assignee_ids.description: Legacy alias for the replacement assignee set. Equivalent to `assignees` with every entry `type` `person`. Mutually exclusive with `assignees`: sending both returns an error. An empty array clears all assignees.

assignees.description: Replacement assignee set. Each entry is `{type, id?}`. `type` is `person` or `ai_sre`; an `ai_sre` entry omits `id`. Mutually exclusive with `assignee_ids`: sending both returns an error. `assignee_ids` is the legacy alias and is equivalent to an all-`person` list. At most 20 entries. An empty array clears all assignees.

ResolveIncidentRequest.description: Parameters for resolving one or more incidents.

custom_fields.description: Custom field values for the resolution form. Allowed keys and values depend on the incident's visible form.

description.description: New incident description, up to 6,144 characters. When set, it replaces the current description before the incident closes.

images.description: Images attached to the resolution timeline entry.

incident_ids.description: Incident IDs to resolve. At most 100 per call.

resolution.description: Optional resolution note applied to every resolved incident.

root_cause.description: Optional root cause note applied to every resolved incident.

summary.description: Form summary recorded as a timeline comment. Accepted only when the resolution form contains a summary element.

acknowledged_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the member acknowledged. 0 if not yet acknowledged.

assigned_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the member was assigned.

email.description: Member email, filled by the server.

person_name.description: Member display name, filled by the server.

allOf.description: Aggregated incident metrics for a single responder.

acknowledgement_pct.description: This responder's acknowledgement rate (%): acknowledged incidents ÷ involved incidents × 100, rounded to two decimals and capped at 100; 0 when the responder has no incidents.

mean_seconds_to_ack.description: This responder's mean time to acknowledgement in seconds; 0 when the responder acknowledged nothing.

total_engaged_seconds.description: This responder's total engaged time in seconds: each incident contributes close time minus their acknowledgement time.

total_incident_cnt.description: Incidents this responder was involved in.

total_incidents_escalated.description: This responder's incidents that were escalated at least once.

total_incidents_reassigned.description: Incidents reassigned away from this responder.

total_incidents_timeout_escalated.description: This responder's incidents escalated on timeout.

total_interruptions.description: Interruptions for this responder: notifications sent via app push, SMS, or voice call; consecutive notifications within 60 seconds count as one.

total_notifications.description: Total notifications sent to this responder.

total_seconds_to_ack.description: This responder's total time to acknowledgement in seconds: each incident contributes acknowledgement time minus assignment time.

items.description: Per-responder metric rows, newest bucket first. Responders without incidents in a bucket produce no row.

ResponseEnvelope.description: Standard response envelope used by every Flashduty public API. On success `data` contains the endpoint-specific payload and `error` is absent. On failure `error` is present and `data` is absent. `request_id` is always present and is also mirrored in the `Flashcat-Request-Id` response header.

request_id.description: Unique ID for this request. Mirrored in the Flashcat-Request-Id header. Include it when reporting issues.

data.description: Operation-specific payload, documented in each operation's 200 response. Operations without a payload return `{}` or omit `data` entirely.

RevertRemoteConfigRequest.description: Republish an earlier version's content under a new version number.

application_id.description: RUM application ID. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

reason.description: Optional free-text note (not an enum), at most 255 characters, stored verbatim and returned as `reason` by `POST /rum/application/remote-config/history/list`. The server does not fill it in when omitted.

version.description: Version to restore. Must be one of the retained versions listed by `POST /rum/application/remote-config/history/list`.
New version number created by the revert (previous highest version + 1).

role_id.description: Role ID to delete. Get IDs from `POST /role/list` (built-in roles: 2=Admin, 6=Responder, 8=Viewer).

is_force.description: When false (default), deletion fails with `ReferenceExist` while members still hold the role, listing them in `data.refs`. When true, the role is first revoked from all holders and then deleted. Does not bypass the SSO default-role check.

RoleGrantRequest.description: Request to grant or revoke a role from members.

member_ids.description: IDs of the members to grant the role to or revoke it from (from `POST /member/list`). All must be members of the account; duplicates are rejected.

role_id.description: Role ID to grant or revoke. Get IDs from `POST /role/list`.
Role ID to operate on. Get IDs from `POST /role/list` (built-in roles: 2=Admin, 6=Responder, 8=Viewer).
Role ID to query. Get IDs from `POST /role/list` (built-in roles: 2=Admin, 6=Responder, 8=Viewer).

RoleItem.description: A role and its permission set.

role_id.description: Role ID. Built-in roles use the fixed IDs `2` (Admin), `6` (Responder), and `8` (Viewer).

role_name.description: Role name, unique in the account. The built-in roles are named `Admin`, `Responder`, and `Viewer` in every language.

description.description: Role description. For built-in roles it is localized by the request language.

status.description: Role status. `enabled` — active; `disabled` — turned off with `POST /role/disable`; it grants no permissions to the members who hold it. Built-in roles are always `enabled`; deleted roles are never returned.

permission_ids.description: IDs of the permissions the role grants, in ascending order; resolve them with `POST /role/permission/list`. Empty array when none.

editable.description: `false` for the built-in roles (Admin, Responder, Viewer); `true` for custom roles.

created_at.description: Time the role was created, Unix timestamp in seconds. Built-in roles carry a fixed timestamp.

updated_at.description: Unix epoch seconds the role was last updated.

asc.description: Ascending sort order. Default: false (descending).

no_global.description: When true, exclude the built-in global roles (Admin, Responder, Viewer) and return only custom roles. Default: false.

orderby.description: Sort field. Default: `updated_at`.

total.description: Number of roles returned: custom roles plus the 3 built-in roles unless `no_global` is true.

items.description: Array of roles; includes account roles plus built-in global roles unless `no_global=true`; empty array when no results.

role_ids.description: Role IDs (built-in or custom) whose granted permissions to return or mark. IDs that do not exist are ignored.

with_all.description: When true, return every permission and use `is_granted` to mark the ones granted by `role_ids`. When false (default), return only the granted permissions.

items.description: Array of permission items: system-level permissions plus the caller's account-scoped custom-menu permissions (never other tenants' rows).

RoleUpsertRequest.description: Parameters for creating or updating a custom role.

role_id.description: ID of the custom role to update. Omit or set to 0 to create a new role. Do not pass the built-in role IDs `2`, `6`, or `8`.

description.description: Role description, up to 499 characters. Omitting it on update clears the stored description.

permission_ids.description: IDs of the permissions the role grants (from `POST /role/permission/list`). Replaces the existing set; omitting it or sending an empty array leaves the role with no permissions.

role_name.description: Role name echoed from the request.

RouteCase.description: A single case branch in the routing rule. When all of its conditions match, the alert is dispatched to the configured channels.

if.description: Conditions joined with AND; an empty list matches every event. Required.

channel_ids.description: Target channel IDs. Required when `routing_mode` is `standard` (or empty); returned as `null` for `name_mapping`.

fallthrough.description: When `true`, evaluation continues with the next case after this one matches and the channels of all matched cases are combined; when `false`, evaluation stops at this case.

routing_mode.description: Routing mode. `standard` routes to the fixed `channel_ids`; `name_mapping` routes to the enabled channel whose name equals the value of `name_mapping_label` on the event. An empty value is treated as `standard` and is omitted in responses.

name_mapping_label.description: Event field whose value is used as the target channel name, for example `labels.service`. Required when `routing_mode` is `name_mapping`; if no enabled channel has that name, the case adds no channel.

RouteDefault.description: Default branch used when no case matches (or all matched cases yield no valid channels).

channel_ids.description: Channels used when no case yields a channel. An empty list is treated as no default branch.

RouteInfoRequest.description: Parameters for retrieving the routing rule of one integration.

integration_id.description: Shared integration ID, greater than 0; obtain it from `POST /integration/list`.

RouteItem.description: Routing rule of a shared integration. Alerts are evaluated against `cases` in order; when no case yields a channel, `default` is used.

integration_id.description: Integration the rule belongs to.

sections.description: Optional sections that visually group cases.

status.description: Rule status. These endpoints return only `enabled` rules; `deleted` rules (for example of a deleted integration) are not returned.

version.description: Version number, increased on every `POST /route/upsert`. The server does not use it for concurrency checks.

updated_by.description: ID of the person who performed the last update.

creator_id.description: ID of the person who created the rule.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete time, Unix timestamp in seconds. Not returned by these endpoints, which return only active rules.

created_at.description: Creation time, Unix timestamp in seconds.

updated_at.description: Last update time, Unix timestamp in seconds.

RouteMatchCondition.description: A single match condition. All conditions inside one case form an AND group.

key.description: Alert or change event field to match: `title`, `description`, `severity` (alias `alert_severity`, `event_severity`), `status`, `alert_key`, `change_key`, `title_rule`, `integration_id` (alias `data_source_id`), or any `labels.<name>`. An unknown key returns `InvalidParameter`.

oper.description: Match operator. `IN` matches when the field value matches any entry in `vals`; `NOTIN` matches when it matches none. A missing field never matches `IN` and always matches `NOTIN`.

vals.description: Values to compare, at least one. Each entry is matched as: an exact string; a wildcard pattern when it contains `*` or `?` (must match the whole value); a regular expression when wrapped in slashes, such as `/^db-/` (may match anywhere in the value); an IP range written `cidr:<network>`, such as `cidr:203.0.113.0/24`; or a numeric comparison `num:<op>:<number>` with `lt`, `le`, `gt` or `ge`, such as `num:gt:90`.

RouteSection.description: A logical section that groups consecutive cases for display purposes.

name.description: Section name. Must be unique within the rule.

position.description: Index in `cases` where this section starts. Must be between 0 and the length of `cases`.

RuleAuditListResponse.description: Audit records for a rule, ordered by creation time descending. The `content` field is omitted.

check_anydata.description: Any-data check configuration. Fires when the query returns any data rows.

alerting_check_times.description: Number of consecutive evaluations that must satisfy the condition before alerting; minimum 1.

enabled.description: Whether any-data checking is enabled: any returned data row triggers an alert.

push_recovery_event.description: Whether to push a recovery event notification when the alert resolves.

recovery.description: Recovery condition for any-data check. If omitted or `mode` is empty, treated as `nodata`.

args.description: Datasource-specific options for the recovery query, same convention as `queries[].args`; required for Elasticsearch datasources when `mode` is `ql`.

mode.description: `nodata` = recover when the query returns no data; `ql` = recover when the `condition` expression evaluates to true. When `mode` is `ql`, only a single query (`name=A`) is permitted.

recovery_check_times.description: Number of consecutive evaluations that must satisfy the recovery condition before resolving; minimum 1.

severity.description: Severity of any-data alert events; case-sensitive.

alert_on_empty_result.description: Whether to trigger an alert when every query returns an empty result.

alert_on_empty_result_severity.description: Severity of empty-result alerts, case-sensitive; only effective when `alert_on_empty_result` is enabled.

alerting_check_times.description: Number of consecutive evaluations that must satisfy the condition before alerting; minimum 1.

enabled.description: Whether no-data checking is enabled: a previously-seen series that stops returning data triggers an alert.

push_recovery_event.description: Whether to push a recovery event notification when the alert resolves.

recovery_check_times.description: Number of consecutive evaluations that must satisfy the recovery condition before resolving; minimum 1.

severity.description: Severity of no-data alert events; case-sensitive.

alerting_check_times.description: Number of consecutive evaluations that must satisfy the condition before alerting; minimum 1.

critical.description: Critical threshold expression referencing query results via `$<query>` or `$<query>.<value_field>`, e.g. `$A > 90`; at least one severity must be configured.

enabled.description: Whether threshold checking is enabled.

info.description: Info threshold expression, same syntax as `critical`.

push_recovery_event.description: Whether to push a recovery event notification when the alert resolves.

recovery.description: Recovery evaluation configuration for threshold checks.

args.description: Datasource-specific extra parameters for the recovery query, using the same `<datasource>.<param>` key convention as query `args`. Omitted when empty.

condition.description: Recovery condition expression; required when `mode` is `threshold` or `ql`, and must be empty for `invert`.

mode.description: Recovery mode: `invert` = resolve when the alert expression no longer holds (`condition` stays empty); `threshold` = resolve when the `condition` threshold expression holds; `ql` = resolve when the `condition` query expression evaluates true.

value_fields.description: Numeric result fields the recovery `condition` references as `$A.<field>`; same semantics as the query's `value_fields`. Omitted when empty.

recovery_check_times.description: Number of consecutive evaluations that must satisfy the recovery condition before resolving; minimum 1.

warning.description: Warning threshold expression, same syntax as `critical`.

queries.description: Query list with at least one entry; each needs a unique `name` (`R` and `__all__` are reserved) and a non-empty, non-duplicate `expr`.

args.description: Datasource-specific query options keyed by the `<datasource>.<option>` convention (e.g. `es.type`, `tencent_cls.limit`); most datasources need none.

expr.description: Query expression.

label_fields.description: Result fields that become alert event labels — identical label sets collapse into one alert; must not overlap `value_fields`; applies to table-shaped results (SQL/ES-style datasources).

name.description: Query identifier (letter, e.g. `A`). The name `R` is reserved and must not be used.

value_fields.description: Numeric result fields used in threshold evaluation (referenced as `$A.<field>` in threshold expressions); required for threshold checks unless the datasource is `prometheus`/`loki`/`victorialogs`; field names must not contain `.`.

relate_queries.description: Optional auxiliary queries whose results are attached to alert events as context. Each entry must have a unique `name` (not duplicating any query name) and a non-empty `expr`.

args.description: Datasource-specific options for the auxiliary query, same convention as `queries[].args`.

expr.description: Query expression.

name.description: Relate-query identifier.

RuleCounterChannelResponse.description: Map of channel name to rule count. Unresolved channel IDs appear as stringified IDs.

RuleCounterTotalResponse.description: Historical rule-count samples ordered by `clock` ascending.

rule_id.description: Newly created rule ID (MongoDB ObjectID).

rule_name.description: Rule name echoed back from the request.

ids.description: IDs of the rules to update; must contain at least one ID.

fields.description: Names of the fields to update. Each listed field takes the value of the same-named request field, and is set to its zero value when that value is omitted; values sent for unlisted fields are ignored. An unknown name fails the whole call with `InvalidParameter`.

labels.description: Custom label key-value pairs; replaces existing labels as a whole. Effective only when `fields` includes `labels`; cannot be sent together with `labels_patch`.

ds_type.description: Datasource type identifier. Enabled rules must use a type that supports alerting: `prometheus`, `elasticsearch`, `loki`, `clickhouse`, `mysql`, `oracle`, `postgres`, `sls`, `tencent_cls`, `victorialogs`. Effective only when `fields` includes `ds_type`.

ds_list.description: Datasource name match patterns; wildcards supported. Effective only when `fields` includes `ds_list`.

ds_ids.description: Datasource IDs, merged with `ds_list` to decide which datasources the rule monitors; IDs survive datasource renames. Effective only when `fields` includes `ds_ids`.

enabled.description: Whether the rule is enabled. Setting it to `false` makes the server clean up the rule's active alerts. Effective only when `fields` includes `enabled`.

debug_log_enabled.description: Whether to enable debug logging; the edge emits detailed evaluation logs for troubleshooting. Effective only when `fields` includes `debug_log_enabled`.

cron_pattern.description: Schedule expression: a 6-field cron (with seconds) or an `@every 30s` interval descriptor; `CRON_TZ=`/`TZ=` prefixes are not allowed. Effective only when `fields` includes `cron_pattern`.

timezone.description: Timezone the rule runs in, as an IANA name (e.g. `Asia/Shanghai`, `UTC`); empty falls back to `Asia/Shanghai`. Effective only when `fields` includes `timezone`.

delay_seconds.description: Seconds to shift the evaluation query window backward, compensating for data ingestion latency. Effective only when `fields` includes `delay_seconds`.

enabled_times.description: Time windows during which the rule is in effect; element structure see `EnabledTime`. Effective only when `fields` includes `enabled_times`.

annotations.description: Annotation key-value pairs delivered with alert events; replaces existing annotations as a whole, and keys must not start with `$` (reserved for query fields). Effective only when `fields` includes `annotations`; cannot be sent together with `annotations_patch`.

description.description: Rule description, rendered according to the rule's existing `description_type` (which this endpoint cannot change). Effective only when `fields` includes `description`.

channel_ids.description: IDs of the collaboration spaces alerts are sent to; may be empty. Effective only when `fields` includes `channel_ids`.

repeat_interval.description: Interval in seconds between repeated alert notifications; values below 1 fall back to 3600, maximum 2147483647. Effective only when `fields` includes `repeat_interval`.

repeat_total.description: Maximum number of repeated notifications; values below 1 fall back to 3, maximum 2147483647. Effective only when `fields` includes `repeat_total`.

labels_patch.description: Partial label update that keeps unmentioned labels. Requires `labels` in `fields` and cannot be sent together with `labels`; otherwise the call returns `InvalidParameter`.

annotations_patch.description: Partial annotation update that keeps unmentioned annotations. Requires `annotations` in `fields` and cannot be sent together with `annotations`; otherwise the call returns `InvalidParameter`.

id.description: Alert rule ID. Obtainable per folder via `POST /monit/rule/list/basic`.

ids.description: IDs of the alert rules to delete; must contain at least one ID. Get them from `POST /monit/rule/list/basic`.

RuleImportRequest.description: Array of alert rule export objects to import.

RuleListRequest.description: Filter parameter for listing rules in a folder.

folder_id.description: ID of the folder to list. Must be an existing folder the caller can manage; `0` or an unknown ID returns `InvalidParameter`.

include_descendants.description: Also search all descendant folders. When `true`, results are sorted by name, capped by `limit`, and each item fills only `id`, `folder_id` and `name` (other fields carry zero values); combine with `query` for rule-picker scenarios.

query.description: Filter by rule name substring; a numeric value also matches the rule with that ID. Only effective when `include_descendants` is `true`.

limit.description: Max number of rules returned; only effective when `include_descendants` is `true`. Defaults to 50, capped at 100.

ids.description: IDs of the rules to move; must contain at least one ID.

dest_folder_id.description: Destination folder ID, from `POST /monit/folder/list`. Must be non-zero; a folder that does not exist or that the caller cannot manage fails the whole call with `AccessDenied`.

channel_ids.description: On-call channel IDs that receive the alerts; used only when `delivery_mode` is `oncall`. Kept as a draft in `webhook` mode. Can be `null` when never set.

delivery_mode.description: Alert delivery channel: `oncall` routes alert events through Flashduty On-call, `webhook` POSTs them directly to `webhook_url`. An empty value is treated as `oncall`, and on create/update it is persisted as the deployment default (`webhook` on RUM-only on-premises deployments, `oncall` otherwise). Omitted when empty (legacy rows).

enabled.description: Whether alerting is on. `false` turns alerting off; with `false`, `webhook_url` is not checked.

integration_id.description: Associated on-call integration ID (read-only, auto-assigned on save when `delivery_mode` is `oncall`).

webhook_url.description: URL that receives alert events when `delivery_mode` is `webhook`. Required in that mode while `enabled` is `true`; must use `http` or `https`, and on Flashduty cloud must not resolve to a private, loopback, link-local or reserved address. Ignored in `oncall` mode. Omitted from responses when empty.

RumApplicationCreateRequest.description: Parameters for creating a RUM application.

alerting.description: Alerting configuration; defaults to disabled (`enabled: false`) when omitted.

is_private.description: If `true`, only the account owner, account admins, the creator and members of the owning team can see or edit the application. Default `false`.

repositories.description: Source code repositories to link, in order; the first entry is the primary repository. At most 10 entries.

no_geo.description: If `true`, geographic location is not inferred from the client IP. Default `false`.

no_ip.description: If `true`, client IP addresses are not collected. Default `false`.

team_id.description: Owning team ID. Get team IDs via `POST /team/list`.

tracing.description: Optional APM tracing integration configuration. Stored as empty (`enabled: false`, empty `open_type` and `endpoint`) when omitted.

type.description:
Platform identifier:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `browser` | Web browser application (JavaScript SDK) |
| `ios` | Apple iOS application |
| `android` | Android application |
| `react-native` | React Native application |
| `flutter` | Flutter application |
| `kotlin-multiplatform` | Kotlin Multiplatform application |
| `roku` | Roku channel application |
| `unity` | Unity application |
| `miniprogram` | WeChat mini program |
| `harmony` | HarmonyOS application |
| `electron` | Electron desktop application |

RumApplicationCreateResponse.description: Result of creating a RUM application.

application_id.description: Server-generated application ID (22-character short UUID); pass it as `application_id` to the other application operations.

client_token.description: Token used to initialize the RUM SDK. Also returned by `POST /rum/application/info`.

RumApplicationIDRequest.description: Request with a single application ID.

application_id.description: RUM application ID. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

application_ids.description: Up to 200 application IDs. Duplicates are collapsed, and unknown or deleted IDs are skipped. Get IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

items.description: Applications found among the requested `application_ids`, in no guaranteed order. Empty array when none match.

account_id.description: ID of the Flashduty account that owns the application.

alerting.description: Alerting configuration of the application. Always an object.

application_id.description: Unique application ID.

client_token.description: Token used to initialize the RUM SDK.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp, Unix epoch milliseconds.

created_by.description: Member ID of the creator. The creator can always edit the application.

is_private.description: If `true`, only the account owner, account admins, the creator and members of the owning team can see or edit the application.

links.description: External-link integration configuration. Always an object; `systems` can be `null` when no system was ever saved.

repositories.description: Linked source code repositories, in order; the first entry is the primary repository. Empty array when none are linked. Linking grants no access by itself: AI sessions can only read repositories granted to the account's GitHub App installations.

no_geo.description: If `true`, geographic location is not inferred from IP.

no_ip.description: If `true`, IP addresses are not collected.

status.description:
Application status:

- `enabled`: the SDK `client_token` is accepted and data is collected. Every application created through the API starts in this state.
- `disabled`: the `client_token` is rejected, so no new data is collected. No public operation sets this status.
- `deleted`: soft-delete marker; deleted applications are filtered out of every response, so this value is never returned.

team_id.description: Owning team ID. Members of this team can edit the application and, when it is private, see it.

tracing.description: APM tracing integration configuration. Always an object; when tracing was never configured it is `enabled: false` with empty `open_type` and `endpoint`.

type.description:
Platform identifier:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `browser` | Web browser application (JavaScript SDK) |
| `ios` | Apple iOS application |
| `android` | Android application |
| `react-native` | React Native application |
| `flutter` | Flutter application |
| `kotlin-multiplatform` | Kotlin Multiplatform application |
| `roku` | Roku channel application |
| `unity` | Unity application |
| `miniprogram` | WeChat mini program |
| `harmony` | HarmonyOS application |
| `electron` | Electron desktop application |

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp, Unix epoch milliseconds.

updated_by.description: Last updater member ID.

RumApplicationLink.description: External system link rendered on matching RUM event detail pages.

enabled.description: Whether this external system link is shown. Treated as `false` when omitted.

event_types.description:
RUM event types where this external system link is shown; at least one is required.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `crash` | Crash events (errors flagged `is_crash`) |
| `error` | Error events |
| `view` | Page/screen view events |
| `action` | User action events |
| `resource` | Resource load events |
| `session` | Session events |
| `all` | All event types |

icon_color.description: Display color for the link icon, e.g. `#0F766E`. Omitted from responses when empty.

icon_text.description: Short text shown in the link icon, e.g. `S3`. Omitted from responses when empty.

id.description: Client-chosen identifier for this external system, kept as sent; the server does not validate it.

name.description: Display name of the external system.

url.description: HTTP or HTTPS URL template. `${var}` tokens are resolved from the RUM event context.

RumApplicationLinks.description: External link integration settings for the application.

enabled.description: Master switch for the external-link integration. Treated as `false` when omitted.

systems.description: External systems whose URL templates can be opened from matching RUM events.

asc.description: Sort ascending if `true`; default `false` (descending).

is_my_team.description: If `true`, return only applications owned by teams the caller belongs to. When the caller belongs to no team, the list is empty.

limit.description: Page size. Range: 1–100. Default: 20.

orderby.description: Sort field: `created_at` (creation time) or `updated_at` (last update time); defaults to `updated_at` when omitted.

query.description: Substring match on the application name (SQL `LIKE`, so `%` and `_` act as wildcards).

team_id.description: Filter by team ID. Get team IDs via `POST /team/list`.

has_next_page.description: Whether more pages exist; `true` when matching records remain beyond the current page.

items.description: RUM applications on the current page. Empty array when nothing matches.

total.description: Total number of applications matching the filter conditions.

enabled.description: Whether trace links are shown on RUM events.

endpoint.description: Trace endpoint URL; must start with `http` or `https`. Required whenever `tracing` is sent, even with `enabled: false`. Empty in responses when tracing was never configured.

open_type.description:
How the trace link opens:

- `popup`: open trace details in a popup.
- `tab`: open them in a new browser tab.
- `""` (empty): returned only when tracing was never configured; rejected in requests.

RumApplicationUpdateRequest.description: Parameters for updating a RUM application. All fields except `application_id` are optional.

alerting.description: Alerting configuration. When sent, it replaces the stored alerting object (except `integration_id`, which the server manages). Omit to leave unchanged.

application_id.description: Application ID to update. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

application_name.description: New application name, 1–40 characters. Omit to leave unchanged.

is_private.description: `true` limits access to the account owner, account admins, the creator and members of the owning team; `false` makes the application visible to everyone in the account. Omit to leave unchanged.

links.description: External-link integration configuration. When sent, it replaces the stored object, including the whole `systems` list. Omit to leave unchanged.

repositories.description: Replaces the linked source code repositories when present; an empty array removes all links, and omitting the field leaves them unchanged. At most 10 entries.

no_geo.description: When `true`, stop inferring geographic location from IP; when `false`, resume inferring it. Omit to leave unchanged.

no_ip.description: When `true`, stop collecting user IP addresses; when `false`, resume collecting them. Omit to leave unchanged.

team_id.description: New owning team ID. Get team IDs via `POST /team/list`. Omit to leave unchanged. Moving the application to another team changes who can edit it.

tracing.description: APM tracing integration configuration. When sent, it replaces the stored object and must carry a valid `open_type` and `endpoint`. Omit to leave unchanged.

type.description:
Application type. Omit to leave unchanged. Platform identifier:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `browser` | Web browser application (JavaScript SDK) |
| `ios` | Apple iOS application |
| `android` | Android application |
| `react-native` | React Native application |
| `flutter` | Flutter application |
| `kotlin-multiplatform` | Kotlin Multiplatform application |
| `roku` | Roku channel application |
| `unity` | Unity application |
| `miniprogram` | WeChat mini program |
| `harmony` | HarmonyOS application |
| `electron` | Electron desktop application |

name.description: Column name or alias as written in `sql`; `ts` for the bucket column of `time_series` queries.

nullable.description: Whether values in this column may be `null`. `true` when the driver cannot tell.

type.description: Column type name as reported by the database driver, such as `VARCHAR`, `BIGINT`, `DOUBLE` or `DATETIME`. It depends on the selected column or expression, so the set is open; use it as a hint for parsing `values`.

disable_sampling.description: When `true`, the query always runs on the full data and the response never carries `sampling`. When `false` (default), the server may sample aggregate queries over large time windows.

dql.description: Optional RUM DQL filter. It is translated and `AND`-ed into the `WHERE` clause of `sql`. A DQL parse error is reported in this query's `error` entry.

format.description: Output format. `table` returns rows; `time_series` returns bucketed time-series rows.

id.description: Client-supplied query ID. The same value is used as the key in the response object.

interval.description: Minimum time-bucket width in **milliseconds** for `time_series` queries. Default 3600 (3.6 seconds). The effective width is the smallest step of a fixed ladder that is at least this value and at least the window length divided by `max_points`; it is returned as `interval`. Ignored for `table` queries.

max_points.description: Upper bound on the number of buckets for `time_series` queries. Default 1226. The bucket width grows so that the window holds at most this many buckets. Ignored for `table` queries.

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor from a previous response's `search_after_ctx`, to fetch the next page of the same `table` query. Only used by non-aggregate queries with `ORDER BY` and no `OFFSET`. An invalid value makes this query fail.

sql.description: RUM SQL `SELECT` statement. `FROM` names a scope table (`sessions`, `views`, `actions`, `errors`, `resources`, `long_tasks`, `vitals`, `issues`, `sourcemaps`); columns are `field_key` values from `POST /rum/field/list`. The server adds the account and time-range filters.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone name, such as `Asia/Shanghai`, used to align `time_series` bucket boundaries to local time. Defaults to UTC alignment. Ignored for `table` queries; an unknown name fails the request with `InvalidParameter`.

RumDataQueryOutput.description: Result for one query. Failed subqueries populate `error`; successful ones populate `data`.

data.description: Query result. Omitted when the query failed.

error.description: Set when this query failed after request validation (unknown table or column, invalid `dql` or `search_after_ctx`, database error). The code is always `InternalError`. Omitted when the query succeeded.

RumDataQueryRequest.description: Batch of RUM data queries over a bounded time range.

end_time.description: End of the query window, Unix epoch milliseconds. Maximum 31-day span.

queries.description: Queries to execute concurrently. 1 to 10 queries are allowed.

start_time.description: Start of the query window, Unix epoch milliseconds.

RumDataQueryResponse.description: Map from request query ID to that query's result or error.

RumDataQueryResult.description: Rows and metadata returned by one RUM data query.

fields.description: Column metadata, one entry per returned column, in the same order as `values`. For `time_series` queries the first column is `ts`.

interval.description: Effective time-bucket width in **milliseconds** used by a `time_series` query. Omitted for `table` queries.

sampling.description: Sampling metadata. Omitted when the query did not use sampling.

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor for the next page of a non-aggregate `table` query with `ORDER BY` and no `OFFSET`. Present only when this page returned as many rows as the `LIMIT`; omitted otherwise.

values.description: Result values in column-major order: `values[i]` is the list of every row's value for column `fields[i]`. A column is `null` when the query returned no rows. Datetime values are returned as RFC 3339 strings.

RumDataSamplingDecision.description: Sampling metadata returned when the query engine used sampled data.

enabled.description: Whether sampling was applied. Always `true` here — the `sampling` object is omitted entirely when sampling was not used.

scale_factor.description: Multiplier applied to scale sampled results back to estimated full values. `COUNT`, `SUM` and `COUNT(DISTINCT)` columns in `values` are already multiplied by it; other aggregates are returned as computed on the sample.

RumErrorIngestionCreateRequest.description: Fields for creating a new error ingestion rule.

application_id.description: RUM application ID. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

description.description: Rule description, up to 512 characters. Defaults to an empty string.

filters.description: Conditions (OR-of-ANDs) that select errors. A matched error is still stored but is not grouped into any issue.

rule_id.description: ID assigned to the new rule.

rule_name.description: Echo of the created rule's name.

RumErrorIngestionFilterCondition.description: A single filter condition matched against one error field.

key.description: Field to match. One of `error.usr_id`, `error.usr_email`, `error.error_type`, `error.error_message`, `error.error_stack`, `error.view_url`, `error.env`, `error.version`, `error.service`, `error.browser_name`, `error.browser_version`, `error.fingerprint`, `error.is_crash` (value `true` or `false`), or a `context.`-prefixed path into the error's custom context. Context objects are flattened with dots up to 3 levels (`context.a.b.c`); a deeper object is compared as its JSON text, and array values can't be matched.

oper.description:
Match mode:
- `IN`: matches when the field value matches any entry in `vals`. A context field the error doesn't carry never matches.
- `NOTIN`: matches when the field value matches none of `vals`. A context field the error doesn't carry always matches.

vals.description: Values to match against, at least 1 entry. Each entry is one of: an exact, case-sensitive string; a wildcard pattern using `*`/`?` that must match the whole value; a regexp wrapped in `/` (matches anywhere in the value unless anchored); `cidr:<range>` (the value is parsed as an IP); or `num:lt|le|gt|ge:<number>` (the value is parsed as a number, non-numeric values don't match).

RumErrorIngestionHistoryItem.description: A snapshot of every rule for the application at one history version.

rules.description: The application's complete non-deleted rule list as it was just before the change that created this version. Empty for the version created by the application's first rule.

updated_at.description: Time of the change that created this version, as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

updated_by.description: Member ID of the person who made the change that created this version.

updated_by_name.description: Display name of that member at the time of the change.

version.description: History version number, starting at 1 and incremented by every write. Pass it to `POST /rum/error-ingestion/rules/history/revert`.

RumErrorIngestionHistoryListRequest.description: Query parameters for paginating an application's rule history.

application_id.description: RUM application ID. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

asc.description: `true` sorts ascending; `false` (default) sorts descending, newest first.

limit.description: Page size. Default 20; values above 100 are clamped to 100, and values of 0 or below fall back to 20.

orderby.description:
Sort column:
- `updated_at`: time of the change that created the version (default).
- `version`: version number.
Any other value falls back to `updated_at`.

has_next_page.description: `true` when more versions exist after this page.

items.description: History snapshots, ordered by `orderby`/`asc`.

total.description: Total number of history versions for the application, across all pages.

RumErrorIngestionListRequest.description: Query parameters for listing an application's error ingestion rules.

application_id.description: RUM application ID. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

RumErrorIngestionListResponse.description: All error ingestion rules configured for the application.

items.description: Rules, newest-created first.

RumErrorIngestionOrFilters.description: OR-of-ANDs filter set. The outer array is OR: an error matches the rule if it matches at least one inner AND-group. An empty outer array never matches; an empty inner group matches every error.

items.description: AND-group. The group only matches when every condition inside it matches.

RumErrorIngestionRevertRequest.description: Selects the history version to revert an application's rules to.

application_id.description: RUM application ID. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

version.description: History version number to revert to. Get versions via `POST /rum/error-ingestion/rules/history/list`.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the rule was created; reset to the revert time when the rule is restored by a history revert.

description.description: Rule description, up to 512 characters; empty string when none was given.

filters.description: The rule's conditions. An error that matches them is stored but not grouped into any issue.

rule_id.description: Rule ID, generated by the server on `create`. It stays the same across updates and history reverts.

rule_name.description: Rule name, 1-128 characters. Not required to be unique within the application.

status.description:
Rule status:
- `enabled`: the rule is applied to newly ingested errors.
- `disabled`: the rule is kept but not applied.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds of the last update, enable, or disable; reset to the revert time when the rule is restored by a history revert.

RumErrorIngestionRuleIDRequest.description: Identifies a single rule within an application.

application_id.description: RUM application ID. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

rule_id.description: Rule ID. Get rule IDs via `POST /rum/error-ingestion/rules/list`.

RumErrorIngestionRuleSnapshotItem.description: One rule record inside a history snapshot. Carries the raw storage fields, a superset of the fields returned by `list`.

account_id.description: ID of the account that owns the rule.

application_id.description: RUM application ID the rule belongs to.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the row was created.

created_by.description: Member ID who created the rule.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete time as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Always `0` here, because snapshots contain only non-deleted rules.

description.description: Rule description as of this snapshot version; empty string when none was given.

filters.description: The rule's filter conditions as of this snapshot version.

id.description: Internal storage row ID. Not accepted by any endpoint; use `rule_id` instead. Changes when the rule is restored by a history revert.

rule_id.description: Rule ID, the same value `list` returns for this rule.

rule_name.description: Rule name as of this snapshot version.

status.description:
The rule's status as of this snapshot version:
- `enabled`: applied to newly ingested errors.
- `disabled`: kept but not applied.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the row was last updated.

updated_by.description: Member ID who last updated the rule before this snapshot.

RumErrorIngestionUpdateRequest.description: Partial update to an existing error ingestion rule. Omitted fields are left unchanged.

application_id.description: RUM application ID. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

description.description: New rule description, up to 512 characters. Omit to leave unchanged.

filters.description: New filter conditions. Omit to leave unchanged.

rule_id.description: Rule ID to update. Get rule IDs via `POST /rum/error-ingestion/rules/list`.

rule_name.description: New rule name, 1-128 characters. Omit to leave unchanged.

RumFacetCountRequest.description: Parameters for counting facet value distribution.

dql.description: RUM DQL filter expression applied before counting. Fields in it are validated against the `scope`.

end_time.description: End of the time range, Unix epoch milliseconds. Maximum 31-day span.

facet_key.description: Field key whose value distribution to count, such as `error_type`. Must be a facet field of the given `scope` with `show_type: list` and a non-array `value_type`. List candidates with `POST /rum/field/list`.

facet_value.description: When set, count only events whose `facet_key` equals this value. The JSON type must match the field's `value_type` (string, number or boolean); a mismatch returns `InvalidParameter`. When omitted, events with a `null` value are excluded.

kind.description: Symbol kind, used only when `scope` is `sourcemap` and only meaningful for `android`/`harmony`: `mapping` (default) selects ProGuard/R8 mappings or ArkTS sourcemaps, `native` selects native .so symbols.

limit.description: Maximum number of top values to return. Default 100, maximum 100.

scope.description:
RUM data scope to query. One of:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `session` | User sessions |
| `view` | Page views |
| `action` | User actions |
| `error` | Error events |
| `resource` | Resource loads |
| `long_task` | Long tasks |
| `vital` | Performance vitals (Web Vitals, etc.) |
| `issue` | Aggregated error-tracking issues |
| `sourcemap` | Sourcemap / symbol files |

sql.description: Bare SQL `WHERE` condition (without the `WHERE` keyword) for extra filtering, such as `env = 'prod'`. Any occurrence of `SELECT` is rejected.

start_time.description: Start of the time range, Unix epoch milliseconds.

type.description:
Symbol-store platform, used only when `scope` is `sourcemap`. Defaults to `browser` when omitted; `web` and `javascript` are accepted aliases of `browser`.

| Value | Store queried |
|---|---|
| `browser` / `web` / `javascript` | JavaScript sourcemaps (excluding HarmonyOS ArkTS and React Native rows) |
| `android` | Android ProGuard/R8 mappings; with `kind=native`, Android NDK .so symbols |
| `ios` | iOS dSYM symbols |
| `miniprogram` | WeChat mini program sourcemaps |
| `harmony` | HarmonyOS ArkTS sourcemaps; with `kind=native`, HarmonyOS .so symbols |
| `flutter` | Flutter Dart AOT symbols |
| `electron` | Electron Breakpad symbols |
| `react-native` | React Native JS sourcemaps |

RumFacetCountResponse.description: Top N facet values sorted by count descending.

items.description: Facet values with their occurrence counts, sorted by count descending, capped at `limit` (max 100).

account_id.description: Account ID. 0 for built-in fields.

description.description: Description of what this field captures.

edit_able.description: True if this is a custom field that can be edited by the user.

enum_values.description: Predefined enumerable values for this field. Element type matches the field's `value_type`: string for `string`, number for `number`, boolean for `boolean`. Empty when the field has no fixed set of values.

group.description: Display group used to cluster fields in the console, such as `error`, `action` or `device`. Empty when the field has no group.

high_cardinality.description: True when grouping by this field is restricted: event ID fields cannot be grouped at all, other high-cardinality fields only with count or sum.

is_facet.description: True if value distribution counting is supported for this field.

queryable.description: True if this field can be used in DQL/SQL queries.

scopes.description: RUM scopes this field appears in, using the same values as the request `scopes` (for example `error`, `issue`).

show_type.description: Display type in the analytics UI. One of `list` (shown as an enumerated value list; only this type supports facet counting) or `range` (filtered and shown as a numeric/time range).

status.description: Field status. `enabled`: the field is in use. `disabled`: the field is defined but switched off. Deleted fields are never returned.

unit_family.description: Measurement unit family. `time`: a duration or timestamp (see `unit_name`). `bytes`: a size in bytes. Empty string for dimensionless fields.

unit_name.description: Unit of the stored value. Durations: `nanosecond`, `microsecond`, `millisecond`, `second`. Timestamps: `unix_millisecond`, `unix_second`. Sizes: `byte`. Empty string for dimensionless fields. Most built-in duration fields are in `nanosecond`.

value_type.description:
Data type of the field value. One of:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `string` | String |
| `number` | Numeric |
| `boolean` | Boolean |
| `array<string>` | Array of strings |
| `array<number>` | Array of numbers |
| `array<boolean>` | Array of booleans |

RumFieldListRequest.description: Filter parameters for listing RUM field definitions.

is_facet.description: When omitted or `null`, return all fields. When `true`, return only facet-enabled fields. When `false`, return only fields that are not facet-enabled.

scopes.description:
Filter by RUM data scopes; unknown values are rejected with a parameter error. Omit to list fields of all scopes.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `session` | User sessions |
| `view` | Page views |
| `action` | User actions |
| `error` | Error events |
| `resource` | Resource loads |
| `long_task` | Long tasks |
| `vital` | Performance vitals (Web Vitals, etc.) |
| `issue` | Aggregated error-tracking issues |
| `sourcemap` | Sourcemap / symbol files |

items.description: RUM field definitions matching the `scopes` / `is_facet` filters, with names and descriptions localized to the request locale.

RumIssueExportRequest.description: Filters for exporting RUM error tracking issues to CSV.

application_ids.description: Filter by application IDs. Get IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

asc.description: Sort ascending when `true`; descending by default.

by_intersection.description: When `true`, match by time-range overlap: export issues still active within the window (`last_seen_timestamp` >= `start_time`) even if created before it. Default `false` exports only issues created inside the window.

console_origin.description: Console origin used to build the `issue_url` column, e.g. `https://console.flashcat.cloud`; a trailing `/` is trimmed. The service cannot infer it. When omitted, `issue_url` holds only the path `/rum/error-tracking/issue/<issue_id>`.

dql.description: DQL query for advanced filtering. Field names must be fields of the `issue` scope (see `POST /rum/field/list` with `scopes: ["issue"]`); a bare full-text term searches the error message. Cannot be used with `sql`.

end_time.description: End of the time range, Unix epoch milliseconds. Must be greater than `start_time`; maximum range: 183 days.

error_required.description: If `true`, only export issues with at least one associated error event.

export_fields.description:
CSV columns to export, in the order they appear. Unknown keys are rejected with a parameter error and duplicates are dropped. Empty or omitted: every column below except the `sample_first_*` group.

| Value | Column content |
|---|---|
| `issue_id` | Issue ID |
| `issue_url` | Console URL of the issue detail page (built from `console_origin`) |
| `application_name` | Owning application name |
| `service` | Service name |
| `error_type` | Error type |
| `error_message` | Error message |
| `status` | Triage status |
| `severity` | Severity |
| `is_crash` | Whether the error caused a crash |
| `error_count` | Error occurrence count |
| `session_count` | Affected session count |
| `first_seen_at` | First occurrence time (rendered in `time_zone`) |
| `first_seen_version` | Application version at first occurrence |
| `last_seen_at` | Most recent occurrence time (rendered in `time_zone`) |
| `last_seen_version` | Application version at the most recent occurrence |
| `versions` | All affected versions |
| `suspected_cause` | Suspected cause category |
| `resolved_at` | Resolution time (rendered in `time_zone`); empty while unresolved |
| `sample_time` | Latest error event in the time window: time of the event (rendered in `time_zone`) |
| `sample_version` | Latest error event in the time window: application version |
| `sample_view` | Latest error event in the time window: view name, or the view URL when the name is empty |
| `sample_session_id` | Latest error event in the time window: session ID |
| `sample_device` | Latest error event in the time window: device brand and model |
| `sample_os` | Latest error event in the time window: OS name and version |
| `sample_browser` | Latest error event in the time window: browser name and version |
| `sample_stack` | Latest error event in the time window: error stack, truncated to the first 20 lines |
| `sample_first_time` | Earliest error event in the time window: time of the event (rendered in `time_zone`) |
| `sample_first_version` | Earliest error event in the time window: application version |
| `sample_first_view` | Earliest error event in the time window: view name, or the view URL when the name is empty |
| `sample_first_session_id` | Earliest error event in the time window: session ID |
| `sample_first_device` | Earliest error event in the time window: device brand and model |
| `sample_first_os` | Earliest error event in the time window: OS name and version |
| `sample_first_browser` | Earliest error event in the time window: browser name and version |
| `sample_first_stack` | Earliest error event in the time window: error stack, truncated to the first 20 lines |

limit.description: Page size (1–100). Ignored by the export — the row cap is fixed at 100.

orderby.description:
Sort field; defaults to `updated_at` when omitted.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `created_at` | Issue creation time |
| `updated_at` | Last update time |
| `session_count` | Affected session count |
| `error_count` | Error occurrence count |
| `severity` | Severity rank (`Critical` > `Warning` > `Info`) |

p.description: Page number (1-based). Ignored by the export — the first 100 matching rows are always read.

sql.description: SQL-style WHERE condition for advanced filtering, without the `WHERE` keyword (for example `error_count > 100`). Field names must be fields of the `issue` scope; any text containing `SELECT` is rejected. Cannot be used with `dql`.

start_time.description: Start of the time range, Unix timestamp in milliseconds (a value that looks like seconds is rejected). Issues are matched by creation time unless `by_intersection` is `true`.

statuses.description:
Filter by triage status; any other value is rejected with a parameter error.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `for_review` | Pending triage |
| `reviewed` | Reviewed |
| `ignored` | Ignored |
| `resolved` | Resolved |

suspected_causes.description:
Filter by suspected cause category.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `api.failed_request` | API request failure (e.g. HTTP 4xx/5xx responses) |
| `network.error` | Network connectivity error (offline, aborted requests, etc.) |
| `code.exception` | Code exception (Syntax/Reference/Range and similar runtime errors) |
| `code.invalid_object_access` | Invalid object access (e.g. reading a property of `undefined`/`null`) |
| `code.invalid_argument` | Invalid argument passed to a function |
| `unknown` | Cause could not be determined |

team_ids.description: Filter by team IDs. Get team IDs via `POST /team/list`.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone used to render the CSV time columns and the file name, e.g. `Asia/Shanghai` or `UTC`. Default: `Asia/Shanghai`. An unknown zone name returns `InvalidParameter`.

issue_id.description: Issue ID. Get issue IDs via `POST /rum/issue/list`.

age.description: Time span between the first and most recent occurrence, in seconds.

application_id.description: ID of the RUM application this issue belongs to.

application_name.description: Name of the owning application, resolved by `application_id` at query time (reflects the application's current name).

created_at.description: Issue creation time (client time of the first error event), Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

error.description: Representative error of this issue, taken from the error event that created it.

message.description: Normalized error message, truncated to at most 512 characters.

type.description: Error type reported by the SDK in the error event's `error_type` field — free-form, not a fixed set. Browser errors carry the JavaScript exception name, e.g. `Error`, `TypeError`, `ReferenceError`.

first_seen.description: Information about the issue's first occurrence (time and application version).

timestamp.description: Client time of the first error event, Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

version.description: Application version at first occurrence; empty string when the event carries no version.

is_crash.description: Whether the error caused an app crash.

last_seen.description: Information about the issue's most recent occurrence (time and application version).

timestamp.description: Client time of the most recent error event, Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

version.description: Application version at the most recent occurrence; empty string when the event carries no version.

regression.description: Regression record. Present only after a resolved issue was reopened because its error recurred; cleared when the issue is resolved again.

regressed_at.description: Time the regression was detected, Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

regressed_at_version.description: Application version in which the regression was observed.

resolved_at.description: When the issue was resolved before this regression, as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.
Time the issue was marked resolved (by a user or automatically), Unix timestamp in milliseconds; `0` while unresolved.

resolved_by.description: Person ID of the user who marked the issue resolved; `0` while unresolved or when the issue was resolved automatically.

resolve_mode.description: How the issue reacts when its error recurs after being resolved: `any` reopens it on any recurrence; `version` reopens it only when the error recurs in an application version the issue has not been seen in (errors without a version always reopen it). New issues and automatic resolution use `version`; resolving through `POST /rum/issue/update` without `resolve_mode` sets `any`.

service.description: Name of the service that produced this issue, taken from the error event's `service` field.

severity.description: Issue severity, fixed when the issue is created: the first matching enabled preset severity rule (see `POST /rum/issue/preset-severity/rules/list`) decides it, otherwise a built-in rule (crashes are `Critical`; other errors are scored by environment and message keywords). An error only joins an existing issue of equal or higher severity, so the same error can produce separate issues per severity. Empty string on legacy issues created before severity existed.

status.description:
Triage status of the issue; soft-deleted (`deleted`) issues are never returned. The system resolves an issue automatically when its error has not been seen for 14 days, or when a newer application version reports no such error, and reopens a resolved issue as `for_review` when the error recurs (see `resolve_mode`).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `for_review` | Pending triage |
| `reviewed` | Reviewed |
| `ignored` | Ignored |
| `resolved` | Resolved |

suspected_cause.description: Suspected root cause analysis, determined automatically (rules or AI) or set manually by a user.

person_id.description: Person ID of the user who manually set the cause; 0 when `source` is `auto`.

reason.description: Free-text explanation of the cause, written only by AI analysis; empty string when AI analysis is disabled, has not run yet, or the cause was set by a user.

source.description: Origin of the cause: `auto` for system-determined, `user` for manually set.

value.description:
Suspected cause category. One of:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `api.failed_request` | API request failure (e.g. HTTP 4xx/5xx responses) |
| `network.error` | Network connectivity error (offline, aborted requests, etc.) |
| `code.exception` | Code exception (Syntax/Reference/Range and similar runtime errors) |
| `code.invalid_object_access` | Invalid object access (e.g. reading a property of `undefined`/`null`) |

team_id.description: ID of the team owning this issue. For `POST /rum/issue/info` this is the owning application's current `team_id`; `POST /rum/issue/list` and `POST /rum/issue/export` report the team recorded when the issue was first seen, which differs once the application moves to another team.

updated_at.description: Time the issue was last updated, Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

versions.description: Deduplicated list of application versions in which this issue has occurred; may contain an empty string for events without version info. `null` on issues that never recorded a version list.

asc.description: Sort ascending when `true`; descending by default.

by_intersection.description: When `true`, match by time-range overlap: return issues still active within the window (`last_seen_timestamp` >= `start_time`) even if created before it. Default `false` returns only issues created inside the window.

dql.description: DQL query for advanced filtering. Field names must be fields of the `issue` scope (see `POST /rum/field/list` with `scopes: ["issue"]`); a bare full-text term searches the error message. Cannot be used with `sql`.

end_time.description: End of the time range, Unix epoch milliseconds. Must be greater than `start_time`; maximum range: 183 days.

error_required.description: If `true`, only return issues with at least one associated error event.

limit.description: Page size. Range: 1–100. Default: 20.

orderby.description:
Sort field; defaults to `updated_at` when omitted.

|---|---|
| `created_at` | Issue creation time |
| `updated_at` | Last update time |
| `session_count` | Affected session count |
| `error_count` | Error occurrence count |
| `severity` | Severity rank (`Critical` > `Warning` > `Info`) |

sql.description: SQL-style WHERE condition for advanced filtering, without the `WHERE` keyword (for example `error_count > 100`). Field names must be fields of the `issue` scope; any text containing `SELECT` is rejected. Cannot be used with `dql`.

start_time.description: Start of the time range, Unix timestamp in milliseconds (a value that looks like seconds is rejected). Issues are matched by creation time unless `by_intersection` is `true`.

statuses.description:
Filter by triage status; any other value is rejected with a parameter error.

| `for_review` | Pending triage |
| `reviewed` | Reviewed |
| `ignored` | Ignored |
| `resolved` | Resolved |

suspected_causes.description:
Filter by suspected cause category.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `api.failed_request` | API request failure (e.g. HTTP 4xx/5xx responses) |
| `network.error` | Network connectivity error (offline, aborted requests, etc.) |
| `code.exception` | Code exception (Syntax/Reference/Range and similar runtime errors) |
| `code.invalid_object_access` | Invalid object access (e.g. reading a property of `undefined`/`null`) |
| `code.invalid_argument` | Invalid argument passed to a function |
| `unknown` | Cause could not be determined |

items.description: Issues of the current page.

total.description: Total number of issues matching the filter conditions.

issue_id.description: Issue ID to update. Get issue IDs via `POST /rum/issue/list`.

status.description:
New status. Setting `resolved` on an unresolved issue records the resolution time and operator and clears `regression`; switching away from `resolved` clears the resolution time and operator. Omit to keep the current status.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `for_review` | Pending triage |
| `reviewed` | Reviewed |
| `ignored` | Ignored |
| `resolved` | Resolved |

resolve_mode.description:
How the issue reacts when its error recurs after being resolved. Applied only together with `status: resolved`; defaults to `any` there when omitted, and is ignored with any other status.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `any` | Reopen the issue on any recurrence |
| `version` | Reopen only when the error recurs in an application version the issue has not been seen in; errors without a version always reopen it |

suspected_cause.description:
New suspected cause; setting it marks the cause source as `user`, overriding the automatic classification. One of:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `api.failed_request` | API request failure |
| `network.error` | Network connectivity error |
| `code.exception` | Code exception |
| `code.invalid_object_access` | Invalid object access |
| `code.invalid_argument` | Invalid argument |
| `unknown` | Unknown cause |

RumPresetSeverityRuleCreateRequest.description: Parameters for creating a preset severity rule.

application_id.description: RUM application ID. Get application IDs via `POST /rum/application/list`.

filters.description: OR-of-ANDs filter structure: the outer array is OR'd, each inner array is AND'd. A rule matches an error when at least one inner AND-group fully matches. An empty outer array never matches; an empty inner group matches every error.

severity.description: Severity to assign to errors matching this rule.

priority.description: Evaluation order assigned to the new rule (always the current lowest precedence, i.e. current max + 1).

rule_id.description: ID of the newly created rule.

rule_name.description: Echo of the rule's display name.

RumPresetSeverityRuleFilterCondition.description: One filter condition within an AND group.

key.description:
Filter attribute key. Only these Error-level attributes are supported for preset severity rules.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `error.usr_id` | User ID |
| `error.usr_email` | User email |
| `error.view_url` | Full URL of the page where the error occurred |
| `error.view_url_path` | URL path of the page where the error occurred |
| `error.error_type` | Error type |
| `error.error_message` | Error message |
| `error.env` | Environment (e.g. production/staging) |
| `error.service` | Service name |
| `error.device_type` | Device type |
| `error.os_name` | Operating system name |
| `error.browser_name` | Browser name |
| `error.is_crash` | Whether the error is a crash, compared as the string `true` or `false` |

oper.description: Match semantics: `IN` matches when the attribute value matches any of `vals`; `NOTIN` matches when it matches none of them. An attribute the error does not carry is compared as an empty string.

vals.description: Values to match against; at least one, none empty. Each entry is one of: an exact, case-sensitive whole-value match; a wildcard pattern with `*`/`?` (whole value); a regular expression wrapped in `/.../` (matches anywhere in the value unless anchored with `^`/`$`); `cidr:<network>` for IP-shaped values, e.g. `cidr:10.0.0.0/8`; or a numeric comparison `num:<op>:<number>` with `op` one of `lt`, `le`, `gt`, `ge`, e.g. `num:gt:100`. For `error.is_crash`, use `true` or `false`.
