id.description: Folder ID. Pass it as `id` to update, move, or delete the folder, as `parent_id` or `dest_parent_id` to nest folders under it, and as `folder_id` on alert rules and dashboards.

account_id.description: Owning account ID.

parent_id.description: Parent folder ID; 0 at the root.

parent_path.description: Comma-separated ancestor IDs from the root, excluding this folder; empty at the root.

team_id.description: ID of the team the folder belongs to; 0 when it has no team. Members of the team can see and modify the folder.

name.description: Folder name.

creator_id.description: Member ID of the creator; the creator can always see and modify the folder.

updater_id.description: Member ID of the last updater. Updates and moves both set it.

created_at.description: Creation time as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

updated_at.description: Time of the last update or move as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

IntegrationTypeListRequest.description: Filter parameters for listing integration types.

limit.description: Page size. Defaults to 20, maximum 100.

orderby.description: Sort field. When omitted, types are returned in console ranking order.

category.description: Comma-separated category filter. Values: `event.alert` (alert events), `event.change` (change events), `im` (IM bots), `webhook` (custom webhooks). Unknown values are not rejected and match nothing.

asc.description: Sort ascending when `true` (the default); descending when `false`.

IntegrationTypeItem.description: An integration type the account can configure.

plugin_type.description: Type key to pass as `plugin_type` when creating an integration, for example `standard.alert`, `prometheus.alert`, `zabbix.alert` or `feishu`. The set grows as integrations are added; this endpoint returns the full list.

category.description: Category the type belongs to: `event.alert` alert events, `event.change` change events, `im` IM bots, `webhook` custom webhooks.

status.description: Platform status of the type: `enabled` types can be used; `disabled` types are switched off platform-wide and `POST /integration/create` or `POST /integration/update` returns `InvalidParameter` for them.

limit.description: Page size echoed back.

total.description: Total number of matching types.

items.description: Integration types on the current page.

limit.description: Page size. Defaults to 100, maximum 100.

orderby.description: Sort field. Defaults to `created_at`; `plugin_type` is sorted by the underlying plugin.

category.description: Comma-separated category filter. Values: `event.alert` (alert events), `event.change` (change events), `im` (IM bots), `webhook` (custom webhooks). Unknown values are not rejected and match nothing.

type.description: Deprecated alias of `plugin_type` (comma-separated type keys such as `prometheus.alert`, `zabbix.alert`). Ignored when `plugin_type` is also set.

plugin_type.description: Comma-separated integration type keys, for example `standard.alert,prometheus.alert`; the keys are the `plugin_type` values from `POST /integration/type/list`.

status.description: Comma-separated status filter: `enabled` (accepting events) and/or `disabled` (paused).

name.description: Filter by integration name; matches any name that contains this text.

ref_ids.description: Filter by source reference IDs. Each value must start with `c_` (channel), `a_` (account) or `w_`.

asc.description: Sort ascending when true, descending when false.

is_my_team.description: Limit the result to integrations owned by your teams.

team_ids.description: Filter by team IDs. With `is_my_team`, the values narrow that set further.

IntegrationItem.description: Public integration list item with full stored configuration. Timestamps are Unix epoch seconds.

integration_id.description: Integration ID; pass it as `integration_id` to the other `/integration/*` endpoints.

team_id.description: ID of the team that owns the integration. `0` when it is not assigned to a team.

plugin_type_name.description: Display name of the integration type, in the language of the request.

category.description: Category the integration belongs to: `event.alert` alert events, `event.change` change events, `im` IM bots, `webhook` custom webhooks.

name.description: Integration name.

status.description: Lifecycle status: `enabled` while the integration accepts events, `disabled` when it is paused.

ref_id.description: Source reference ID, normally `a_<account_id>` for an account-level integration; legacy `w_` references may also exist. Channel-owned `c_` integrations are excluded.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp in seconds when the integration was created.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp in seconds when the integration was last updated.

last_time.description: Unix timestamp in seconds of the most recent event received. `0` when no event has arrived yet.

last_source_time.description: Unix timestamp in seconds of the most recent event received from the upstream tool, including events dropped before they became alerts. `0` when none has arrived yet.

editable.description: Whether the current caller passes the integration object-permission check; write calls also require Integrations Manage.

creator_id.description: ID of the member who created the integration.

updated_by.description: ID of the member who last updated the integration.

no_editable.description: Read-only flag. When true, the public APIs do not allow changes to this integration.

plugin_id.description: Internal integration type ID; use `plugin_type`, not this ID, when creating an integration.

integration_key.description: Decrypted integration key for inbound pushes. Empty when no key is stored; distinct from the account `app_key`.

settings.description: Stored type-specific configuration. Each saved secret (passwords, app secrets, tokens, encryption keys, webhook endpoints, HTTP pull URL and body, headers, custom bodies) is returned as `******`; unset values stay empty.

account_id.description: ID of the account that owns the integration.

exclusive_data_source_id.description: Legacy compatibility field; `0` for items returned by this public-integration list.

limit.description: Page size echoed back.

total.description: Total number of matching integrations.

items.description: Integrations on the current page.

integration_id.description: ID of a public integration, returned by `POST /integration/list`. An unknown ID or a channel-owned integration returns `ResourceNotFound`.

IntegrationDetail.description: Public integration detail with stored settings and its decrypted key. Timestamps are Unix epoch seconds.

integration_id.description: Integration ID; pass it as `integration_id` to the other `/integration/*` endpoints.

team_id.description: ID of the team that owns the integration. `0` when it is not assigned to a team.

plugin_type_name.description: Display name of the integration type, in the language of the request.

category.description: Category the integration belongs to: `event.alert` alert events, `event.change` change events, `im` IM bots, `webhook` custom webhooks.

name.description: Integration name.

status.description: Lifecycle status: `enabled` while the integration accepts events, `disabled` when it is paused.

ref_id.description: Source reference ID, normally `a_<account_id>` for an account-level integration; legacy `w_` references may also exist. Channel-owned `c_` integrations are excluded.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp in seconds when the integration was created.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp in seconds when the integration was last updated.

last_time.description: Unix timestamp in seconds of the most recent event received. `0` when no event has arrived yet.

last_source_time.description: Unix timestamp in seconds of the most recent event received from the upstream tool, including events dropped before they became alerts. `0` when none has arrived yet.

editable.description: Whether the current caller passes the integration object-permission check; write calls also require Integrations Manage.

creator_id.description: ID of the member who created the integration.

updated_by.description: ID of the member who last updated the integration.

no_editable.description: Read-only flag. When true, the public APIs do not allow changes to this integration.

plugin_id.description: Internal integration type ID; use `plugin_type`, not this ID, when creating an integration.

integration_key.description: Decrypted integration key for inbound pushes. Empty when no key is stored; distinct from the account `app_key`.

settings.description: Stored type-specific configuration. Each saved secret (passwords, app secrets, tokens, encryption keys, webhook endpoints, HTTP pull URL and body, headers, custom bodies) is returned as `******`; unset values stay empty.

test.description: Plugin test result, returned only when a test is performed.

message.description: Test failure message; empty on success.

plugin_type.description: Integration type. Must be one listed by `POST /integration/type/list` with `supports_api_create: true`.

name.description: Integration name, 2–49 characters when nonempty; defaults to the integration type name when omitted or empty.

team_id.description: Owning team ID; omit or use `0` for no team. A nonzero ID must belong to the current account.

settings.description: Type-specific configuration; the accepted keys depend on `plugin_type`.

integration_key.description: Optional pre-generated key: 35 characters, ending with the account ID modulo 1000 padded to three digits; it must not already be in use. Omit to generate a key.

is_test.description: Run the plugin test during creation; false when omitted. Inspect the returned `test.success` for the test outcome.

CreateIntegrationResponse.description: The created integration and its key.

integration_id.description: ID of the new integration.

integration_key.description: Integration key for inbound pushes; also readable from `/integration/list` and `/integration/info`.

test.description: Plugin test result, returned only when a test is performed.

message.description: Test failure message; empty on success.

UpdateIntegrationRequest.description: Payload for updating an integration. Only the fields you send are changed.

integration_id.description: ID of a public integration, returned by `POST /integration/list`. An unknown ID or a channel-owned integration returns `ResourceNotFound`.

name.description: New name, 2–49 characters.

team_id.description: New owning team ID; `0` clears the team assignment.

settings.description: Replacement type-specific configuration. Known sensitive fields omitted or sent as `******` keep their stored value; an explicit empty headers object clears headers. A stored secret cannot be kept while its destination (such as `endpoint`, `url`, or a database host or port) changes.

is_test.description: Run the plugin test when submitting `settings`; no test is performed for a metadata-only update.

IntegrationLifecycleRequest.description: Identifies the integration to act on.

integration_id.description: ID of a public integration, returned by `POST /integration/list`. An unknown ID or a channel-owned integration returns `ResourceNotFound`.

integration_key.description: New integration key; the previous key stops working immediately. Also readable from `/integration/list` and `/integration/info`.

FolderCreateRequest.description: Request to create a monitor folder.

name.description: Folder name; required, and must not contain a period (`.`), slash (`/`), or comma (`,`).

parent_id.description: ID of the parent folder; 0 or omitted creates a root folder. The caller must be allowed to modify the parent.

team_id.description: ID of the team the folder belongs to; 0 or omitted means no team. Members of the team can see and modify the folder and everything below it.

FolderUpdateRequest.description: Request to update a monitor folder. Editable fields are replaced as a whole.

id.description: ID of the folder to update, from `/monit/folder/list` or the create response.

name.description: New folder name; required, and must not contain a period (`.`), slash (`/`), or comma (`,`).

note.description: New note. Omitted or empty clears the note.

team_id.description: New team ID; 0 or omitted removes the team assignment.

FolderMoveRequest.description: Request to move a monitor folder and its descendants.

id.description: ID of the folder to move, from `/monit/folder/list`.

dest_parent_id.description: ID of the new parent folder; send 0 to move to the root. The field cannot be omitted. Must differ from `id` and must not be a descendant of the folder.

FolderDeleteRequest.description: Request to delete a monitor folder.

id.description: ID of the folder to delete, from `/monit/folder/list`. The folder must be empty.

FolderHealthItem.description: Health summary for a visible folder.

folder_id.description: ID of the folder this entry describes; matches `id` in `/monit/folder/list`.

has_issue.description: `true` when a rule in this folder or in any descendant has an active alert or a runtime problem (`runtime_state` of `offline`, `abnormal`, `stale`, or `no_datasource`). Rules in folders the caller cannot read are not counted.

items.description: One health entry per folder visible to the caller, sorted by `folder_id`.

RumDashboardActor.description: Person who created or last changed the dashboard or a revision.

id.description: Person ID.

name.description: Person name.

RumDashboardBarViz.description: Category bars built from grouped series.

kind.description: Panel kind. Always `bar`.

options.description: Free-form display options stored with the panel; not validated.

unit.description: Display unit of the panel value. One of `unitless`, `ratio`, `percent`, `milliseconds`, `seconds`, `bytes`, `bits`, `count_per_second`, `bytes_per_second`, `bits_per_second`.

decimals.description: Number of decimal places to show.

category_field.description: Field key that supplies the category axis.

value_fields.description: Field keys plotted as bars. Must be non-empty with unique names; `frame_index` and `field_index` are not allowed.

items.description: Field key.

RumDashboardCandidate.description: One option of a custom variable.

text.description: Label shown in the variable bar. Defaults to `value` when empty. At most 1024 characters.

value.description: Value substituted into the query, 1-1024 characters. Cannot be `$__all`.

RumDashboardColumnOption.description: Per-column presentation of a table panel.

display_name.description: Column header. Defaults to the field key when empty.

hidden.description: Whether the column is hidden. `false` hides nothing; omit to inherit.

unit.description: Display unit of the panel value. One of `unitless`, `ratio`, `percent`, `milliseconds`, `seconds`, `bytes`, `bits`, `count_per_second`, `bytes_per_second`, `bits_per_second`.

threshold_display.description: How the threshold is drawn: `text` colours the value, `background` colours the cell.

RumDashboardCreateRequest.description: Create request. The caller supplies the dashboard ID, so a retry with the same ID is rejected as a conflict instead of creating a duplicate.

dashboard_id.description: Dashboard ID to create, a canonical UUIDv7.

schema_version.description: Wire schema of the definition. Must be `dashboard.v1`.

RumDashboardCustomVariable.description: Variable whose options are a fixed list.

kind.description: Variable kind. Always `custom`.

name.description: Variable name, referenced as `${name}` in panel queries. 1–64 characters starting with a letter or underscore. `app` and names starting with `__` are reserved; names must be unique.

label.description: Label shown in the variable bar, 1-189 characters when set.

options.description: Fixed list of options, 1–1000 entries with unique `value`s.

RumDashboardDataLink.description: Link from a panel cell to another dashboard.

dashboard_id.description: Target dashboard ID, a canonical UUIDv7.

target_id.description: Target tab or panel ID inside the dashboard, a canonical UUIDv7 when set.

pass_time.description: Whether the current time range is forwarded.

variable_mappings.description: Target variable name to its mapping.

RumDashboardDatasourceRef.description: Datasource a panel or query variable reads. RUM dashboards only read the built-in RUM datasource, so the reference is always fixed.

kind.description: Reference kind. Always `fixed`.

datasource_id.description: Reserved, and always `0` for the built-in RUM datasource.

RumDashboardDefinition.description: The dashboard body: title, default time range, variables, and tabs. A dashboard is capped at 10 tabs, 100 panels and 300 queries. A tab holds at most 30 panels and 100 queries, top panels and sections together.

refresh_interval.description: Auto-refresh interval of the dashboard. One of `off`, `30s`, `1m`, `5m`.

variables.description: Variable bar entries, at most 20. The built-in `app` switch is not declared here.

RumDashboardDeleteResponse.description: Result of moving a dashboard to the trash.

revision.description: Revision created by the deletion. Pass it as `expected_revision` to restore the dashboard.

RumDashboardFieldSort.description: Sort order of a table column.

RumDashboardGridPosition.description: Panel position on the tab's 24-column grid. `x + w` must not exceed 24. Panels in the same `top_panels` list or the same section must not overlap.

x.description: Zero-based column of the left edge, 0–23.

y.description: Zero-based row of the top edge.

RumDashboardLinkMapping.description: How one variable of the target dashboard is filled when the link is followed.

source.description: Where the value comes from: `variable` (another variable), `row_column` (the clicked row's column), or for bar panels `category`, `series`, `value`.

column.description: Column of a `row_column` source. At most 1024 characters.

name.description: Variable name of a `variable` source. 1–64 characters starting with a letter or underscore.

RumDashboardListItem.description: One row of the dashboard list; the definition is not included.

updated_at.description: Last change time as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

RumDashboardListRequest.description: List request. `p` is 1-based and `limit` defaults to 20, newest first.

query.description: Search text, at most 128 characters. Split on spaces; each word must appear in the title or the description.

sort.description: Sort order, at most two unique fields; defaults to `updated_at` descending.

limit.description: Page size, 1–100. Defaults to 20.

items.description: Dashboards on this page.

total.description: Total number of dashboards matching the query.

RumDashboardListSort.description: Sort order of the dashboard list.

RumDashboardMutationRequest.description: Delete or restore request. `expected_revision` must match the current revision.

expected_revision.description: Revision the caller last read. Must be at least 1.

id.description: Panel ID, a canonical UUIDv7, unique in the dashboard.

datasource_ref.description: Required for every panel kind except `text`, which must omit it.

queries.description: Queries of the panel, each with a unique `ref_id`. `time_series` and `top_list` take 1-26 queries, `table`, `stat` and `bar` exactly 1, `text` none.

RumDashboardPanelQuery.description: One query inside a panel, identified by a single-letter reference.

ref_id.description: Query reference, a single uppercase letter `A`–`Z`, unique within the panel.

legend_alias.description: Legend label for the query's series. At most 1024 characters.

RumDashboardQuery.description: One analytics question of a panel: a DQL filter plus the analytics spec and the application it reads.

expr.description: DQL filter over the RUM events of the scope. At most 16 KiB. `${name}` must name a variable declared in the dashboard; formatters such as `${name:fmt}` and a bare `$name` are rejected.

min_step_seconds.description: Minimum step of the series in seconds; a duration, not a timestamp.

RumDashboardQueryArgs.description: The analytics spec of a query: which scope, aggregation, field and grouping it reads. Unknown keys are rejected.

scope.description: RUM explorer scope the query reads. One of `session`, `view`, `resource`, `action`, `error`, `long_task`, `vital`.

agg.description: Aggregation applied to the scope. One of `count`, `count_distinct`, `avg`, `sum`, `min`, `max`, `p50`, `p75`, `p90`, `p95`, `p99`.

field.description: Field key the aggregation reads. Required unless `agg` is `count`.

group_by.description: Field key to group by, 1-255 characters. Cannot be an event ID such as `session_id` or `view_id`. For a high-cardinality field, `agg` must be `count` or `sum`.

limit.description: Maximum number of series returned. One of `5`, `10`, `20`, `50`.

draw_style.description: How the series is drawn: `line` or `bar`.

application_id.description: Application the query reads: a concrete application ID, or `$app` to follow the application selected on the dashboard. Required, at most 64 characters. Saving fails if the application does not exist or you cannot read it.

RumDashboardQueryVariable.description: Variable whose options are the values of a RUM field.

kind.description: Variable kind. Always `query`.

name.description: Variable name, referenced as `${name}` in panel queries. 1–64 characters starting with a letter or underscore. `app` and names starting with `__` are reserved; names must be unique.

label.description: Label shown in the variable bar, 1-189 characters when set. When omitted, the console shows the field's display name.

refresh.description: When the candidates are re-read: `on_dashboard_load` or `on_time_range_change`.

RumDashboardRelativeTimeRange.description: Time range a dashboard opens with. `from` is a relative offset and `to` is fixed at `now`.

from.description: Relative start of the default time range. One of `now-15m`, `now-30m`, `now-1h`, `now-3h`, `now-6h`, `now-12h`, `now-24h`, `now-7d`.

RumDashboardResource.description: A dashboard as stored, including its current definition and revision.

schema_version.description: Wire schema of the definition. Always `dashboard.v1`.

revision.description: Revision number, starting at 1 and incremented on every change.

created_at.description: Creation time as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

updated_at.description: Last change time as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

RumDashboardRevisionGetRequest.description: Request for one revision of a dashboard.

revision.description: Revision number to read. Must be at least 1.

RumDashboardRevisionItem.description: One entry of the revision history; the definition is not included.

message.description: Change message supplied with the update, at most 1024 characters.

created_at.description: Creation time of this revision as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

RumDashboardRevisionListResponse.description: Revision history of a dashboard, newest first. Up to 20 revisions are kept.

items.description: Revisions of the dashboard.

RumDashboardRevisionResource.description: One revision with its full definition.

schema_version.description: Wire schema of the definition. Always `dashboard.v1`.

message.description: Change message supplied with the update, at most 1024 characters.

created_at.description: Creation time of this revision as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

id.description: Section ID, a canonical UUIDv7, unique in the dashboard.

kind.description: `values` selects the listed values; `all` selects everything and must carry no values.

values.description: Selected values. Required for kind `values`, forbidden for kind `all`. Must be non-empty and unique, and none may equal `$__all`. With selection `mode` `single`, exactly one value.

items.description: One allowed value.

RumDashboardSelectionConfig.description: How the variable bar lets the viewer pick values.

include_all.description: Whether an `All` entry is offered, which a selection of kind `all` requires.

kind.description: Panel kind. Always `stat`.

options.description: Free-form display options stored with the panel; not validated.

unit.description: Display unit of the panel value. One of `unitless`, `ratio`, `percent`, `milliseconds`, `seconds`, `bytes`, `bits`, `count_per_second`, `bytes_per_second`, `bits_per_second`.

decimals.description: Number of decimal places to show.

value_fields.description: Field keys whose values are reduced into the displayed number. Must be non-empty with unique names; `frame_index` and `field_index` are not allowed.

items.description: Field key.

reducer.description: How the series are reduced to one value. One of `last_non_null`, `min`, `max`, `mean`, `sum`.

RumDashboardTab.description: One tab of the dashboard. At most 30 panels and 100 queries, top panels and sections together.

id.description: Tab ID, a canonical UUIDv7, unique in the dashboard.

sections.description: Sections of the tab, at most 10.

kind.description: Panel kind. Always `table`.

options.description: Free-form display options stored with the panel; not validated.

column_options.description: Per-column presentation, keyed by column name. At most 100 columns.

sort.description: Initial sort order of the table.

link_columns.description: Data links rendered as extra columns. Together with the `data_link`s in `column_options`, at most 5 per table.

kind.description: Panel kind. Always `text`.

options.description: Free-form display options stored with the panel; not validated.

markdown.description: Markdown body, at most 64 KiB. Text panels take no datasource or query. Images, raw HTML and `${` templates are rejected; links must be HTTPS or start with `/`.

RumDashboardThreshold.description: Warning/critical thresholds drawn on a numeric panel. At least one of `warning` and `critical` is required.

warning.description: Warning threshold. Not above `critical` when `mode` is `higher_is_worse`, not below it otherwise.

RumDashboardTimeSeriesViz.description: Line or area chart over time.

kind.description: Panel kind. Always `time_series`.

options.description: Free-form display options stored with the panel; not validated.

unit.description: Display unit of the panel value. One of `unitless`, `ratio`, `percent`, `milliseconds`, `seconds`, `bytes`, `bits`, `count_per_second`, `bytes_per_second`, `bits_per_second`.

decimals.description: Number of decimal places to show.

RumDashboardTopListViz.description: Ranked bar list of reduced series.

kind.description: Panel kind. Always `top_list`.

options.description: Free-form display options stored with the panel; not validated.

unit.description: Display unit of the panel value. One of `unitless`, `ratio`, `percent`, `milliseconds`, `seconds`, `bytes`, `bits`, `count_per_second`, `bytes_per_second`, `bits_per_second`.

decimals.description: Number of decimal places to show.

reducer.description: How the series are reduced to one value. One of `last_non_null`, `min`, `max`, `mean`, `sum`.

limit.description: Number of entries shown, 1–100. Omit to show all.

RumDashboardTrashItem.description: One row of the trash list.

revision.description: Revision created by the deletion. Pass it as `expected_revision` to restore the dashboard.

deleted_at.description: Deletion time as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

RumDashboardTrashListRequest.description: Trash list request. `p` is 1-based and `limit` defaults to 20, newest deletion first.

sort.description: Sort order, at most two unique fields; defaults to `deleted_at` descending.

limit.description: Page size, 1–100. Defaults to 20.

items.description: Deleted dashboards on this page.

total.description: Total number of dashboards in the trash.

RumDashboardTrashListSort.description: Sort order of the trash list.

RumDashboardUnitFields.description: Numeric presentation shared by the value-bearing panel kinds.

unit.description: Display unit of the panel value. One of `unitless`, `ratio`, `percent`, `milliseconds`, `seconds`, `bytes`, `bits`, `count_per_second`, `bytes_per_second`, `bits_per_second`.

decimals.description: Number of decimal places to show.

RumDashboardUpdateRequest.description: Update request. `expected_revision` makes the write conditional: the update fails with `DashboardRevisionConflict` when the dashboard has moved on.

schema_version.description: Wire schema of the definition. Must be `dashboard.v1`.

expected_revision.description: Revision the caller last read. Must be at least 1.

message.description: Optional change message stored with the revision, at most 1024 characters.

RumDashboardUpdateResponse.description: Result of an update. `changed` is `false` when the submitted definition matched the stored one, in which case `resource` is still returned.

changed.description: Whether the stored definition actually changed.

RumDashboardVariable.description: One entry of the variable bar. The `kind` field selects the shape: `custom` carries a fixed option list, `query` reads the values of a RUM field.

RumDashboardVariableQuery.description: Where a query variable takes its candidates from. RUM lists the values of one RUM field.

kind.description: Query kind. Always `rum_field`.

field.description: RUM field key whose values become the candidates.

RumDashboardVizConfig.description: How a panel renders its queries. The `kind` field selects one of six shapes: `time_series`, `table`, `stat`, `bar`, `top_list`, `text`.

AlertEvent.description: One raw alert event, in the shape the ingestion pipeline receives and stores.

title.description: Event title. Required unless `title_rule` is set; the two are the source of the alert title.

title_rule.description: Title template such as `$service::$alertname`, built from `labels` when `title` is empty.

alert_key.description: Deduplication key that merges events into one alert. Empty is allowed: the preview mints a random key, so nothing is merged.

event_status.description: Event status. `Critical`, `Warning` and `Info` are firing events; `Ok` is a recovery.

event_severity.description: Severity carried by a firing event. The preview overwrites it with `event_status` for firing events.

event_time.description: Unix timestamp in seconds. The preview stamps the current time, so the value sent is ignored.

labels.description: Event labels. Up to 50 entries; keys are label names, values strings.

EnrichmentPreviewEvent.description: The event as the enrichment preview saw it.

title.description: Event title after the steps applied so far.

labels.description: Label set after the steps applied so far.

EnrichmentSample.description: One raw event an integration received, as it entered enrichment.

received_at.description: Unix timestamp in seconds of when the integration received the event.

event.description: The raw event, before any enrichment rule ran.

description_truncated.description: `true` when the stored description was cut to the sample size limit.

dropped.description: `true` when the integration discarded the event before it became an alert. Omitted when `false`.

EnrichStep.description: What one enrichment rule did to the event.

index.description: Zero-based position of the rule in `rules`.

kind.description:
Rule type that ran.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `extraction` | Extract a value from the alert's `title`, `description` or a `labels.*` key and write it to a label. |
| `composition` | Render a template against the event and write the result to a label. |
| `mapping` | Look up labels from a mapping schema or an external mapping API. |
| `drop` | Remove the listed labels from the alert. |

matched.description: Whether the rule's `if` conditions all matched. `false` means the rule changed nothing.

skipped_reason.description: Why the rule was skipped: `condition_not_met`, `regex_not_matched`, `source_label_missing`, `mapping_row_not_found`, `result_label_exists` or `error`. Empty when the rule ran.

detail.description: Rule-specific detail: the matched mapping row, the rendered value, or the error message when `skipped_reason` is `error`.

added.description: Labels the rule wrote that were not there before. `null` when it added none.

removed.description: Labels the rule deleted. `null` when it removed none.

changed.description: Labels the rule rewrote, each as a `[old_value, new_value]` pair. `null` when it rewrote none.

mapping_row.description: The mapping row the rule matched. `null` for a rule that is not a mapping rule or matched no row.

AlertPipelinePreviewEvent.description: The event as the pipeline preview saw it.

severity.description: Severity the event carried at this point.

labels.description: Label set.

PipelineStep.description: What one alert processing rule did to the event.

index.description: Zero-based position of the rule in `rules`.

kind.description:
Rule type that ran.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `title_reset` | Rewrote the title from the rule's template. |
| `description_reset` | Rewrote the description from the rule's template. |
| `severity_reset` | Reset the severity and status to the rule's `severity`. |
| `alert_drop` | Discarded the event; no alert is created. |
| `alert_inhibit` | Discarded the event while a matching source alert is active. |

result.description: Outcome of the rule: `applied` (it changed the event or stopped the pipeline), `not_matched` (its `if` conditions did not all match), or `not_executed` (an earlier rule stopped the pipeline, or the event is a recovery).

detail.description: `condition_not_met`, `no_active_source_alert`, `inhibit_not_evaluated` or `recovery_event` for those outcomes; otherwise the resulting value or the error message.

AlertEmailPreviewSettings.description: Email integration settings to preview, in the shape the save endpoint accepts.

mode.description:
How the integration decides what an email becomes. Omitted defaults to `alwaysTrigger`.
- `alwaysTrigger`: every email becomes its own alert, keyed randomly.
- `triggerByTitle`: every email becomes a firing event whose alert key is hashed from the subject.
- `triggerOrCloseByRule`: `rules` decide whether an email triggers, closes or is discarded, and `default` handles the rest.

rules.description: Rules tried in order when `mode` is `triggerOrCloseByRule`; each entry must be a non-empty object. At most 50.

default.description: What happens to an email that matches no rule when `mode` is `triggerOrCloseByRule`: `trigger` turns it into a firing event, `discard` drops it.

AlertEmailRule.description: One rule that matches an email and extracts the alert key from it.

type.description: `trigger` turns a matching email into a firing event, `close` into a recovery event.

extract_from.description: Which part of the email the alert key is extracted from: `title` or `description`. For `description` the body text is searched first, then the body text with tables, then the description.

extract_pattern.description: Regular expression the key is extracted with; the captured groups are joined by `,` to form the key source. A pattern that captures nothing falls back to the subject.

filters.description: AND conditions the email must match for the rule to apply. Send `[]` to match every email.

AlertEmailPreviewEmail.description: The email to run the preview over.

body.description: Email body: HTML when it starts with `<`, otherwise plain text.

eml.description: A whole email file (`.eml`) as base64. When set it stands in for `subject`, `body` and `from` and is parsed the way the SMTP server parses mail.

AlertEmailPreviewEvent.description: The alert event the email would have produced.

event_status.description: Status of the event this email produces.

event_severity.description: Severity of a firing event; empty for a recovery.

labels.description: Labels taken from the email: the body, sender, recipients and subject are exposed as labels.

AlertEmailPreviewParsed.description: The email as the conversion read it.

subject.description: Subject as the parser decoded it.

from.description: Sender address taken from the email.

body.description: Body the conversion used: the HTML part when there is one, otherwise the text part.

body_text.description: Body as plain text; a key extracted from the description is looked for here first.

integration_id.description: Integration whose context the preview runs in. The rules you send are not saved.

rules.description: Enrichment rules to try, in order. At most 50. The integration's stored rules are not used.

event.description: The event to run the rules over.

after.description: The event after the rules ran, with the `[TPL]` labels, title and description of a firing event rendered.

steps.description: One entry per rule, in the order they ran.

integration_id.description: Integration whose recent raw events to list.

EnrichmentSampleListResponse.description: Recent raw events of one integration.

items.description: Samples, newest first. Empty when no event has arrived yet.

integration_id.description: Integration whose saved enrichment runs first and whose pipeline context the preview uses.

rules.description: Alert processing rules to try, in order. At most 50. The integration's stored pipeline is not used.

event.description: The event to run the rules over.

is_recovery.description: `true` when the event is a recovery event: ingestion closes the alert without running the pipeline.

after.description: The event as notification templates would render it once the rules ran.

dropped.description: `true` when a rule dropped the event, so no alert would be created.

inhibited.description: `true` when a rule inhibited the event because a matching source alert is active.

steps.description: One entry per rule, in the order they ran.

integration_id.description: Email integration whose saved settings seed the preview. `0` or omitted is what the console sends on the create page, before the integration exists.

settings.description: Settings to preview. They are validated the way the save endpoint validates them.

AlertEmailPreviewResponse.description: How the settings treated the email, plus what the conversion read.

result.description: What the settings make of this email: `trigger` (a firing event), `close` (a recovery event) or `discard` (dropped).

matched_rule.description: Zero-based index of the rule that matched. `null` when no rule matched, and always `null` in `alwaysTrigger` and `triggerByTitle` modes.

key_source.description: What the alert key was hashed from. Empty when every email is its own alert (`alwaysTrigger`) or the email is discarded.

key_fallback.description: `true` when the rule's pattern captured nothing and the subject was used as the key source.

alert_key.description: Hash of `key_source`. Empty in `alwaysTrigger` mode, where each email gets a random key.

event.description: The event the email produces. `null` when the email is discarded.

email.description: What the conversion read from the email. `null` when the email could not be parsed.

AppKeyAuth.description: APP Key created in the Flashduty console under My → APP Key. Send it as the `app_key` query parameter or in the `Fd-App-Key` request header. Its effective access is the intersection of the key's permission scope and the creator's current role permissions. Keep it secret.

info.description: Public HTTP API for the Flashduty incident management platform — incidents, notification templates, channels, schedules, monitors, RUM, and platform administration. Every operation is authenticated with an `app_key` query parameter issued from the Flashduty console under Account → APP Keys. ## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **300 requests/minute**; **20 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | None — any valid `app_key` can call this operation |

## Usage

- Identify the member with one of `member_id`, `member_name`, `email`, `phone`, or `ref_id`. If multiple identifiers are present, the server checks them in that order.
- The caller must be the account owner, the member themself, or hold the Admin role; otherwise the call returns `403 AccessDenied`.
- Put the fields to write under `updates`: `member_name`, `password`, `phone`, `country_code`, `email`, `avatar`, `locale`, `time_zone`, or `ref_id`. Omitted or `null` fields keep their current value; `updates` must carry at least one field.
- A new `member_name`, `email`, or `phone` must not belong to another member of the account; a conflict returns `400`. A changed `email` or `phone` is marked unverified unless `from` is `api` and the account has member invitations disabled.
- `updates.time_zone` set to an empty string clears the member's own time zone, so the member follows the account's.
- `updates.country_code` is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code (e.g. "CN", "US"). It is an independently updatable field: `updates.phone` is not required, and the new region is stored even when the phone is unchanged. An explicit empty string is rejected with a 400.

## Usage

- `id` is required and the rule must already exist; otherwise the call returns `InvalidParameter`.

- `investigation_targets` is the exception: omit it to keep the current value, pass `[]` to clear, or pass a value to replace it entirely.
- `folder_id` cannot be changed through this operation; use `/monit/rule/move` to move the rule to another folder.
- The caller must be able to manage the rule's folder (account owner or admin, creator of the folder or one of its ancestors, or member of the team bound to the folder or an ancestor); otherwise the call returns `AccessDenied`.
- `name` must be unique within the rule's folder; a duplicate returns `InvalidParameter`.
- When `enabled` is `true`, `ds_type` must be a datasource type that supports alerting and every ID in `ds_ids` must be an enabled datasource with alerting turned on; otherwise the call returns `InvalidParameter`.
- Callers other than the account owner or admins need read-only access to every datasource listed in `ds_ids` or currently matched by `ds_list`; otherwise the call returns `AccessDenied` (`no permission to reference datasource "<name>"`).

- `account_id`, `creator_*`, `updater_*`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` are maintained by the server; client-supplied values are ignored.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **1,000 requests/minute**; **50 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | None — any valid `app_key` can call this operation |

## Usage

- Send 1 to 10 queries in one request; each query `id` becomes a key in the response object.
- `start_time` and `end_time` are Unix epoch milliseconds, at most 31 days apart. The server adds the time-range and account filters itself; you do not need them in `sql`.
- `FROM` names a RUM scope table: `sessions`, `views`, `actions`, `errors`, `resources`, `long_tasks`, `vitals`, `issues` or `sourcemaps` (the singular form is also accepted). Column names are the `field_key` values returned by `POST /rum/field/list`.
- A query whose top-level `AND` conditions pin `application_id` (`=` or `IN`) must name applications the caller can read: a private application the caller's team does not own fails the whole request with `AccessDenied`, an unknown one with `ResourceNotFound`, and one request may name at most 50 distinct applications. A query that names no application silently skips the private applications the caller cannot read.
- Malformed SQL, an invalid `time_zone` or an out-of-range time window fails the whole request with `InvalidParameter`. A query that fails later (unknown table or column, invalid `dql`, invalid `search_after_ctx`, database error) only sets `error` on its own entry, with code `InternalError`; the other queries still return `data`.
- `values` is column-major: `values[i]` holds every row's value of column `fields[i]`.
- `table` queries return at most 1,000 rows; a missing `LIMIT` or one above 1,000 is replaced with 1,000. A non-aggregate query with `ORDER BY` and no `OFFSET` returns `search_after_ctx` when the page is full — send it back with the same `sql` to get the next page.
- `time_series` queries get a `ts` column prepended (bucket start, Unix milliseconds), grouped and ordered by it. The bucket width, returned as `interval` in milliseconds, is the smallest step from a fixed ladder (1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500 ms; 1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 30 s; 1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 30 min; 1, 2, 3, 6, 12 h; 1, 2, 3, 7 d; 30, 60, 90, 180 d) that is at least both `interval` and the window length divided by `max_points`.
- On large time windows an aggregate query may run on sampled data; the response then carries `sampling`, and `COUNT`, `SUM` and `COUNT(DISTINCT)` columns are already multiplied by `scale_factor`. Set `disable_sampling: true` to always query the full data.

## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |

## Usage

- When `url_mode` is `false` (default), the response streams `application/x-ndjson` — one decompressed replay segment JSON object per line — and is **not** wrapped in the standard envelope. - If the session belongs to a private application the caller cannot access, the call returns `AccessDenied` ("You do not have permission to access this application").
- A page with no segments returns an empty result. Segments uploaded moments ago may not be indexed yet; the call then returns `ResourceNotFound` ("Replay segments are not available yet. Please retry shortly"), so retry after a short wait.

## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **16 requests/second** per account (no per-minute limit) |
| Permissions | **Datasources Read** (`monit`) |

## Usage

- Resolves the variables of the current revision of a stored dashboard. `variables` holds the caller's current selections; a variable without an entry falls back to its stored default (`default` for `custom` and `query` variables; for `datasource` variables the `default_datasource_id` if it is still a candidate, otherwise the first candidate ordered by name).

- An explicitly empty `values` selection means unresolved (`variable_invalid`); the resolver does not fall back to the stored default.
- Variables are resolved in dependency order, so a variable that depends on a failed variable also reports an error. A name in `variables` that the dashboard does not define fails the call with HTTP 400.
- Each variable returns at most 1000 candidates, and all candidates together must fit in 8 MiB, otherwise the call fails with `EntityTooLarge` (HTTP 413). `query` variables can only run against Prometheus, MySQL and Loki datasources.
- The caller must be able to see the dashboard's folder; otherwise the call returns `DashboardNotFound` (HTTP 404). The call has a 35-second overall deadline; exceeding it returns `RuntimeTimeout` (HTTP 504).

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |

## Usage

- Nothing is written: no integration, alert or event is created or changed.
- `integration_id` seeds the preview with the integration's stored address prefix; the address itself is never used, so the preview works on the create page too.
- `settings` passes the same validator the save endpoint runs, so an unsupported `mode`, rule `type`, `extract_from` or an invalid `extract_pattern` fails with `InvalidParameter` before the email is parsed.
- When `eml` is set the message is parsed as a mail file, within the SMTP message size limit, and `email` in the response shows what the parser read.
- `event` is `null` when the settings discard the email, and `email` is `null` when the message cannot be parsed.
- In `alwaysTrigger` mode every email becomes its own alert: `alert_key` and `key_source` come back empty.

| Aspect | Value |

## Usage

- Nothing is saved and no alert or event is created.
- The integration's saved enrichment rules run first, then your `rules` in order, against the enriched event.
- A recovery (`Ok`) event closes the alert without running the pipeline: `is_recovery` is `true` and every step comes back `not_executed` with detail `recovery_event`.
- `dropped` and `inhibited` report which rule stopped the event: `alert_drop` discards it, `alert_inhibit` discards it while a matching source alert is active. Rules after that one are `not_executed`.
- When no rule matches, `after` is the event as the notification templates render it, so the preview shows what the channel would deliver.

## Usage

- Nothing is saved and no alert or event is created.
